rag_documents.title: Challenging tax assessment in county where one has no mineral rights - Texas?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Challenging tax assessment in county where one has no mineral rights - Texas?

Author: min4me
Date: 2025-07-16T15:53:39Z
Content: In Texas, I own royalties on an abstract in Midland county. 7 wells pass thru this abstract and other abstracts ending in Martin county. My royalty revenue is based solely on my Midland county holdings, but I have been notified of an assessment for taxation in Martin county. Has anyone successfully challenged a similar situation? Can you cite an appropriate law or ruling that I might use in a challenge?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-16T17:11:34Z
Content: Review the two county tax notices and appraisal detail from the appraisal companies to make sure that the well value has been divided between the two counties based on the proportion of the wellbore or unit acreage in each county.  Such as, 40% in Martin County and 60% in Midland County.  This is a common practice, to divide the well between the two counties where the unit or horizontal wellbore is in both counties.  You just need to verify that each county is not taxing at 100% of the total well value, only the reduced portion.  Have seen this in multiple Texas counties.

Author: min4me
Date: 2025-07-17T21:25:38Z
Content: I realize this is a practice used on some wells. If the horizontal well goes through 5 tracts (abstracts) in the 2 counties and I owned mineral royalties in all 5 tracts, this is a non issue. The question pertains to when I own mineral royalties in only 1 tract in one county and the other county is assessing taxes.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-18T00:08:52Z
Content: No because there is zero economic harm to any party to have the taxes divided between the two counties.  Producing minerals are not tax exempt and so you will pay taxes regardless. You taxes are based on your well or unit DOI which is by definition producing.  No lawyer would consider spending his own money for a such losing class action because there will be no damages or fees to cover the costs. Nothing to stop you from filing,

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-22T22:13:59Z
Content: That has nothing whatsoever to do with your post about the taxable valuation being subdivided between 2 counties.  Clearly the total value of the minerals / well / unit exceeds the limit or you would not be complaining.  I addressed only the fact that the subdivision of value between counties is done all the time.  If the assessed value is $3,000 and it is divided in half between the counties to be $1,500 in each county, then you will still only be taxed on a total of $3,000.  Moreover, Sec 11.146 provides that the $500 exemption is based on the aggregated value of all mineral interests in the taxing unit (eg county) and not on an individual well basis.  Seven wells at $200 each is $1400 aggregated total.  So it may well be that a mineral owner is better off having the value subdivided if he does not own other producing minerals in the one or both counties and the total value is less than $1,000.

posts.author: min4me
posts.content: In Texas, I own royalties on an abstract in Midland county. 7 wells pass thru this abstract and other abstracts ending in Martin county. My royalty revenue is based solely on my Midland county holdings, but I have been notified of an assessment for taxation in Martin county. Has anyone successfully challenged a similar situation? Can you cite an appropriate law or ruling that I might use in a challenge?

posts.author: TennisDaze
posts.content: Review the two county tax notices and appraisal detail from the appraisal companies to make sure that the well value has been divided between the two counties based on the proportion of the wellbore or unit acreage in each county.  Such as, 40% in Martin County and 60% in Midland County.  This is a common practice, to divide the well between the two counties where the unit or horizontal wellbore is in both counties.  You just need to verify that each county is not taxing at 100% of the total well value, only the reduced portion.  Have seen this in multiple Texas counties.

posts.author: min4me
posts.content: I realize this is a practice used on some wells. If the horizontal well goes through 5 tracts (abstracts) in the 2 counties and I owned mineral royalties in all 5 tracts, this is a non issue. The question pertains to when I own mineral royalties in only 1 tract in one county and the other county is assessing taxes.

posts.author: TennisDaze
posts.content: No because there is zero economic harm to any party to have the taxes divided between the two counties.  Producing minerals are not tax exempt and so you will pay taxes regardless. You taxes are based on your well or unit DOI which is by definition producing.  No lawyer would consider spending his own money for a such losing class action because there will be no damages or fees to cover the costs. Nothing to stop you from filing,

posts.author: TennisDaze
posts.content: That has nothing whatsoever to do with your post about the taxable valuation being subdivided between 2 counties.  Clearly the total value of the minerals / well / unit exceeds the limit or you would not be complaining.  I addressed only the fact that the subdivision of value between counties is done all the time.  If the assessed value is $3,000 and it is divided in half between the counties to be $1,500 in each county, then you will still only be taxed on a total of $3,000.  Moreover, Sec 11.146 provides that the $500 exemption is based on the aggregated value of all mineral interests in the taxing unit (eg county) and not on an individual well basis.  Seven wells at $200 each is $1400 aggregated total.  So it may well be that a mineral owner is better off having the value subdivided if he does not own other producing minerals in the one or both counties and the total value is less than $1,000.

Author: 4theRightChild
Date: 2025-06-23T01:15:21Z
Content: I’ve recently signed a lease that has been decided as  paying me only 1/4 of what I’d thought I’d get. Here is the shortest way I can describe it… many years ago 160 acres was divided amongst 5 people. 1 of those 5 is my grandmother and she & my father have both passed. So myself and another are heirs to the 32 acres - giving us 16 each.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-23T02:46:10Z
Content: You are mixing gross acres and net acres.  The legal description is 160 acres.  When it was divided, each heir got 1/5 of the 160 acres.  So a lease would describe the 160 acre tract, and the owner would be paid on 1/5 of the 160 acres = 32 NMA (net mineral acres).  If your grandmother sold 1/10 of her interest, the buyer got 1/10 X 1/5 X 160 acres = 3.2 NMA.  That left your grandmother with 9/10 X 1/5 x 160 = 28.8 NMA.  Your father got the 28.8 NMA.  You get 1/2 X 9/10 X1/5 X 160 acres = 14.4 NMA out of the 160 acres.  Each of the other 4 original heirs each still would have 1/5 X 160 acres = 32 NMA.  Of course, each interest has likely been subdivided since then.

Author: 4theRightChild
Date: 2025-06-24T02:39:30Z
Content: I hear ya! Huge help, so thank you. Unfortunately, it’s a 1971 ‘Warranty Deed’ and according to their landman (and Oil Co. lawyer) the wording of this particular document isnt specific enough to side on the Net Mineral Acre (N.M.A.) side which would’ve been the 3.2 N.M.A.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-24T03:39:44Z
Content: Deeds need to be read in their entirety to determine the effect, not just an excerpt.  You should have your own lawyer review and give you his opinion.

Author: Norse
Date: 2025-06-24T18:00:07Z
Content: A basic flaw in the logic here is that, in fact, the grandmother sold 1/10 interest in the entire undivided 160 acres, NOT1/10 interest of her 1/5 share.  Another unspoken piece of the equation is how many other heirs to the grandmothers estate are out there, assuming it was divided equally (e.g. suppose the grandmother had 4 children, that would mean at least 4 potential heirs).

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-24T18:35:44Z
Content: There is no way to be certain about what was sold without reading the deed in its entirety.  Many deeds contain limiting language or reservations in subsequent paragraphs.  Or in some cases the deed may expand the assignment, such as by including ‘all other minerals in the county.’  Commentary is always limited to the facts circumstances as set forth by the poster, and not on speculation.  Certainly, the grandmother could have had more children and heirs. But she could also have assigned 90% of her interest to her son before executing the 1971 warranty deed.

Author: Norse
Date: 2025-06-24T18:50:49Z
Content: Since you posted the legal description in another post I was able, via 1docmarket, to look at the 1971 deed in its entirety. Seemed pretty unambiguous to me.

Author: Norse
Date: 2025-06-24T19:00:05Z
Content: It appears the original undivided 160 acres was inherited/owned by 5 people one of whom was your grandmother.  She subsequently sold 1/10 of the undivided 160 acres (i.e. 1/2 her total share) to a third party leaving her with a 1/10 interest in the undivided 160 acres (16 net acres). Since you share 16 NMA with another heir your share is 8 NMA.

Author: Larry_W_Love
Date: 2025-07-22T18:13:46Z
Content: When you say “divided” was this by individual deeds with legal descriptions or in some other manner? If it was, it is easy to determine what your grandmother later sold. However, say it was by inheritance - I give X to my five children. If this was the case, and the land was not divided and then transfer during probate, then you have a co-tenancy issue of some type.

Author: Danelle3327
Date: 2025-05-09T01:39:52Z
Content: Hi all,
I’m trying to help my family sort out a royalty issue and would appreciate advice. In 2012, my parents signed an oil & gas lease for97.12 acres in Labor 18, League 18, Wichita CSL, Hockley Co., TX. I have a fully executed lease and documents showing it waspooled by Occidental (OXY)in a 2013Form P-17withTract 100 (Labor 15, League 28, Hood CSL)— Lease No.03780, which has beencontinuously producingever since.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-05-09T02:54:13Z
Content: Was your grandmother ever in pay? Have you sent the recorded probate and/or deeds to Oxy proving that your parents now have title?  Oxy will not watch the deed records for changes.  You need to discuss with Oxy’s land department and division order department and find out what they need.  Best to send by certified mail.  RRC has zero to do with royalties so do not contact them.  An oil and gas attorney can also help you.

Author: Danelle3327
Date: 2025-05-10T21:52:47Z
Content: Yes, the affidavit of heirship was sent to OXY for the Labor 18, League 18 tract. My grandmother had dementia and passed without a will, so settling her estate across multiple counties in Texas and New Mexico has been an interesting process. That said—after doing a deep dive into her paperwork again—I think I’ve figured out what’s going on. The P-17 form that was included with the Labor 18, League 18 documentation actually belongs to the Tract 100, Labor 15, League 28 lease, which turns out to be a completely separate tract that my family didn’t know she owned mineral rights for—until last night. So the affidavit of heirship currently on file with OXY is for League 18, which never went into production. We’ll now need to have League 28 added to the affidavit in order to receive royalties.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-05-11T21:00:34Z
Content: Filing a new or amended AOH is a good practice. OXY still may require other curative filings prior to transfer of title.

Author: Evan_Thomas
Date: 2025-05-12T02:50:12Z
Content: Have you looked to see if any of your grandmother’s interests have been escheated to the state of her last known address? If TX, I’ve had some success getting fund out of them under similar circumstances. Good luck!

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-05-20T22:37:54Z
Content: It is a transfer to a State Unclaimed Property Division and not escheat, which is a common mistake. If you look up the definition of escheat, you will see the difference.

Author: Evan_Thomas
Date: 2025-05-22T18:46:15Z
Content: I didn’t come up with that word on my own, it’s the one my lawyers have used.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-05-22T20:34:41Z
Content: As I said, a common mistake. Ask your lawyer if he/she can explain the difference in the terms.

Author: sclausen
Date: 2025-05-26T19:38:05Z
Content: Because your first filing created a problem, you should have an attorney prepare a new affidavit of heirship.  Based on facts you are not an heir.  Your preparation of the affidavit of heirship for your parent who is the heir is engaging in the unauthorized practice of law.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-05-27T19:18:41Z
Content: What problem did the first filing create? You clearly did not graduate from law school, based on the rest of your post. Its hard to do given that Im 78, but the unauthorized practice of law at the end made me chuckle, thank you for the laugh today

Author: sclausen
Date: 2025-05-27T20:11:18Z
Content: The problem was that the affidavit was incomplete at best and without seeing it, there is no way to know whether it was prepared properly, which has made it necessary to prepare a second one. As I recall the facts, the geologist prepared the affidavit of heirship for a parent, and she is not an attorney.  The affidavit of heirship is a legal document.  Under the laws of most states, her action would constitute the unauthorized practice of law.  Or do you think she should start preparing estate planning documents too for her family?

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-05-28T10:21:15Z
Content: So, you clearly did not go to law school.  The affidavit was incomplete due to a missing legal desciprtion, has nothing to do with how it was prepared or an attorney being involced which is not required.  An affidavit of heirship requires a 3rd party, which the poster is, simply stating that they know and are familiar with the family history of the grandparents and that mom or dad was an heir to grandma. Youre acting as if the poster is commiting a crime or as you say, “unauthorized practice of law” by filing said affidavit which I have no idea where in the world you came up with that and it is quite simply, laughable.  No, I dont think the poster should go in to estate planning nor do I think you should be handing out this advice that others may read and run with.

Author: sclausen
Date: 2025-05-28T19:55:35Z
Content: You excel at making assumptions.  You have no knowledge whether the initial affidavit was correctly prepared or not.  Because there is a need to do another affidavit, the recommendation to have an attorney prepare it is sound advice. If the poster was an heir herself, she could prepare an affidavit of heirship in which was listed as an heir, but she is not an heir based on her facts so preparing a document that has legal consequences for someone else is the unauthorized practice of law.  Will anyone report her on these facts or would the bar in most states care-the answer is no.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-05-28T21:26:17Z
Content: Serious question, have you ever seen an affidavit of heirship? A college student could prepare one.  She already stated that she left off the legal needed in the AOH, I dont know why you continue to harp on the prepared doc, if she gave all the info she had and paid an attorney to do it, the same result would have happened.

Author: sclausen
Date: 2025-05-29T13:48:59Z
Content: Suggest you read Section 203.002 of Texas Estates Code regarding what should be included in a Texas affidavit of heirship.  You will see it requires one affiant.  In practice, third parties require two corroborating witnesses sign the affidavit.  The preparation of the base affidavit with the two corroborating affidavits to induce third parties to rely on it to pay royalties is the preparation of a legal document and is the unauthorized practice of law.  It is clear there is not a great deal we can agree on so this will be my last response on this issue.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-05-29T14:23:58Z
Content: @Bob77a question. If a person is provided and completes a form AOH by inserting information they believe to be correct and executes as the information being the same, then is this the unauthorized practice of law?

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-05-29T21:30:37Z
Content: a question. If a person is provided and completes a form AOH by inserting information they believe to be correct and executes as the information being the same, then is this the unauthorized practice of law?

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-05-30T01:46:13Z
Content: Thanks@Bob77for helping to define this issue. I hope this clarifies this issue for many on the forum. You covered some great points for people to consider that us title wonks take as second nature.

Author: Larry_W_Love
Date: 2025-07-22T16:54:18Z
Content: In Texas, an Affidavit of Heirship can be found in the code. ESTATES CODE. TITLE 2.  ESTATES OF DECEDENTS; DURABLE POWERS OF ATTORNEY
SUBTITLE E.  INTESTATE SUCCESSION
CHAPTER 203.  NONJUDICIAL EVIDENCE OF HEIRSHIP
See 203.002.

Date: 2025-06-13T23:04:29Z
Content: Revisiting this area from my previous post.
Signed a lease from April 2023 with Cowbell Creek Land Company representing Silver Creek Oil & Gas. Lease was never recorded with the OKC until two days ago 6/11/2025. Reached out a year+ back to the landman from Cowbell about my unrecorded lease and he said Silver Creek had shut their doors, which I took as “out of business.” I asked for the lease back and never heard from him. Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-07-16T13:22:36Z
Content: Are you in pay status already?  If you just inherited, then you need to contact the operator and get the royalties transferred to you first.  Section 15 has a horizontal well with quite a bit of life left in it.  and the potential for several more wells.  Section 10 does not have a current well, but is surrounded by sections with multiple horizontals, so potential for the future.  Buyers want any royalties pending at the state treasurer’s office or at the operator’s suspense files.  Make sure you get them before deciding what to do.

Content: And in general, have extra copies of the death certificate.  In Texas you can get from the funeral home for a fee at the time you are making arrangements.  If you have multiple interests, order multiples, it will make being the executor / or interest owner easier.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: Selling mineral rights questions

Author: noressacarson
Date: 2025-06-12T20:56:06Z
Content: Has anyone else had problems when selling your mineral rights with a company misrepresenting information and filing a contract you didn’t sign? A company contacted me to buy my rights. My dealings with them proved to be very problematic with serious red flags and questionable behaviors.

Author: Andrewl00
Date: 2025-06-12T21:33:55Z
Content: RUN, don’t walk to an attorney that can represent you in the state the minerals are located. This is fraud, I hope you saved a copy of the original contract with the appropriate amount you intended on selling.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-12T23:29:10Z
Content: Lesson here for others is that the first time you see a red flag or questionable behavior is the time to walk away from all interaction.  Do not think the other party did this by accident or will change his ways.  Do not respond to any further communications.  Assuming the facts as presented, the biggest danger is that the purchaser will immediately sell the minerals to someone else, greatly complicating the chances of recovery of the minerals.  Additional lesson is that it is the mineral owner’s responsibility to thoroughly research permits, drilling activity and wells and to determine whether there may be royalties in suspense or about to start.  Never just accept someone’s word that there is nothing going on and no real value, but he still wanting to buy the minerals.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-06-18T18:57:55Z
Content: You have no recource on a well being drilled at the time of the sale, thats on the mineral owner.

Author: Sean_Preston
Date: 2025-07-20T23:37:16Z
Content: This is highly unethical and fraudulent. It’s unethical to express a mineral interest is not producing, when it in fact is. It’s fraudulent to swop any deeds you didn’t sign or authorize. If I were you I’d hire an Oil and Gas Attorney. If this company really didn’t swop out deeds…I’d reclaim the minerals which were blatantly stolen from you.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: Review of Upland Operating leasing

Author: James_Flesher
Date: 2025-07-09T14:56:20Z
Content: I negotiated the identical leases for family members in 26-15N-25W and 28-14N-24W with Upland Exploration, which is very active in Roger Mills county now, for $1850 and 1/5th with a good Exhibit A.  Upland’s Exploration’s leasing agency was Jenkins Energy Partners.  You may access the leases by googling “Roger Mills County Clerk search” although viewing the leases 'themselves requires you to get a $10 account withokcountyrecords.org. Or you can visit the county courthouse for free and take photos. Overall, I was pleased with Upland/Jenkins although I initially was very displeased when they included a document outside of the lease which gave them the option of not executing the lease for 60 business days.  I got that paragraph struck but family members had to wait 45 business days (9 weeks) to receive their bonus checks.

Author: sparkle-motion
Date: 2025-07-10T15:07:56Z
Content: I was contacted by Jenkins representing Upland regarding my property in Roger Mills 33-13N-24W. Current offers are:
$1,000.00 per net mineral acre bonus consideration, for a three (3) year term oil and gas lease providing for a 3/16th royalty

Author: Don_Ayres
Date: 2025-07-10T17:05:53Z
Content: I usually take the highest royalty and not worry about the bonus money.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-07-10T23:22:39Z
Content: You signed something before you leased that dealt with the closing date.  Not to be rude, but if youre now upset with the timing upon being paid, you should have negotiated that beofre you signed

Author: James_Flesher
Date: 2025-07-16T20:55:29Z
Content: Right.  Sometimes I don’t get everything I want.  Initially the cash bonus was to be paid 60 business days after the lease’s start date.  I got that reduced to 45 business days.  Jenkins Energy’s reasoning to me was that unlike in the good old days when owners could receive their bonus check the day they delivered their signed lease to the lessee, Jenkins  doesn’t start their research to lock in title verification until after they have received a signed copy of the lease. Our lease doesn’t warrant the title. Surely 45 or 60 extra days for the lessee to hold on to the cash bonus is a nice incentive for the lessee to do as they did here.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-07-20T23:36:33Z
Content: Its hard to follow what your complaint is? You say, “I got that paragraph struck but family members had to wait 45 business days (9 weeks) to receive their bonus checks. Surely 45 or 60 extra days for the lessee to hold on to the cash bonus is a nice incentive for the lessee to do as they did here” The Lessee didnt hold on to the cash, they simply ran due dilligence on your mineral interests which they then paid you upon the agreed closing date.  If your gripe is the effective date, thats on the mineral owner and should have made the OGL effective date the same time as the closing date, but in the big picture, youre hoping that they drill a well on your property so that shouldnt matter, if they dont drill your minerals, you will be open to lease again a month sooner so a win win for you

Date: 2025-07-14T11:36:49Z
Content: My sister died without leaving information about whether she sold her inherited Mineral Rights to a third party.  We do not know if she did or not.  If an heir of a mineral rights holder sells his/her interest to a third party, is that transfer recorded and filed with the County?  How does a landman figure out who to contact for a splintered rights situation.  Do they only rely on an Affidavit of Heirship

Author: Larry_W_Love
Date: 2025-07-15T13:34:13Z
Content: The transfer of a mineral ownership, like a transfer of a real estate ownership, requires a deed. To effect the transfer, the mineral deed needs to be filed in the county records. This filing puts the world on notice of who owns the minerals. It is the buyer’s responsibility to ensure the deed is filed in order to protect his interest.

Author: user68
Date: 2025-06-15T10:27:54Z
Content: guess she inherited from my dad who passed 7 yrs ago.  They first offered 1500 then sent a letter offering 1100.  she just told me they gave her until Tuesday to respond.  I have no idea what to do.  It’s a little over an acre flat run 12-18-14.  is this a good offer?  thanks

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-06-15T15:48:43Z
Content: You also should google “Mineral Buyers in West Virginia” and you will better know if that is a good offer if you get another potential buyer in the mix

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-06-15T15:50:58Z
Content: And yes there is NO RUSH at making a decision like this.  There isnt a lot of development yet in that area of Marion, so I GUARANTEE you they will make an offer if you tell them you need more time to decide

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-06-16T10:45:26Z
Content: @user68The best way to find out if its a good offer is to find another potential buyer.  Your area is a ways away from development, so trying to rush you into a deal is really just a sales tactic so you dont think about the offer - you’ll find tons of companies willing to pay that price in Manington

Author: user68
Date: 2025-06-16T10:47:28Z
Content: Thanks for quick response - - I have so many questions.  she said the rights were ‘non-leaseable’ … what does that mean?  Also they sent a general warranty deed for my mother to sign (that I was just informed of a minute ago).  That should help me with the heir designation, shouldn’t it?  It looks like the mineral company wants the rights 50% along with an agriculture company 50%.  Does that mean they want the water rights? I see also where they say 0 net oil/gas acres and 1.12 net oil / gas royalty acres.  does that mean there are wells on the land?

Author: E_W_WILLIS
Date: 2025-06-16T16:26:13Z
Content: RUN from this offer.  It sounds bad on its face, but regardless of the price do not sign a general warranty deed. With a general warranty deed the Grantor (your mother) is guaranteeing forever that she has legal title to the property conveyed. I never sell mineral rights, but if I did it would be via a Quit Claim deed.

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-06-16T19:00:47Z
Content: You probably have just the royalty rights (called an “NPRI interest”) and you can probably google it to get all the information on what that means.

Author: user68
Date: 2025-06-17T14:50:16Z
Content: this has now become so interesting that she doesn’t want to sell because here is an actual part of not only family history but American history as well.  Thanks for your help!

Author: user68
Date: 2025-06-18T12:52:38Z
Content: Thanks for the info … it’s just so strange that this happens after my dad passed.  He was an engineer for one of the big oil/gas companies his whole life, retired from there.  That’s why we were so caught off-guard when this person called with an offer for her ‘mineral rights’.  My dad would have known exactly how to get the info needed, it’s weird but he obviously wasn’t aware of this because he would have done whatever was necessary to make life easier for my mom but thanks to you guys, we’re okay.  Now we just have to figure out how to go about putting in this in her name so the inheritance can continue through the family like it is now.  any suggestions?  I suppose we start with the county clerk?  so I guess this originated with my great great (great?) grandfather and has been passed along since 1903 or thereabouts.  Now that we’re not on a deadline I’m a bit chatty … !  I sincerely appreciate your help (standing in my dad’s shoes so-to-speak).  Obviously, I miss him but glad to know there are other good people in this world.

Content: I don’t know how to message you directly on this site.  Is there another way to contact you that is allowed here?  I’m new at all this.

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-07-18T11:09:01Z
Content: @user68I know Nick from MountainView Minerals has helped owners understand some of these topics with a free call.  So I would try that too if you still have questions

Author: Petroleum9202
Date: 2025-07-18T13:06:38Z
Content: @user68- When your mother mentions“non-leasable,”there could be ​a​ couple ​of different scenarios. One is that an older shallow well was holding the tract, meaning it was drilled a long time ago (vertical) and is considered Held by Production (HBP). This means ​that if a deep well operator, such as EQT, wants to come in and drill Marcellus Shale wells (deeper) horizontally, they need to sign an amendment and ratification to the existing lease (modifying), or it is considered NPRI, as mentioned by WVOGM in the comments. After looking at this tract on the oil and gas DEP drilling map, that old shallow well was plugged, which ​r​eleased the older lease taken back in the day. There might also be another situation where a shallow well drilled on an adjacent tract could be tying up the tract your grandmother has mineral interest in. A full title search will need to be conducted, and CR doesn’t always do that until you sign the PSA (Agreement) with them. Please contact an oil and gas professional or attorney.

Author: Elizabeth_McBride
Date: 2025-07-15T18:56:56Z
Content: Question about leases in WV.  If there is production on a part of the leased land, does the entire parcel described in the lease become part of the DO calculation?  I am trying to figure out how percentages are arrived at.

Author: Petroleum9202
Date: 2025-07-15T21:32:50Z
Content: @Elizabeth_McBride-Hi Elizabeth, that’s a difficult question to answer since many different scenarios are involved. I recommend reaching out to an Oil and Gas professional or advisor to explore details about the drilling unit, lease, etc.

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-07-16T00:05:09Z
Content: While it may be lease specific, generally ONLY the portion of your parcel included in the Unitization is going to be used in your Division Order calculation.  So if you own a 1/10th interest in a 15 acre parcel but they are only using 50% of the parcel, your NMA for the land included in the calculation is going to be 15 acres / 10 * 50% = 0.75 acres included

Author: Elizabeth_McBride
Date: 2025-07-16T21:39:03Z
Content: That explanation is really helpful..  On one DO, the calculation started with the lease acreage and then had decimal multipliers.  But there is another long number in the middle that signifies something but doesn’t affect the end number.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: How many horizontal wells have been drilled after your 1st well?

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-07-11T18:02:52Z
Content: Just out of curiousity and think it would be a good discussion point for the board. For those that have multi unit/wells filed, how many wells have they drilled after the 1st one and were the results similar for wells 2, 3, 4 etc?

Author: Lee_Clark_Archer
Date: 2025-07-13T03:05:47Z
Content: I have a lease where they drilled 3 more wells. Two came in much better one was about the same. If I remember right my acreage was at the end of the 3rd section. I think the rules changed and they were able produce closer to the property line.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-07-16T13:16:02Z
Content: The question needs to be narrowed down to state and county and reservoir.  The answer depends upon the technology available at the time, the proppant and fluids used, the ability of the reservoir to deliver, pressure profile, spacing, etc.  Some companies drill up their leased inventory and put one well per spacing to hold it and then come back and drill infills.  Other companies drill their infills immediately.  The parent well will tap into virgin pressure.  Child wells may perform better if the technology is better, or they may be slightly to terribly worse depending upon how much pressure the parent well bled off.  Also, the commissions may limit production to protect the reservoirs.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-07-16T20:10:38Z
Content: It was a general question for owners across all states and reservoirs.  They can state their state and county if theyd like, just thought it would be helpful for everyone that has new horizontal drilling with the promise of multiple other wells to be drilled to get a look at whats going on with other owners.  Of course it differs greatly by location, just thought it would be an interesting topic but guess I was wrong.

Date: 2025-05-12T14:08:04Z
Content: Welcome to the forum.  This is a developing play. You can do some hunting onwww.Texasfile.comand see who is leasing in the area. Author: user78
Date: 2025-07-15T21:32:16Z
Content: We have a unique situation. We live about 2 miles from Harrison county. We actually live in Lewis county. We pay all our taxes in Lewis county, except for a tax we have to pay for oil and gas that we can’t find any info about. We tried to figure it out years ago, but just got the run around.

Author: Nancy_Mosley
Date: 2025-07-15T21:57:36Z
Content: Is your oil and gas in a horizontal well? If so, it probably has at least some of it in Harrison County and the rest in Lewis County. I have seen this situation a few times in other counties. If it is this situation, Harrison County does not contain your tract within its boundaries so you pay that part of taxes to Lewis but since you get income from the part of the well that lies in Harrison, and maybe the wellhead is there, they have you pay tax for that portion of your income. You could call the Assessor’s office at each county and ask, but my guess is this is your situation.

Author: Lost_Aggie
Date: 2025-07-14T16:16:18Z
Content: Chevron operates the Texas 10 13/16 lease that covers all of Section 13 and the north half of 16 in Blk 40 T3S. They’ve recently pulled 6 new permits on the lease which is what drew my attention to it. There has been some activity on the lease dating back to 2017 but it is not as active as adjacent sections.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-14T18:52:08Z
Content: When you post about wells, include the full name (no abbreviation) and preferably an API number.  In this case, the Texas Ten wells are drilled from Section 42, Block 40, T-2-S (not T-3-S), but the producing well bores are in Section 13 and Section 16, TB Brashears Survey, Block 40 (located to the south and has no Township designation).  According to RRC, the most recent Texas Ten permits were issued in 2019.  Sections 13 and 16 are not adjacent in Block 40, T3S or T2S.  COG operates wells in Section 13, Block 40, T3S, under Braun and Parks Field.  Are you in pay on these?

Author: Lost_Aggie
Date: 2025-07-15T01:24:34Z
Content: Apologies. I was focused on the land, not the wells. The new permits are for the GBG Hercules 37-16 (A-F) wells, API 329478(60-65). They are indeed drilled from Section 42 T2S but the permit shows them transiting to Section 13 T3S. I know I am missing something basic here because yes, COG does operate in Section 13 Blk 40 T3S, A-279 and I am in pay on those. I am confused as to why there appears to be another Section 13 Blk 40 T3S, A-861.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-15T02:54:06Z
Content: This is a section idenfication mistake by the surveyor on the plat.  Abstract 861 in Midland County is Section 13, Block 40, TB Brashears Survey on the GLO viewer and Section 13, NO BLOCK #, TB Brashears Survey, on the RRC Gis Viewer.  It is not T-3-S and not part of the  T&P RR Co Survey.  And it is not close to Sec 13, Blk 40, T3S.  Section 16, A-860, is properly identified on the plat.  How interesting and unusual that the error was not caught by RRC in review before approval.

Author: Lost_Aggie
Date: 2025-07-15T03:09:34Z
Content: Thank you. This has vexed me for 7 years. I have asked many this question but you’re the first to say it was an error in the survey. The original land was purchased in 1909 and there is a reasonable legal description for it in the deed (not metes and bounds) but this “duplicate” in the survey has always bothered me.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-15T03:27:43Z
Content: The error is not in the GLO or RRC records for these sections (sometimes called surveys).  You can always double check by the Abstract number which is unique and never repeated within any one Texas county.  The problem is that the original surveyor hired by the oil company to draw a well plat made a mistake on the plat and then it has been perpetuated by successive surveyors.  Your Section 13, Blk 40, T-3-S is Abstract 279.

rag_documents.title: Inherited Mineral Rights
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Inherited Mineral Rights

Author: MT1985
Date: 2025-06-03T20:28:21Z
Content: My mother received a call from an Antero Landman some weeks back who said that Antero had been trying to locate mineral rights heirs for 3 pieces of property in Wetzel County since 2018. He had tracked my mother down because she had been married to my father, though they divorced 20 years ago and he passed away in 2022. She let the landman know that they were not married at the time of his death and that his only heir would be me, as I am his only child. She sent in the divorce paperwork and went ahead and sent my birth certificate as well to remove herself from the process.
Apparently the mineral rights were owned by his father or grandfather, and has apparently been split among a few people, and were leased to Antero in 2019 by a few of the heirs that could be located.
I’m new to this side of things, and I have a few questions. I contacted the landman, but he has yet to contact me back. He told my mother that Antero had been looking for the rest of the heirs for years, and had eventually turned it over to him because he specializes in harder cases.
With the lease being signed before anyone located me or even my father, how do the royalties typically work? Were all payments due split among the heirs that had been found, or would Antero had kept other royalty payments while they worked on finding the heirs they had trouble locating?
I’m sure this seems like a stupid question, but while I’m familiar with the industry, I’ve never dealt with this side of it. I know which pieces of property it was, I know which wells they were, I know the total production to date, I’ve even found the lease that was signed by one party for 15%. But I’m completely lost about the rest of this. Any help would be appreciated.

Author: Nancy_Mosley
Date: 2025-06-03T21:34:00Z
Content: They should be holding in suspension account any royalty money due to the Not Yet Located heirs. I have had that happen for my mother several years ago so I know. Ask them about that.

Author: MT1985
Date: 2025-06-04T01:45:38Z
Content: Thank you so much. I’m still waiting to hear from them, but I’ll make sure to ask them about it when they contact me. I genuinely appreciate the help.

Author: MT1985
Date: 2025-06-29T11:15:57Z
Content: Landman just got in touch with me on Friday. Apparently no one has been paid yet because they’ve been trying to figure out the heirs since before the lease was signed in 2019. And that does explain why one person already sold their rights.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-07-09T19:51:24Z
Content: This will most likely take quite a bit of time. I have worked on several similar projects of this nature. Antero will complete the title research and then  proceed to a Quiet Title Action or a Determination of Death and Heirship (Probate) proceeding. Their title to the OGL is encumbered, similar to your interest, so they have a vested interest to complete the work.

Author: MT1985
Date: 2025-07-14T18:36:34Z
Content: Yeah, the landman mentioned that it was nearly done, and then he got told to stop and they dumped 10 more on him to sort out that took priority over ours. He said he should be able to get it submitted within a couple of weeks.

Author: galetime
Date: 2025-07-12T21:39:04Z
Content: That ties up your land for 15 years without drilling.  Thats a long time and who knows what will happen?  If they do drill and hit, then the option goes away, but, of course, you are paid per your interest in the well.  Depending on spacing regulations for the well / pool, your land might not be drilled on, but your interest might be included in another well.  Neither one of the options you listed is a bonus.  A ‘bonus’ is a one time cash payment  for signing a lease.  Have you figured the monetary outcome for the scenarios?

rag_documents.title: How to get a royalty audit in Texas?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: How to get a royalty audit in Texas?

Author: Pelischek
Date: 2025-06-24T14:04:52Z
Content: I have royalty interests and override interests in La Salle county, Texas with Verdun Oil Co (EP Energy), Ridgemar (now Crescent) and Texas American Resources.  I am highly skeptical that I’m being paid and taxed for the correct decimal and for all the wells to which I’m entitled. What can I do to find out if I’m paid and taxed correctly?

Author: KyndallLeone
Date: 2025-06-26T17:05:34Z
Content: There are a few issues with different solutions here. A good way to see if you are being paid on all wells you own in is to go tohttps://gis.rrc.texas.gov/gisviewer/, look for your lands, and look for all producing wells within your interests.  How to know if you are being paid at the correct NRI is to know what your % interest is in the tract, how many acres in the unit/well, your royalty rate (less possible burdens), and calculate it from there.  To know if you are being taxed on the right NRI, just to compare royalty statements to the tax roll.  If you are asking about ad valorem value, then you can roughly compare annual revenue and expect that the ad valorem value will be ROUGHLY 3-5x that.  You can also compare old division orders or possibly Stipulations of Interest to you current royalty statements for more data points.  For a one-stop solution, hire a landman and let them do it for you.Happy hunting!

Author: Pelischek
Date: 2025-06-26T20:27:46Z
Content: Thanks so much for your answer! One of the problems is that I don’t own any of the surface. I bought producing interests and I have reason to believe I’m not paid properly.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-28T20:55:04Z
Content: For a proper audit to proceed, you must start at your base title. From that point you include any OGL obligations. You will have to pull permits and unit agreements before you start to advance to Division Orders. Ad valorem taxes are based on Division Orders. A landman can perform any part of this work that you do not feel comfortable completing.

Author: KyndallLeone
Date: 2025-07-01T15:55:34Z
Content: I wouldn’t give any different advice knowing that you don’t own surface, if that helps.  Do you mean that you own mineral interests that are producing, or do you own and override or NPRI?  I might be able to give better guidance depending on the type of asset.

Author: Pelischek
Date: 2025-07-12T15:27:52Z
Content: Thanks! How do I find a good landman that can do that? Can you recommend some?

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-07-13T01:04:20Z
Content: I have used Kelly Morton for some work in Burleson. She did a great job on that project.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-13T14:47:25Z
Content: First step is careful review of the documentation from the seller, including copies of his royalty checks and his DOI, division orders, deeds, etc.  Second is the assignment language, such as limitations to wellbore only or depths, and whether he assigned 100% or a fraction of his interest.  If the seller assigned his interests in specific leases, then the landman can help you trace the status of those leases (such as expired or released depths) and which wells were drilled under those leases.  Hopefully you have or can obtain copies of the original leases.  Whether or not the seller was the original lessor, the landman will need to track the assignments into the seller (and out of the seller) to determine what he owned at the time of your purchase.  For example, was an assignment of an override into the seller limited to specific depths or formations.  You may also be able to pull the seller’s tax listings from the county CAD to see what wells and DOI he was paying taxes on.

Date: 2025-07-13T00:40:53Z
Content: Sid,
Matador is a $6.5 billion company.  They have a large legal team inside and outside the corporation.  All of those lawyers do their best to advance Matador’s business interests.  That’s why it is worth your money to have an attorney looking out for your interest.
That said, sometimes it is hard to find a good oil and gas attorney, because you are a one time customer and the oil companies are repeat customers.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: De-Mystifying mineral offers in Western Haynesville

Author: Sotexnrg
Date: 2025-05-29T14:31:11Z
Content: I see a lot of posts on this so thought it might be helpful to give a general guideline of how mineral buyers evaluate a play like this.
The Leon/Robertson core has enough production history now to generate a satisfactory type curve (disclaimer: I am not a PE.) Using a composite curve of Aethon & Comstock’s wells under following parameters:
Well set: 21 wells, 8800’ perforated lateral being average of well set
DCA model: Modified Arps with exponential terminal decline at month 40 (B factor of .96 before terminal rate)
450 months, P10 EUR: 44 BCF P50 EUR: 38 BCF P90 EUR: 36.4 BCF.
Pretty tight range ran on 500 bayesian trials. To get a engineers stamp on that it would have to be the P90 case but buyers can rarely transact that way so we are rolling with the P50 EUR.
As for the DCF model, have to make some wide assumptions here. I am basing this on:

rag_documents.title: Suspensed funds from XTO oil
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Suspensed funds from XTO oil

Author: Caseysnow
Date: 2025-06-03T09:56:00Z
Content: My father inherited mineral rights in Reagan County.  After a years worth of work, We were able to get a payment from XTO Energy for $10,300 for suspended funds from 2019-current.

Author: brokendash
Date: 2025-06-03T11:48:44Z
Content: Forgive me but you might have already done this… have you looked up the wells with on the Reagan County aprasial dist website? Thats one way to refference them, and you can do some searching on the county clerks website for the lease names, gransfathers name, etc..to run them down. Usuaslly these are conveyed via probate but that doesnt always have occur. Im not an expert and only know some things mostly from needing to track down stuff my folks have inheriented. If you like you can send me a message with some well info and some lease names, I think there is a way to send it directly so it isnt seen by everyone an their dogs brother.If they are tied to a person then usually the county is wanting some tax money for it over the years so thats where I would start but you might have already done so.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-03T19:01:37Z
Content: There could be many complexities with this issue. First, try to establish a purchaser/operator history for the subject wells using the TX RRC. Second, use theReagan CADto perform searches on the properties under your great grandfather’s name looking at years prior to 2019. This will provide you with some more information.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-06-03T19:19:59Z
Content: I would first start with finding the deed or deeds that your Grandfather acquired and read the deed to see if there were any minerals reserved by the previous owners.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-03T19:56:51Z
Content: The first question is the date of first production from the identified wells.  If no lease was signed, then your grandparent was an unleased mineral owner and would not have received any revenues until the wells paid-out (recovered all costs).  Is your father receiving revenues and paying a JIB or has he now signed a lease?

Author: Caseysnow
Date: 2025-06-04T14:17:11Z
Content: I’ve found the original deed from 1916. It’s under two different names that are not my great grandfather, but it is the deed XTO Energy had us use for the change of ownership. It doesn’t mention any reserved mineral rights, it’s just selling the 100 acres out right.

Author: Caseysnow
Date: 2025-06-04T14:17:17Z
Content: When I researched the wells individually (there are 9), it looks as though they were all put into production in 2018. I wasn’t able to find any records prior to that.

Author: Caseysnow
Date: 2025-06-04T14:17:22Z
Content: I can’t seem to find a way to direct message you, but the lease names are under Frank Powell, lease numbers 20101, operator is XTO Energy. There are 9 wells. From what I’ve found, they just started producing in 2018. I cannot find anything prior to that

Author: Caseysnow
Date: 2025-06-04T14:17:26Z
Content: I was able to look further into the production of the wells, but it appears there’s nothing prior to 2018. I’m assuming there are no additional funds since they paid out 2018-current in the check they sent two days ago.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-04T18:02:32Z
Content: You have been a busy person with your research. If the wells started producing in 2018 and there were no previous wells on the property, then you have most likely located all suspended and UCP funds.

Author: CameronBussell
Date: 2025-06-04T21:49:03Z
Content: I had a very similar problem and discovered that any unclaimed funds from XTO Energy (a subsidiary of Exxon) will not show up on any unclaimed site other than this one:https://unclaimedproperty.delaware.gov/app/claim-searchtype your family member’s name in and if there was anything that they have reported that your family member is owed it will pop up there.

If you like you can send me a message with some well info and some lease names, I think there is a way to send it directly so it isnt seen by everyone an their dogs brother.If they are tied to a person then usually the county is wanting some tax money for it over the years so thats where I would start but you might have already done so.

posts.author: James_Garner1
posts.content: There could be many complexities with this issue. First, try to establish a purchaser/operator history for the subject wells using the TX RRC. Second, use theReagan CADto perform searches on the properties under your great grandfather’s name looking at years prior to 2019. This will provide you with some more information.

posts.author: Mineral_Owner5
posts.content: I would first start with finding the deed or deeds that your Grandfather acquired and read the deed to see if there were any minerals reserved by the previous owners.

posts.author: TennisDaze
posts.content: The first question is the date of first production from the identified wells.  If no lease was signed, then your grandparent was an unleased mineral owner and would not have received any revenues until the wells paid-out (recovered all costs).  Is your father receiving revenues and paying a JIB or has he now signed a lease?

posts.author: Caseysnow
posts.content: I’ve found the original deed from 1916. It’s under two different names that are not my great grandfather, but it is the deed XTO Energy had us use for the change of ownership. It doesn’t mention any reserved mineral rights, it’s just selling the 100 acres out right.

posts.author: Caseysnow
posts.content: When I researched the wells individually (there are 9), it looks as though they were all put into production in 2018. I wasn’t able to find any records prior to that.

posts.author: Caseysnow
posts.content: I can’t seem to find a way to direct message you, but the lease names are under Frank Powell, lease numbers 20101, operator is XTO Energy. There are 9 wells. From what I’ve found, they just started producing in 2018. I cannot find anything prior to that

posts.author: Caseysnow
posts.content: I was able to look further into the production of the wells, but it appears there’s nothing prior to 2018. I’m assuming there are no additional funds since they paid out 2018-current in the check they sent two days ago.

posts.author: James_Garner1
posts.content: You have been a busy person with your research. If the wells started producing in 2018 and there were no previous wells on the property, then you have most likely located all suspended and UCP funds.

posts.author: CameronBussell
posts.content: I had a very similar problem and discovered that any unclaimed funds from XTO Energy (a subsidiary of Exxon) will not show up on any unclaimed site other than this one:https://unclaimedproperty.delaware.gov/app/claim-searchtype your family member’s name in and if there was anything that they have reported that your family member is owed it will pop up there.

Author: AJ11
Date: 2025-04-15T18:23:26Z
Content: If you agree to a full warranty instead of a special/limited warranty, will you be responsible for defending the entire chain of title (in court) against all comers at any time in the future? I am not an attorney and would not sign a oil lease without having an attorney review the document. The following language is for informational purposes only and is not–nor should it be construed as being–legal advice:
“Lessor warrants title only as held by itself at the time of executing this lease and disclaims any further warranty as to title not actually in its possession at that time.”

Author: Bully5
Date: 2025-04-19T12:49:25Z
Content: I agree with AJ11on this one. Special Warranty if any warranty at all. They will uncover any defects during their due diligence search. Also don’t give them a signed lease in the promise of a payment later. Lease and money change hands at the table. Immediately available funds ( wire, cash or Cashiers Check.) I am not a lawyer but I have common sense.

Author: Sid_Stuart
Date: 2025-07-12T11:03:21Z
Content: You can usehttps://countyrecords.com/to search for records around your property. You can specify the range, township and section to limit the records. You can also search on names. It costs around $5 to get a copy of the record. I tracked down my familiy’s holdings with it.
We used Elliot & Waldron to confirm the title on one of our holdings. It was not cheap though, if I remember correctly around $3,000.

Author: jvt
Date: 2025-07-11T00:41:29Z
Content: There is no activity currently in your township.  The nearest drilling is in sec 6 T7N R60W, three miles to the north of your minerals.
The slow permitting process by the state of Colorado coupled with lousy oil prices has killed leasing in this area.  No one is leasing until they are ready to begin permitting a well.That being said, I think your minerals will eventually be leased and drilled but you will have to be patient.  It may be ten years before anything happens.  There may be a silver lining in the long wait.  The wells currently being completed in the Niobrara are much better than the wells drilled ten years ago. Technology advances and wells drilled ten years from now will probably be better than today. As long as there is money to be made, someone will figure out how to do it better.

Topic: Someone with same last name claiming royalties?

Author: bredia
Date: 2025-07-10T01:55:38Z
Content: So what can I do if someone with my Grandfathers last name if claiming our Royalies, also the  SURVEYOR has the same last name as well?   Now is trying to get a plat?  What does this mean?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-07-10T12:49:28Z
Content: Contact the operator’s Division Order department and put in your own claim and ask for a copy of the paragraphs from the division order title opinion that pertain to your family.  Ask them what they need to put you into pay status.  It is usually along the lines of probate documents, death certificates, affidavit of heirships, driver’s license, etc.  Families are complicated and some last names can be common.  There may be heirs that you do not know about or it might be fraud.  True legal documents are the best tool. Some families have good clean documents and others do not.  Work with the Division Order Analyst to get it cleaned up.  Send documents by certified mail return receipt.  Keep copies of everything that you send.

Author: SKK
Date: 2025-07-04T16:06:34Z
Content: Good morning I am new to the forum. I currently received a lease offer from Antero Resources for leasing 37 gross acres and net 0.08326 net mineral acres. Offer is $300 bonus and 15% royalties.

Author: Nick-TBM
Date: 2025-07-04T19:33:24Z
Content: Hi@SKKthey are saying that you only own 0.08326 of a mineral acre. The $300 signing bonus is due to the size of your parcel and is pretty much the minimum they will offer. You can ask for 18% royalty without deductions, but Antero is not offering leases without deductions any longer. They will not sign anything unless you pay a portion of the transportation fee’s. Just being realistic, you don’t have much to negotiate with.

Author: WTX878
Date: 2025-07-04T21:59:02Z
Content: The bonus isn’t as important as the royalty rate, especially with a small interest. I would however, recommend you push for at least an 18% royalty rate.

Author: DT11
Date: 2025-07-04T21:59:35Z
Content: That offer is bottom line.  You have a small interest so it’s hard to bargain unless you are sitting on a “Motherload” tract that the company needs to finish their wells.  Best i can give you is do lots of reading and lots of research.  You can drive yourself crazy with this mineral rights stuff.  Nancy Mosley and myself can attest to all the work that can be put into leasing and such.   There are some knowledgeable folks on here that can help.  Listen and learn.  The percentage of royalty should be in the neighborhood of 18 to 20 percent.  Gross at the well head cuts out all the post production cost that eat up your share of the royalty.  Thats what we settled on.  There are items in the lease that should be deleted and some that should be added.  This info pertains to everyone dealing with a company wanting to lease your mineral rights.  There will be those that contribute on here that will give you some of those items.  I am presently retired from the mineral stuff because i get frustrated and a headache when i think about Antero.  Lol

Author: JP1316
Date: 2025-07-05T06:04:14Z
Content: Do we ever see any royalty payments? Thats the question I cant get answered

Author: SKK
Date: 2025-07-05T19:45:18Z
Content: Should I ask for **free from the costs related to production” including taxes”?

Author: Nancy_Mosley
Date: 2025-07-05T21:19:39Z
Content: You can ask for no costs, including taxes; no warranty of title, and no right of first refusal for sale. See what you get. Also research the WV Co-tenancy laws, and forced pooling. There are some good terms in there for those who do not lease but get forced into one. Or consult an attorney. Remember free advice not necessarily worth anything!

Author: SKK
Date: 2025-07-07T17:02:46Z
Content: What is the big difference between “Gross Reduction Clause” and “Wellhead Royalty - No Deductions”.

Author: SylviaG
Date: 2025-07-09T20:32:10Z
Content: I would recommend having a lawyer look over any contracts BEFORE you agree and/or sign anything.  There are some who post here. I have used Kyle Nuttall
304-473-1403. He has been very helpful.

Author: Land101
Date: 2025-07-10T23:25:42Z
Content: Can you elaborate on the “Gross Reduction Clause”?. Wellhead Royalty means you would not be paid on NGLs but instead you are paid based on the BTU factor of the gas coming out at the wellhead. In theory, it should be similar but depends on downstream contracts, etc the operator has and how efficiently they are transporting the gas to market.

Author: Christy
Date: 2025-07-10T15:02:42Z
Content: Our mother passed away and left us her inherited Mineral Interest in several Oklahoma counties.  We are living out of state and so was she.  She has a Trust and Will.  Some of her Deeds were transferred to her Trust but others were not. We are unsure about how to approach this.  There are royalties coming in but we are unable to deposit checks unless they are written to the name of the Trust and not all of them are. We would like to transfer all known ownership/deeds, go on record as the beneficiaries and track down all other interest to get it properly recorded in our names. She was not able to complete this task but has piles of paperwork. We need to track the transfer of title on several dating back to our grandfather. Our goal is to divide the interest between my sibling and me and place it into our individual Family Trust for our kids. and dissolve the Trust. We have tried using Proof of Death & Heirship but we feel there is a cleaner way to do this having a Trust Document. Some of the operators want a Final Decree and others just the Death & Heirship filed in the county to pay royalties to us but the bigger picture is being notified down the road. We want all of this to be clean and filed correctly. Any advise would be very much appreciated. Thank you!

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-07-10T23:25:31Z
Content: Sorry for the loss of your mother.
The properties transferred into the trust alreadyshouldbe fairly straightforward.  For properties not retitled into the trust the probate would be the cleanest route.  Her estate may be eligible for a summary probate which can usually be completed remotely and fairly quickly.

rag_documents.title: Beware ROFR Clause In Drake and Vanna II Leases
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Beware ROFR Clause In Drake and Vanna II Leases

Author: Donald_wilson
Date: 2025-07-09T00:20:50Z
Content: My family and some of our neighbors have been receiving lease offers from Vanna II and Drake Exploration in Anderson County, and based off my research on here, these Entities are leasing for Expand Energy. PLEASE BE CAREFUL of the Right of First Refusal Clause in these leases regarding mineral sales, the one’s I’ve seen read as follows: “The Lease further grants to Lessee a preferential right of first refusal for any offers to top lease or purchase underlying oil, gas, and mineral interests.”

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-07-09T00:54:51Z
Content: Drake is leasing for Expand, but Vanna is leasing for Mitsui.  These two companies are currently competing for acreage in Anderson County.  As of a few days ago, lease offers had reached $1,250/NMA bonus with 25% cost-free royalty.

Author: Ltaylor12
Date: 2025-07-09T19:36:17Z
Content: Yes, and from what I am hearing all the companies are going to be exercising these ROFR.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-07-10T01:07:42Z
Content: They cannot demand to purchase the minerals.  ROFR means that if the mineral owner wants to sell and negotiates a price, then he must reveal the offer to the oil company lessee and allow them to match it and buy instead.  Majority of mineral buyers will not bother to negotiate if the deal can be usurped by the lessee.  No one should sign a lease with this provision.  This is just another example of why it is so important to understand all the legal implications of any lease (contract) that you sign.  Leases can last decades and you do not get to renegotiate the terms.

Date: 2025-07-09T19:52:03Z
Content: Merit Energy Company (Dallas, TX) has purchased wells in Oklahoma that I have mineral interests in. They purchased them from XTO. I was wondering if anyone has dealt with Merit Energy and what I can expect when one company sells to another. These are producing wells. The production has decreased some over the last fifteen years but they still pay every month. I am a relatively new mineral owner and haven’t experienced this yet.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-07-09T21:35:36Z
Content: It may take a few months to straighten everything out, but royalty payments usually continue.  Some buyers take the pay deck from the previous operator and just continue as usual.  Some buyers do a more advanced title work job to make sure that the pay deck is correct.  Save your statements from XTO for seven years and you also want them to compare the wells and the decimals to make sure they match when the new checks come.

Content: Hello. I recently found out I have over 25 acres of land in Harrison County, WV. I’ve been contacted and offered 2k per acre for a term of 5 years plus royalties at 15%. Author: Petroleum9202
Date: 2025-07-09T20:31:46Z
Content: @labyrinthqueen3800-​ I would call back the Landman and ask if he can explain the title to you. A lot of people in West Virginia own a net acreage amount. It will be helpful to know what that company shows in their title abstract about what you own so you can present that to an attorney.

posts.author: Nancy_Mosley

If you want to see this on a map, go to the WV Office of Oil and Gas website and search for the map database (WVDEP Oil&Gas Well Information) and put in 95-02889  or 95-02890 (they are both in the Ivory Unit.) See if that makes sense and if it is what you are looking for.

Author: Rieter
Date: 2025-07-05T18:55:53Z
Content: So these have been in my family for a while. My father passed away this year and I had the paperwork to get the deed transferred to me. I know there is one well thats been going off and on since it looks like 1981 and nothing else. What are my options to make money with this? How can I get them evaluated for sale or lease to do something with them instead of the occasional 100 check? This is all very new to me and honestly, id rather just sale them than have to worry about the taxes each year. what advice if any is there? Like mentioned, how do I turn this into money either a better re-occuring profit or just sell? I appreciate the help and if theres any other questions, please let me know! Thanks!

Author: KyndallLeone
Date: 2025-07-08T17:56:03Z
Content: Those sections mostly have only a handful of plugged and abandoned wells.  The geology of that area is not likely going to be of interest to anyone to lease.  Even in good areas, they come to you with a planned prospect.  The portion that is still tied to the producing well is not available to lease, either.  So, you can continue receiving royalties or sell.  To sell, you can expect to get 3-5x what the annual revenue is.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-07-08T18:25:51Z
Content: If your name and address and title information are properly filed in the county, leasing agents will come to you.  The closest permits are in 29/32 5N-6W and going into into 5-4N-6W about six miles to the east.  Gulfport is the operator

Content: I’ve gotten two offers on 23-17S-1W in the past six months. Anyone know what’s going on? It’s been producing small amounts for years so surprised to get offers.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-04-30T18:39:35Z
Content: Not really any new activity out there. Someone is probably putting together a prospect to drill based on historical data. Maybe a zone that was previously missed. Looks like a good section to own in. You have any others in KS?

Author: Evan_Thomas
Date: 2025-04-30T18:55:51Z
Content: In KS, I just have more up in Greenwood Co, not here. Do they have to get a spacing unit approved by the state here? And allow force pooling? I don’t know much about KS! Thx.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-05-01T19:22:56Z
Content: These are normally 160acre leases or smaller, usually not less than 80. Units are not common in this area. Forced pooling very rare in Kansas from my experience. Greenwood County is a good one. Are your interests there producing?

Author: Evan_Thomas
Date: 2025-05-01T20:07:43Z
Content: Thanks for the info. I have one active producer in Greenwood, which doesn’t seem to be on this forum, even.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-05-02T19:32:03Z
Content: Greenwood is very remote. But very old production. Some good leases there. Definitely on my radar.

Author: Evan_Thomas
Date: 2025-05-05T20:29:13Z
Content: I need to get a runner to pull my deeds there and McPherson. I’m running off legal docs that are 60 years old! Those counties don’t appear to be online for deeds as old as mine.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-05-06T13:50:04Z
Content: Call the register of deeds and ask if you can order a copy of the index for your section, patent to present. Many counties will let you do that at a reasonable price.

Author: Evan_Thomas
Date: 2025-05-06T14:30:55Z
Content: I’ve twice tried with Greenwood and they twice told me to hire a landman. I might have better luck with McPherson.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-05-13T13:55:42Z
Content: Technically the records are public and by asking for a copy of a known document (like the index records for a specific section) that is not “research”, which is what some counties attempt to use as their excuse to not have to make you copies. Now if you don’t know the document you need, technically that is research and they do not have to look it up for you. You can always file your request as a KORA request - check that out.

Content: Hi.  I live in Ohio and got a call from Country Roads Minerals asking to purchase my small   0.7937 net mineral ac I own in Marion county Mannington district
Parcels: 12-15-10,11,11.1,11.2,11.3,11.4,11.5, 12(PART)  for $2,000.00   I had no clue I inherited this or if it’s a lot or little     They did their research on how I ended up with it    Any help will be greatly appreciated

Author: erinyes

Content: Hi. I’m kind of in the same situation with a different company contacting me. I know very little about this stuff and I’m trying to figure out which companies are fair and reputable. I’m also in Ohio with the property in West Virginia.

Date: 2025-06-29T02:09:54Z
Content: I think you can do better but it depends on where it is. Mannington is a good spot. Is it under an existing lease?

Author: Petroleum9202
Date: 2025-06-29T15:55:22Z
Content: @emilysma1995- CR is offering to purchase before the drilling operator (EQT) gets to your area. If you don’t need to sell, wait for the drilling operator to present you an oil and gas lease. That offer from CR is very low.

Author: WVGAS
Date: 2025-06-30T01:28:07Z
Content: Country Roads is going to flip that to an energy company (EQT?) or investors. Their first offers are always low ball.  Don’t take it.  Ask for 10K or 12k an acre Don;t fall for their 'money in your bank account in 14 days." There is a good chance someone is readying to drill those tracts, hich makes the property valuable.

Author: Petroleum9202
Date: 2025-07-03T00:51:18Z
Content: @emilysma1995- Yes, they may be correct on that, but you are unleased and can get an average of $3K to $5K per net acre on the lease bonus, and if you decide to sell it after you lease it, you can get another $3K to $6K an acre, on average.

Author: Land101
Date: 2025-07-07T18:27:09Z
Content: If you are ultimately wanting to sell, you should consider the tax implications of leasing 1st before selling. A buyer should account for that potential lease bonus and pay up accordingly. Keep in mind you are paying ordinary income tax on a lease bonus and you would pay capital gains on the sale.
