Topic: Lithium royalty lease

Author: robstacks
Date: 2025-04-12T18:16:54Z
Content: My wife has recently been in contact with a firm about a lithium royalty lease in Hopkins county. It looks like there was some previous discussions in the forum but they were all closed within 90 days for no activity. We are curious as to the going royalty rates and bonus payments. We are somewhat familiar with oil and gas leases but have no experience with lithium. Any comments would be appreciated.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-25T13:26:46Z
Content: Lithium royalty rates are much lower than oil and gas and vary from state to state.  The market is fairly fluid on them right now as the technology and companies working on it are still emerging.  The first draft leases that I have seen were not very good (in my opinion).  The wording looked like it had been copied and pasted from various oil and gas leases and was contradictory from paragraph to paragraph, so be very careful.  Would suggest that an experienced oil and gas or surface attorney review any lease.  Various state legislations are working on bills regarding lithium.

Author: Lisa61
Date: 2025-06-03T18:29:47Z
Content: We are about to sign a lease in Franklin/Titus. We are working with a lawyer— but we need to decide the royalty percentage. I’m curious what others are getting. We’ve been advised 3.5% would be possible, but that we should try to find what others are getting.

Author: Phil_Sartin
Date: 2025-06-03T20:29:39Z
Content: I can’t help you with the royalty rate, but I can say that, for me, it would be important to know if the royalty being offered is cost free or cost bearing.  I’ve heard of some companies that offer 1/16th royalty and another offered 1/8th, but both cases are cost bearing.  The royalty owners, in my opinion, will never see the full royalty amount because of deductions.  Check your lease to see what can be deducted if it is, in fact, a cost bearing royalty.

Author: Lisa61
Date: 2025-06-05T09:57:09Z
Content: Our royalties percentage is on gross. Our lawyer explained to us how the language of our lease protects us from almost all production costs— but I couldn’t explain it if I had to!!

Author: TFD
Date: 2025-06-06T01:58:53Z
Content: Who is the operator and/or brokerage company who proposed the lease?

Content: Our contact is with a landman but the contract is being offered by Stamdard Lithium.

rag_documents.title: How to find out how many acres you have?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: How to find out how many acres you have?

Author: David_C_Fouts
Date: 2025-04-09T18:41:45Z
Content: Hello all, I have mineral rights in Roger Mills, OK 02-17n-25w.  I inherited the rights and have done searches OCC and have found copies of the leases, but no where does it say how many acres.  What should be my next step.

Author: Baylor
Date: 2025-04-09T19:10:20Z
Content: Time to do some Real “Landman” work.  You will need to go back in the deed Records to the point where the surface is separated from the minerals or vice versa.  Then trace conveyance and appropriate percentages to where your predecessor acquired it.  Then family percentages separated until it hits Your percentage.

Author: David_C_Fouts
Date: 2025-04-09T19:27:31Z
Content: Which means I have to go in and page thru the books?

Author: Baylor
Date: 2025-04-09T20:26:31Z
Content: You can do as much as possible online.  Then you may or may not have to resort to some hard time in Deed Records of the Roger Mills Courthouse.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-09T22:02:50Z
Content: Contact the Division Order analyst for Mewbourne Oil.  They have the Sylvia 2 CO 2HT well which is probably spaced to include the whole section which would include your acreage.  Tell them that you just inherited and need to get into pay status and ask them how many net acres you have and what lease or force pooling is holding the acres.  Have the name of your ancestor and be ready to provide probate information, death certificate, etc.

Author: Linda_Jenkins
Date: 2025-06-25T23:13:53Z
Content: The RMC County Clerk records online are very user friendly. Many ways to search by different criteria. You won’t need to go through page after page.

Content: Okay. So you know the Counties and State; that’s a good start. You should have some form of legal documentation showing that it was left to you. Author: jtarbutton
Date: 2025-06-08T20:09:46Z
Content: My brother and I each own 25.8 acres in 3 surveys: A-263, A-714 & A-1098. As far as I know, these are non-producing. We have been presented with an offer of $400/acre and 20% royalty for three years. Does anyone know of activity in these areas and if this is a fair offer? Thanks.

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-06-08T21:01:20Z
Content: Is you offer from Vanna Production?  Based on what’s been filed in the Deed Records so far, Vanna has leased 170 acres in the A-263 and 450 acres in a combination of A-262 and A-714.

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-06-09T01:32:09Z
Content: As AH has indicated, bonus amounts are not public or recorded anywhere. I would give up some bonus money to get a higher royalty.
And a cost-free lease is absolutely what you will want to get - highly recommend that you have a lawyer look over all paperwork before making a decision.

Author: George_D_Cato
Date: 2025-06-09T01:32:30Z
Content: My guess is that they will be willing to go higher than $400/acre bonus but I do not know this area, and I would be firm at 25% royalty.    Mr. Harrington is correct.  Costs for gathering, compression, and other treatment, plus transportation can be extremely high for gas wells.  I would recommend you use an Oil & Gas attorney for this lease.  Just saying “no costs” doesn’t work. The issue of post production costs is the subject of much litigation.  We have our own lease and our O&G attorney has modified our “No cost” and other revenue provisions periodically to make sure we stay up.

Author: poillon1
Date: 2025-06-09T21:36:42Z
Content: Consider negoiation on a 4 year term to keep the upfront and royalty high.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-06-25T17:43:11Z
Content: What I think is happening in Anderson, Leon, Houston and other Counties in this natural gas play is that there are brokers, smaller companies, and individuals speculating, trying to lease “cheap” and flip the leases to make a profit and get an over ride at the mineral owners expense. Most all of these people do not have the money to drill a 30 Million Dollar well and get it into production.

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-06-25T17:57:06Z
Content: It appears that Mitsui and Expand are pulling in more landmen to lease on their behalf in order to get as much acreage leased as quickly as possible since they are competing with each other.  A lease offering a 25% royalty is unlikely to be coming from a flipper.

posts.content: My brother and I each own 25.8 acres in 3 surveys: A-263, A-714 & A-1098. As far as I know, these are non-producing. We have been presented with an offer of $400/acre and 20% royalty for three years. Does anyone know of activity in these areas and if this is a fair offer? Thanks.

posts.author: Alan_Herrington
posts.content: Is you offer from Vanna Production?  Based on what’s been filed in the Deed Records so far, Vanna has leased 170 acres in the A-263 and 450 acres in a combination of A-262 and A-714.

posts.author: Rock_Man
posts.content:
As AH has indicated, bonus amounts are not public or recorded anywhere. I would give up some bonus money to get a higher royalty.
And a cost-free lease is absolutely what you will want to get - highly recommend that you have a lawyer look over all paperwork before making a decision.

posts.author: George_D_Cato
posts.content: My guess is that they will be willing to go higher than $400/acre bonus but I do not know this area, and I would be firm at 25% royalty.    Mr. Harrington is correct.  Costs for gathering, compression, and other treatment, plus transportation can be extremely high for gas wells.  I would recommend you use an Oil & Gas attorney for this lease.  Just saying “no costs” doesn’t work. The issue of post production costs is the subject of much litigation.  We have our own lease and our O&G attorney has modified our “No cost” and other revenue provisions periodically to make sure we stay up.

posts.author: poillon1
posts.content: Consider negoiation on a 4 year term to keep the upfront and royalty high.

posts.author: Mineral_Owner5
posts.content: What I think is happening in Anderson, Leon, Houston and other Counties in this natural gas play is that there are brokers, smaller companies, and individuals speculating, trying to lease “cheap” and flip the leases to make a profit and get an over ride at the mineral owners expense. Most all of these people do not have the money to drill a 30 Million Dollar well and get it into production.

posts.author: Alan_Herrington
posts.content: It appears that Mitsui and Expand are pulling in more landmen to lease on their behalf in order to get as much acreage leased as quickly as possible since they are competing with each other.  A lease offering a 25% royalty is unlikely to be coming from a flipper.

rag_documents.title: Should I call the Operator
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Should I call the Operator

Author: ajaxup
Date: 2025-06-20T02:42:06Z
Content: I have a royalty interest in Howard County Texas that has two wells currently producing oil and gas. I receive offers all the time in the mail for either one of them or both. I keep the ones that have prices quoted for whatever the buyer is interested. I recently received an off on one of the wells that’s almost five times the highest I’ve ever received. I’m thinking about calling the well operator to see if they have any information or opinion about the offer but I don’t know if that’s a proper thing to ask them or if it’s a no-no. Any advice appreciated since I’m obviously a neophyte in the oil royalties arena.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-20T04:47:33Z
Content: An operator will not disclose proprietary information and research about plans it is considering as that could give others the opportunity to jump in and grab some of the action.  Nor will they give you an analysis of an offer as that could lead you to claim you got bad advice and lost money by either selling or holding on to your minerals.  You can look at fling of permits and spudding of wells around your minerals by reviewing data on the RRC website.   if you post the legal description or the wells, then someone familiar with Howard County can help you.

Author: rcfish
Date: 2025-06-20T14:20:22Z
Content: Don’t think the operator is the best one to get an opinion from.  They might be interested in buying you out and offer you just a bit more to induce you to sell.

Author: ajaxup
Date: 2025-06-23T01:10:07Z
Content: Actually the 5x offer was referring to it was 5x of the biggest offer I’d ever received for that particular well. As far as times the production, looking at my statements attached to my monthly checks the offer appears to be somewhere around 60x the annual amount it throws off.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-24T13:58:01Z
Content: Think further ahead than just the current wells.  If you are getting offers, then the buyers likely know of pending activity.  If your current wells are conventional vertical wells, the offers are probably from companies that are looking for future horizontal wells.  They certainly intend to make a profit off of you.

rag_documents.title: Lease Offer $1000/nma
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Lease Offer $1000/nma

Author: acestacy
Date: 2025-06-17T15:51:16Z
Content: I recently received a lease offer for Section 30-10 North – 08 West.
I was offered $1,000 per Net Mineral Acre s, of which I have 4 total.
I was curious whether that was a reasonable offer for a 3-year lease with 2-year extension offered for an additional $1000 per acre if the extension was picked up.
Any thoughts from the members would be appreciated.
Thank you.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-18T02:03:29Z
Content: Your offer is tied to a royalty percentage, so that needs to be included or it doesn’t have all the information.  Usually first offers are open to higher negotiation.  Many of us would want a 1/5th or 1/4 lease which would have a lower bonus.  The clauses in the lease are much more important than the bonus amount.  If you have never leased before, it would be wise to get a good oil and gas attorney to review the lease as the drafts need significant edits.

Author: acestacy
Date: 2025-06-18T16:08:16Z
Content: Yes, I should have mentioned that there is a 3/16ths attached to the lease.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-24T13:20:24Z
Content: The 1/5th and 1/4 royalty will have a lower bonus, but the payout on a successful well over the years will usually far surpass the bonus amount.No leases have been filed in that section in the last 24 months, so the timing is early in the game and you may get other offers.  I always ask about the other options.

Author: CSR30srlty
Date: 2025-06-22T17:40:55Z
Content: In the process of creating an Heirship Affidavit for TX mineral rights, I discovered an unprobated will from West Virginia. My TX attorney said I need to get a referral for a WV estate or probate attorney to discuss the probate options. I contacted the WV Bar Assn. and was given only one name, but he hasn’t responded. Does anyone know where I should go now for a WV referral?

Author: galetime
Date: 2025-06-23T02:54:29Z
Content: Maybe I’m misunderstanding, but … the most currently dated will is the only one that can be determined as valid, no matter in what state it was written.  I assume it was written in WV, so, if the person has passed, you should contact the attorney or the firm of that Will in WV or have your own attorney contact them.  Whichever Will is determined as valid, probated, and Letters of Administration issued, then a move forward with the mineral rights can occur.

Berkeley County said it hadn’t even been registered with them, so no probate, no Letters of Administration, nothing to get the ball rolling in TX. rag_documents.title: Could someone explain this to me in simple terms
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Could someone explain this to me in simple terms

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-04T22:39:57Z
Content: Iam2bearJune 4, 2025, 10:39pm1Lessor hereby warrants and agrees to defend the title to the lands herein described, and
agrees that the Lessee shall have the right at any time to redeem for Lessor, by payment, any
mortgages, taxes or other liens on the above described lands, in the event of default of payment
by Lessor, and be subrogated to the rights of the holder thereof, and the undersigned Lessors, for
themselves and their heirs, successors and assigns, hereby surrender and release all right of
dower and homestead in the premises described herein, insofar as said right of dower and
homestead may in any way affect the purposes for which this lease is made, as recited herein.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-06-04T23:44:10Z
Content: Two sentences, different purposes. Part of the first sentence is a warranty, wherein the lessor guarantees that he/she has title.
The last part of the first sentence allows the lessor to pay off any past due lien, mortgage or taxes that the lessor owns which could impact the lessor’s title, because these items may be superior or prior in time to the lease. An example, the lessor owes taxes and if sold, the lessee would lose their lease. So, the lessee oil company pays the taxes to avoid a foreclosure or tax sale. They then can recover the funds from any royalties owed to the lessee.
The last part dealing with dower and curtesy is a clause that says that this is not the lessors homestead and In waiving homestead rights, the parties are agreeing that the lease shall have legal priority over any statutory exemption that may be present for a person’s home if the owner were to file bankruptcy.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-05T04:04:19Z
Content: But this is for mineral rights leasing. There would be no mortgage, lein or taxes. There is a house on the land, but…I flipped out at “default of payment by lessor” I want to GET paid not being paying anything. Thank you so much for your explanation.

Author: jvt
Date: 2025-06-05T21:46:39Z
Content: If your mineral rights are not severed from the surface ownership, then a foreclosure of the surface property would also be a foreclosure of the mineral rights.  This clause protects the oil & gas operator from a default by the property owner that might invalidate the lease..

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-05T22:12:53Z
Content: All clauses are negotiable in the lease and can be changed or deleted.  The warranty clause is of some concern in the event such as an earlier deed reserved all or portion of the minerals.  You may want to consider either no warranty or limited warranty such as by, through and under lessor.  Depending on your state, statutes and case law will affect your warranty language.  You mention a house - is that your home?

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-05T22:51:08Z
Content: Wow. That had never occurred to me that it could be a chunk that hasnt had the mineral rights severed or that a forclosure of one would effect the other. I was totally confused. So severed doesn’t mean totally, every time. I love learning and thank you for your knowledge and time, jvt. It is very much appreciated.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-05T22:59:02Z
Content: No, the home is not mine. In fact I’m not 100% convinced the mineral rights are mine. The independant landman said the leases were closing so if i didnt agree to sign, he wouldn’t even rush me a lease. I had 6 hours to decide.
A day later he sent it through acusign=bahahah. I’m blonde, not dumb. I am in Minnesota, but this land is in North Dakota. I may have missed an opportunity, but I wont sign legal stuff in a rush-ever. Although a couple of young family members did sign. I am afraid for them.
Thank you so much for your input and time, TennisDaze. You guys are so, so, so valuable!

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-06-07T14:08:35Z
Content: Well, you can always have a mortgage on minerals rights owned.
The company would only come in and pay any mortgage, lien or taxes if the lessor was in default. If they are not in default, and not in danger of losing their lease, they would take no action.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-07T15:29:22Z
Content: I was unaware that you could use mineral right for collateral. And what would be the circumstances as to why you would lose your lease? I was under the impression that once its signed, you are locked in tight. I appreciate your input, Tim_dowd. Thank you.

Author: LookingAtPosts
Date: 2025-06-09T19:17:06Z
Content: On oil & gas leases, I always line out, “hereby warrants and agrees to defend the title to the lands herein described, and” in the first sentence. Most times lessors will request/demand same prior to my offering to do it.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-20T15:02:03Z
Content: Thank you so much for your knowledge. I appreciate it tremendously.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-20T15:03:50Z
Content: Wow, I have never had them offer to void that part. In fact, I thought it would void the lease and its intentions. Thank you.

Author: jvt
Date: 2025-06-21T11:14:27Z
Content: Remember that an oil and gas lease is a contract and like any other contract everything is negotiable.   If you don’t like a clause, delete it.  The lessor can decide whether they can operate under those conditions.  If not, then the lessor and lessee can try to negotiate.

Author: Terrel_Shields
Date: 2025-06-22T02:34:49Z
Content: Oil companies pledge minerals to the bank all the time. But again if the minerals are not severed and the loans are with a bank, they will have title to ‘fee simple’ not just ‘fee in surface’. In fact, FSA usually then severs and keeps mineral rights on farms where they foreclose on the fee simple. If you have severed minerals sometimes there are banks or private parties who will loan on the minerals and any proceeds are paid to them to repay the loan, It is not uncommon in some parts of the states.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: Marshall Marcellus Shale Lease Questions

Author: livetoski78
Date: 2025-06-17T14:51:05Z
Content: I found out I have a 12.5% share of ~100 acres currently under development in Webster District.  What kind of lease offer should I be looking for here in 2025?  I assume I just negotiate for ~12.5 acres (representing my share in the lease agreement?  I see people posting about demanding no pooling, no storage, etc.  Anything else I should be concerned about?  Thanks in advance as I’m new to this stuff!

Author: dome
Date: 2025-06-19T15:06:56Z
Content: Welcome to the forum. As a starting point to better educate yourself on these issues I suggest going to the Marshall County documents site 129.71.117.225 and select Book and Page on the dropdown and then type in 1228 in the Book box and 18 in the Page box. A recent lease example from Southwestern Production (now Expand Energy) comes up and you can peruse the language. Pay particular attention to the Exhibit B and Addendum language in the later pages. This language modifies the boilerplate language in the lease. Things like royalty percentage, storage rights, no cost, hold harmless etc. That said do you know what company is proposing the lease? You need to confirm the net acres you own which the landman can supply. If it is the 12.5 you mentioned you should not settle for less than $4,000 per acre bonus and try to get $4,500 per. The royalty should be 18%, nothing less. They will always lowball in early offers. If you don’t feel comfortable negotiating an O&G attorney can certainly help. You mentioned the property is being developed. Have you been contacted or received a lease proposal? The documents site is a good reference to see what others are negotiating. The memorandum of leases on the site don’t always show complete detail although most from Southwestern are somewhat thorough. You can check earlier Books and Pages for earlier references. Good luck.

Author: Land101
Date: 2025-06-21T19:58:56Z
Content: Not sure why you wouldn’t allow for pooling. If you want your interest horizontally developed (which is the only way to realize the value here), you want to allow for pooling. I don’t think anyone would agree to this anyway. You may have heard someone mention a limitation on the amount of total acres allowed in the unit you are pooled in. This is because in some cases, if the unit you are in is too large in relation to the length of the wells, your interest can be diluted. In my opinion, I don’t think this is something worth negotiating over though. At some point you have to trust the process because ultimately the operator is going to develop the acreage the best possible way they can. It has to do with the area, the geology, dry gas vs liquids, etc. Dry gas areas typically require the need for wider spacing “bigger unit/well length”. Hope that helps.

posts.content: I found out I have a 12.5% share of ~100 acres currently under development in Webster District.  What kind of lease offer should I be looking for here in 2025?  I assume I just negotiate for ~12.5 acres (representing my share in the lease agreement?  I see people posting about demanding no pooling, no storage, etc.  Anything else I should be concerned about?  Thanks in advance as I’m new to this stuff!

posts.author: dome
posts.content: Welcome to the forum. As a starting point to better educate yourself on these issues I suggest going to the Marshall County documents site 129.71.117.225 and select Book and Page on the dropdown and then type in 1228 in the Book box and 18 in the Page box. A recent lease example from Southwestern Production (now Expand Energy) comes up and you can peruse the language. Pay particular attention to the Exhibit B and Addendum language in the later pages. This language modifies the boilerplate language in the lease. Things like royalty percentage, storage rights, no cost, hold harmless etc. That said do you know what company is proposing the lease? You need to confirm the net acres you own which the landman can supply. If it is the 12.5 you mentioned you should not settle for less than $4,000 per acre bonus and try to get $4,500 per. The royalty should be 18%, nothing less. They will always lowball in early offers. If you don’t feel comfortable negotiating an O&G attorney can certainly help. You mentioned the property is being developed. Have you been contacted or received a lease proposal? The documents site is a good reference to see what others are negotiating. The memorandum of leases on the site don’t always show complete detail although most from Southwestern are somewhat thorough. You can check earlier Books and Pages for earlier references. Good luck.

posts.author: Land101
posts.content: Not sure why you wouldn’t allow for pooling. If you want your interest horizontally developed (which is the only way to realize the value here), you want to allow for pooling. I don’t think anyone would agree to this anyway. You may have heard someone mention a limitation on the amount of total acres allowed in the unit you are pooled in. This is because in some cases, if the unit you are in is too large in relation to the length of the wells, your interest can be diluted. In my opinion, I don’t think this is something worth negotiating over though. At some point you have to trust the process because ultimately the operator is going to develop the acreage the best possible way they can. It has to do with the area, the geology, dry gas vs liquids, etc. Dry gas areas typically require the need for wider spacing “bigger unit/well length”. Hope that helps.

Content: Normally a lease provides for royalties to be paid when gas is sold.  I have not seen gas storage volumes being reported, at least in Permian. Topic: Expired mineral rights

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-16T10:47:13Z
Content: I am sure once I hear your answers, I will feel dumb, but…What is to stop the average “jo”, a rogue landman, or the oil companies for that matter, from claiming your mineral rights if they are past 20 years old (deed wise). I do believe ND is a 20 year inactivity law. Can it only revert to the landowner or state?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-18T02:31:19Z
Content: In ND, the rights would revert to the surface owner if not producing.  If you have passed the 20 year time line, you can try to file to keep them.  If I remember correctly, the surface owner would have to make the claim.  It is not automatic.

Author: DaveH
Date: 2025-06-18T12:53:17Z
Content: M_Barnes is right.  File a Statement of Claim to your interests with the lands and your contact information properly identified in the county where your lands are located as soon as you can.  The surface owner has to have a quiet title proceeding in court to vest the mineral interest in them which includes notice to those parties whose addresses are of record in the county records.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-17T19:28:25Z
Content: Noble Energy is operating multiple producing wells in Section 207.  There is likely to be significant funds in suspense.  So the investor may have paid your brother with his own money.  Noble Energy is now owned by Chevron.  You need to establish your title and get in pay with Noble / Chevron. Also check Texas Unclaimed Property under both your father’s name and your name to see if some of the funds are there.   Clay Prewit 206-207 Unit A 1H (42-389-38866 - RRC 08-54973); Clay Prewit 206-207 Unit B 3H (42-389-38867 - RRC 08-54809); and Clay Prewit 206-207 Unit C 5H (42-389-38847 - RRC 08-54827).  Sam Prewit 207 (42-389-33690 - RRC 08-44565) ceased operating in 2019, but you would be due royalties for that well too.

Author: Apache
Date: 2025-06-06T13:09:33Z
Content: I am seeking any information about Brine Well offers by Summit Land Co. on behalf of Woodward Iodine Company (WIC) in Dewey Co., Okla. My mother rec’d an offer of $2.50/acre “bonus” offer and then 3% of profits of sold iodine.  We have a Landman in the family who lives in that area and he says he doesn’t think they are offering enough, but if no other companies are offering, then the only comparison is $0, so holding out awhile in hopes of a better offer might make sense and be a good strategy, but there’s also the variable of whether someone is 95 y/o vs. 50 y/o as to whether it makes sense to accept the offer that’s on the current table.  Curious about thoughts, insights and other information re: this offer and if brine well drilling is going to be more prevalent, therefore becoming more competitive in this area with more offers likely in the future.

Author: John_Wilcox
Date: 2025-06-08T21:00:16Z
Content: Hi Apache,
We received the exact same offer from Summit Land Company also regarding Dewey County. I don’t know if forced pooling will apply for this situation but I’m thinking that might nudge the dollars up a little bit. I don’t know for sure. rag_documents.content:
Topic: Order of payment acres on Matador lease - TBD

Author: Jasper
Date: 2025-06-13T23:03:13Z
Content: The “Order of Payment” page included in my Matador lease offer contains $/Acre but does not contain the estimated interest or net mineral acres. It shows TBD.
I’m assuming they haven’t done their research yet. Normal, not normal, risk?    Sign and send with the signed lease?
Thanks

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-14T02:40:51Z
Content: I never sign an order of payment!  I never hand over a signed lease without getting paid.  If you do, a lease can be filed and you might never get paid.  I make a copy of the signed lease and use a big black marker across every page COPY DO NOT FILE and send to the agent.  I have an attorney, accountant or bank officer hold the lease until payment arrives and it cashed.  Then they will hand over the signed lease to the agent to be filed.  I understand that it can take weeks to run title.  My handing over a copy shows my good faith, so that they can run title.  But they cannot have the lease until they pay for it.

Author: Jasper
Date: 2025-06-14T15:41:24Z
Content: If I have already signed it and have an attorney holding it, how do I know they will get the net acres correct? Is it normal to see TBD?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-15T17:12:53Z
Content: From your post, I assume that you do not know your NMA.  Unless you do your own title research, then you will be dependent on the oil company’s determination.  You might ask for a copy of the title history into you.  Matador May consider that proprietary information as it will have other unleased owners and will have been costly to have done.  But gather and save whatever title information you can amass for your own use and to pass on to your heirs.

rag_documents.title: Shouldn't a 'lot' be listed on the lease?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Shouldn't a 'lot' be listed on the lease?

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-05T15:36:13Z
Content: I have a lease for consideration via a private landman. the township 162N, Range 102W of 5th, Section 6:SE4 in North Dakota. Is the SE4 the lot? or does this not contain a lot#?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-05T16:16:52Z
Content: “Lots” are for city plats or can also be for irregularly spaced sections.  In your case, SE4 is fine.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-05T16:34:52Z
Content: Thank you M_Barnes. I have put my faith in you and your responses for years and truly appreciate your knowledge. Most of this stuff makes my head spin!
I do have some follow up questions if you dont mind. There isn’t really a division percent space on a affidavit. Where would it be added? Perhaps added/stapled with, like the death certificate?
He did send in the lease without a payment made. Does it matter if the check–which has not arrived yet, is cashed or not? I thought it had to be cashed before the lease could be filed.
Again, thank you. Not everyone is so willing to help.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-05T16:49:28Z
Content: The affidavit part is a question for an attorney as to what is required in ND.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-05T17:25:18Z
Content: So essentially, because he has signed it and returned it, it cant be undone. But when he gets a check for double the amount deserved, what will happen?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-05T21:55:09Z
Content: If you have evidence that contradicts the affidavit, then you can follow up with a different one. Best to talk to an attorney to have it done correctly.  The first leasing title opinion may not be the final one.

Author: Terrel_Shields
Date: 2025-06-06T14:17:49Z
Content: The legal is what the legal is. “Lot” is not a term universally used by surveyors.

Author: jsaa
Date: 2025-06-07T13:22:53Z
Content: Hello - my legal descriptions reference specific lots because the area of land owned changed due to the river changing since the original map was drawn from the Louisiana Purchase. When the land was sold years ago the deed referenced including any future accretions (additional land exposed as a result of waterways changing) so we were covered. When oil activity began, there was a new map to reflect the change in the riverbed exposing additional land (accretion). That additional land doesn’t fit in a perfect square so it was assigned lot numbers and specific acreage numbers. My deed legal description now references the specific lot numbers (and of course any future accretion that may happen…because you never know!). So my legal description has section numbers and quarter references, but also says lot numbers for those parts that are adjacent to an area of water.

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-07T20:30:27Z
Content: Indeed you are correct. The recent lease had no lot #, as I was comparing it to an old lease from a different area that did include a lot # (next to the river). So that is perfectly fits in my head now. Yes, the river area dead stoped payments for a great while with my previous land.
Thank you so much! You people are such a blessing, jsaa. I am now trying to explain it to my children so they never have the stress this has caused.. The boys seem to glaze over, but the girls seem to get the essence. i want them to utilize lawyers if needed, but I want them to be knowledgeable enough to seperate ‘legal from ethical, fair, or in their best interest.’ Again, I thank you so very much!

Author: jsaa
Date: 2025-06-10T16:36:03Z
Content: Glad to help! The oil company (Chord) is not paying us on our accretion acres so we have to hire an attorney to get some help with that which we are doing right now. It’s a pain and expensive but my sister and I want to get this cleared up for the next generation, and also so we can benefit from our property rather than the oil company just holding the royalties in suspense. They are not required to pay interest since they are considering it a title issue that needs to be addressed. Since it sounds like you have accretion acres you may have royalties building up that the oil company is holding in suspense. I’d call and ask. If you’re lucky they will tell you how much. But that’s hit and miss depending on who you talk to. Very frustrating.  Good luck!

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-10T16:45:05Z
Content: While you are using the attorney, be sure and get a copy of any new surveys that have been done that give you the accretion acres.  Important to keep in your files.  That river will continue to move, so having a stamp in time is important.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-06-11T00:21:59Z
Content: I have a lease for consideration via a private landman. the township 162N, Range 102W of 5th, Section 6:SE4 in North Dakota. Is the SE4 the lot? or does this not contain a lot#?

Content: thank you! I do have a copy of the new updated survey thanks to my mom’s diligence. I will make sure there hasn’t been another one since 2012 though!!!  Have a great day and thank you for your information

Author: Iam2bear
Date: 2025-06-15T14:52:52Z
Content: Bob 77, concerning the AOH and lease. One member signed as 50% heir, when they are actually 16.6% heir. He regrets signing, but has already turned the lease and the affidavit in. He has not recieved a bonus check yet. The widow (50%) found out last minute & remained unsigned, and two of his siblings( 16.6% heir) were not even contacted. There have been no other offers and all were unaware of this land at all. They do have land elsewhere in ND.
Thank you so much for your interest and reply.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-15T16:50:02Z
Content: It is not sufficient to simply regret signing a legal document which contains false information as that can have legal ramifications.  The signing claimant needs to immediately notify the other party that the affidavit is not true and revoke it.  Best to send a revocation and perhaps a replacement affidavit.  If the affidavit was filed in the deed records, then a correction affidavit should be filed.  Consult an attorney about how to do this effectively.

posts.content: “Lots” are for city plats or can also be for irregularly spaced sections.  In your case, SE4 is fine.

posts.author: Iam2bear
posts.content:
Thank you M_Barnes. I have put my faith in you and your responses for years and truly appreciate your knowledge. Most of this stuff makes my head spin!
I do have some follow up questions if you dont mind. There isn’t really a division percent space on a affidavit. Where would it be added? Perhaps added/stapled with, like the death certificate?
He did send in the lease without a payment made. Does it matter if the check–which has not arrived yet, is cashed or not? I thought it had to be cashed before the lease could be filed.
Again, thank you. Not everyone is so willing to help.

posts.author: M_Barnes
posts.content: The affidavit part is a question for an attorney as to what is required in ND.

posts.author: Iam2bear
posts.content: So essentially, because he has signed it and returned it, it cant be undone. But when he gets a check for double the amount deserved, what will happen?

posts.author: M_Barnes
posts.content: If you have evidence that contradicts the affidavit, then you can follow up with a different one. Best to talk to an attorney to have it done correctly.  The first leasing title opinion may not be the final one.

posts.author: Terrel_Shields
posts.content: The legal is what the legal is. “Lot” is not a term universally used by surveyors.

posts.author: jsaa
posts.content: Hello - my legal descriptions reference specific lots because the area of land owned changed due to the river changing since the original map was drawn from the Louisiana Purchase. When the land was sold years ago the deed referenced including any future accretions (additional land exposed as a result of waterways changing) so we were covered. When oil activity began, there was a new map to reflect the change in the riverbed exposing additional land (accretion). That additional land doesn’t fit in a perfect square so it was assigned lot numbers and specific acreage numbers. My deed legal description now references the specific lot numbers (and of course any future accretion that may happen…because you never know!). So my legal description has section numbers and quarter references, but also says lot numbers for those parts that are adjacent to an area of water.

posts.author: Iam2bear
posts.content:
Indeed you are correct. The recent lease had no lot #, as I was comparing it to an old lease from a different area that did include a lot # (next to the river). So that is perfectly fits in my head now. Yes, the river area dead stoped payments for a great while with my previous land.
Thank you so much! You people are such a blessing, jsaa. I am now trying to explain it to my children so they never have the stress this has caused.. The boys seem to glaze over, but the girls seem to get the essence. i want them to utilize lawyers if needed, but I want them to be knowledgeable enough to seperate ‘legal from ethical, fair, or in their best interest.’ Again, I thank you so very much!

posts.author: jsaa
posts.content: Glad to help! The oil company (Chord) is not paying us on our accretion acres so we have to hire an attorney to get some help with that which we are doing right now. It’s a pain and expensive but my sister and I want to get this cleared up for the next generation, and also so we can benefit from our property rather than the oil company just holding the royalties in suspense. They are not required to pay interest since they are considering it a title issue that needs to be addressed. Since it sounds like you have accretion acres you may have royalties building up that the oil company is holding in suspense. I’d call and ask. If you’re lucky they will tell you how much. But that’s hit and miss depending on who you talk to. Very frustrating.  Good luck!

posts.author: M_Barnes
posts.content: While you are using the attorney, be sure and get a copy of any new surveys that have been done that give you the accretion acres.  Important to keep in your files.  That river will continue to move, so having a stamp in time is important.

posts.content: I have a lease for consideration via a private landman. the township 162N, Range 102W of 5th, Section 6:SE4 in North Dakota. Is the SE4 the lot? or does this not contain a lot#?

posts.author: jsaa
posts.content: thank you! I do have a copy of the new updated survey thanks to my mom’s diligence. I will make sure there hasn’t been another one since 2012 though!!!  Have a great day and thank you for your information

posts.author: Iam2bear
posts.content:
Bob 77, concerning the AOH and lease. One member signed as 50% heir, when they are actually 16.6% heir. He regrets signing, but has already turned the lease and the affidavit in. He has not recieved a bonus check yet. The widow (50%) found out last minute & remained unsigned, and two of his siblings( 16.6% heir) were not even contacted. posts.author: TennisDaze
posts.content: It is not sufficient to simply regret signing a legal document which contains false information as that can have legal ramifications.  The signing claimant needs to immediately notify the other party that the affidavit is not true and revoke it.  Best to send a revocation and perhaps a replacement affidavit.  If the affidavit was filed in the deed records, then a correction affidavit should be filed.  Consult an attorney about how to do this effectively.

Author: kya0730
Date: 2025-06-10T02:11:24Z
Content: I have been trying to connect with TGNR regarding some funds in suspense.  When I send an email I get an automated response with an ID assigned to it and acknowledging receipt of my request.  No answers to my emails.  I started caller customer care and due to the language barrier it is difficult to have a conversation.  Each time I call I am told that the person assigned to my case will reply to my email by COB.  It has been almost 2 weeks and after repeated emails and phone calls they always say the same thing but I never get a reply email or phone call.  What can I do?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-10T12:44:22Z
Content: Have you tried sending a certified letter return receipt to their division order department?  Ask for the reasons that you are in suspense and what do you need to do to clear up the issue. It can take 60-90 days to resolve issues.  The DO folks are dealing with hundreds to thousands of requests.  In your letter, state your issue, give your name, address, email, phone number, description of acreage or well that you are asking about, the ID that you were assigned, ask if they need a W-9, etc.  It requires patience.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-10T16:35:47Z
Content: @M_Barnesprovides solid advice. I will generally grant a 60-90 day response period to many companies before I follow-up. Several calls in two weeks will not move you up in the Q. In the new OR models, the person taking calls can rarely solve your problem. Employ patient and employ diligence.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-10T16:43:45Z
Content: In general, the state oil and gas divisions do not help with operator payment issues.  That is between the mineral owner and the operator.

$400 seems a little low to me…

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-14T02:42:51Z
Content: I always ask for what they are offering for 1/5th and 1/4th.  First offers are usually low, so there is usually room for negotiation.  I prefer a higher royalty and am not so concerned about the bonus.  The clauses in the lease are more important.  It is wise to get legal advice from a good oil and gas attorney.  The draft lease from the agent is not in the mineral owner’s favor and needs significant edits.  An investment of good advice can reap rewards in better royalties for the life of the lease.

Author: Amyh37034
Date: 2025-05-12T15:19:47Z
Content: Hi - we inherited mineral rights and aren’t very familiar with the process. We thought all our land was leased so this was a surprise.  Is it safe to assume that they did their research and this land is not leased? Thank you for your help.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-12T16:17:38Z
Content: We cannot help unless you give us a state, county and location.

Author: Amyh37034
Date: 2025-05-12T17:56:45Z
Content: Thank you! It is in Colorado, township 7 north, range 63 west 6th pm Weld county Section 27:SE/4.  Really appreciate your help!

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-13T14:08:29Z
Content: You may have been leased at some time, but the old shallow wells that were permitted to be drilled have been cancelled, so the lease has probably expired.  The next set of wells were eight horizontal wells planned by Chevron.  They were permitted in 2018, and have also been cancelled. Those leases have probably also expired since it is now seven years later.  Hence, you are probably now open to be leased.

Author: Amyh37034
Date: 2025-05-13T16:49:42Z
Content: We had it reviewed by our oil and gas person and she says its held by production OGL 3687535. Does that mean anything to you? Thank you.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-14T14:26:24Z
Content: Ask her to explain what the number means.  It may be a lease code at the county courthouse, or it may be an internal company lease number.  Ask her where she found the information and what wells are holding the lease.  Ask for how to find a copy of the lease for your files.

Author: smurrah
Date: 2025-06-12T01:36:23Z
Content: How do you find a good oil and gas attorney?  Does it really make sense to pay for you if you have really small interests that don’t normally pay more than $150/yr?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-12T11:54:51Z
Content: I look in the bar association listings for specialists and ask ask around for recommendations.  A few were just given in another post for you.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-12T14:20:32Z
Content: The optimal leasing decision is difficult and personal. My preference is higher royalty and less time, but I manage several properties so patience is a greater component in my decision process. Since your property is in CO you have the benefit or hinderance, depending on your view, of forced pooling as a negotiation factor. Value generally increase the closer you get to the commencement of drilling. The development of horizontal wells is rarely a one and done event. Operators make huge investments in drilling, completion, and surface facility costs. Achieving the highest NRI of their leases is a massive factor in their economics, so they work hard for lower royalty and higher bonus terms. A typical 1280 ac unit in your area could easily have a development cost of $75M and a lease bonus cost of less than $2M. So do not be fooled when they say they cannot afford a higher bonus in a horizontal development. With that said, higher royalty is always best if they drill. Good luck.

Date: 2025-06-12T14:40:43Z
Content: Thank you.  We did negotiate 21% which I thought was pretty good.  Permits are approved and we are bombarded with offers to buy. We definitely aren’t selling.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-12T14:05:19Z
Content: A few quick thoughts. The limited warranty should be a “by, through, and under, but no further” provision. The landman will know what you mean by this provision. I either strike the warranty or offer this option. You will need some help in developing an acceptable “no cost” royalty provision. You may want to try the NARO website for thoughts in this area. The pooling of the lease allows for more effective development by the inclusion of your property in a larger unit, so this is a positive for economic development.

It must be true because my brother inherited a portion too and he has been leasing his land to an oil company and receiving payments. The oil company reached out to me right as the pandemic was hitting and our lives turned upside down and I never followed up. A rep from the oil company sent me a lease, which I never signed. I know that they found oil on the land. What am I entitled to and how would I claim that at this point? I have no idea where to start. I don’t think this is super lucrative based on the small amounts that my brother has mentioned, but it is really hard getting people to discuss money, rights, etc., so I feel lost with this endeavor.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-10T16:35:54Z
Content: Start with the basics. Ask your brother for a copy of the Division Order and Lease he signed. This will provide your with initial information so you can contact the company that sends royalty checks to your brother. If you are an unleased mineral owner (UMO), then you may be in suspense or be in a before payout status. This is a starting point. Come back to the forum when you have more information.

Date: 2025-06-10T22:13:06Z
Content: Thank you for taking the time to help me! I will start by asking my brother. He is not physically well (over 30 surgeries since he nearly died when his pancreas burst) and has so many medical needs and related papers that I’m not sure that he will know where his forms are, but it is worth a try!

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-12T01:56:10Z
Content: If you cannot get the information I suggested, ask him for the detail statement for his latest check. That will provide you with contact information for the company as well as the property numbers and well names. You might also post the county and State for the property so forum members can provide you with ideas on how you can research additional information.

rag_documents.title: Quiet title for minerals
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Quiet title for minerals

Author: Duker
Date: 2025-06-09T13:11:11Z
Content: Quiet title (case#) CV-2024-237 striped the majority of owners interest without
appealing original probate (case#) PB-2019-48> Doesn’t seem legal to me. Anyone out there had this done to them?

Author: Duker
Date: 2025-06-10T13:03:31Z
Content: It is mineral interest we inherited from a relative in 2020.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-06-10T14:34:59Z
Content: Quiet title actions are used to determine legal ownership of real property among claimants of title.  All claimants have the opportunity to prove title through various records.  Probate does not prove title to real property.  Probate establishes who inherits whatever real property interest the decedent owned.  For example, John buys land from Mary and assumes he got both surface and minerals.  John dies and under his probate and will, his land goes to Peter.  Later it is established that Mary only owned surface.  Therefore, John did not get any minerals and so Peter owns no minerals.  Similarly, if John bought minerals from Maxine (who claimed 100%) without tracing title, John would only receive whatever minerals Maxine owned.  If Maxine owned only 1/50th minerals, then that is all John got.  Again, Peter will only inherit the minerals actually owned by John.  All of the claimants should have had the opportunity to prove title based on the deed records in the quiet title action.  From your post, it would seem that some claimant(s) proved that most of the minerals were sold many years ago and that portion belongs to them.

Author: mineralsjb2009
Date: 2025-06-10T15:35:56Z
Content: Did you answer the complaint with the probate? If you didn’t protest after receiving notice then….

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-10T15:53:58Z
Content: Probate can only transfer actual ownership and not the stated ownership in the probate. A QTA allows for a response period for parties in order to defend their interest.@TennisDazegives you a great example.

Author: Duker
Date: 2025-06-11T16:40:02Z
Content: I was never notified. Found out from another owner.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-11T16:56:09Z
Content: Notice may have been made to claims of record. As such, the notice may have been made to the Estate and not the individual devisees. Notice may also be made by publication.

Author: 4theRightChild
Date: 2025-06-02T21:45:16Z
Content: (for adding a depth clause) - Any suggestions as what might be a proper depth to request on an O&G lease? 5 year term on a 63 net acre space.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-05T14:19:59Z
Content: You are probably thinking about a hard depth number which is not how they are usually worded.  They are usually worded regarding a certain number of feet below a depth drilled (not good) or perforated and producing (better).  Since the lease is a legal document, you should contact an attorney to help with the correct wording.  The forum cannot give legal advice.

rag_documents.title: New mineral right deed has big error
rag_documents.content:
Topic: New mineral right deed has big error

Author: Joanie
Date: 2025-05-08T13:21:47Z
Content: I am the administrator of my deceased husband’s estate. He had inherited a portion of mineral rights from his mother. He never received his deed of ownership. Neither have I. Until I do, I cannot finish probating his estate properly. I cannot document the distribution of his mineral rights to his beneficiaries. Recently, I was informed by the executor of the mother’s estate that my husband’s mineral rights were finally transferred into his name. I obtained a copy of the “mineral rights distribution deed” and his name does not appear on it. Furthermore, another name appears on the deed that doesn’t belong there. When I contacted the executor to ask her to correct it, she told me that it was just a mistake and I should call an attorney to get it fixed. Correct me if I am wrong but isn’t this part of her job as executor, her fiduciary duties? She claims it is not her responsibility to have the deed corrected. As I understand it, only she has the legal right to alter that deed. Certainly I don’t. I tried to explain this to her and got nowhere. Now what do I do? She outright refuses to cooperate in getting this deed corrected. Consequently, she has turned a simple task into a monster challenge for me to deal with. The is not an issue of ownership. She knows full well that my husband owns the mineral rights. It’s simply an issue of a faulty deed that needs to be corrected. Initially, she had hired an attorney to draw up the deed and have it processed. Now, all she needs to do is call him and have him correct it, but she won’t do it. This executor is also one of the beneficiaries who appears on the deed. She is my deceased husband’s sister. This is all very frustrating and I don’t know what steps to take to get the situation resolved. Any input would be appreciated greatly.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-05-08T13:45:36Z
Content: Run to an attorney.  As described the tile is another person’s name and he could sell.  This is very serious.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-05-08T21:50:22Z
Content: As TennisDaze and others know, I rarely suggest hiring an attorney even though I am one, but you need to hire an experienced oil and gas attorney this week especially if the property is generating income. If I wasnt out of town Id draft a statement of claim for you, to atleast clout title for awhile for you to file tmw as family members screwing eachother makes my blood boil.

Author: Joanie
Date: 2025-05-09T11:17:33Z
Content: Thank you so very much, TennisDaze and Bob77. Your support to move forward on this, quickly, is invaluable. I have reached out to two attorneys in ND, one by email and one by phone. I received brief responses from both, (one, a paralegal) promising to look into it. I am hoping I will hear back, and within a reasonable amount of time. A few weeks ago I thought I had secured someone to help me, but after a few conversations and giving him a lot of information, he never bothered to contact me again. I also contacted the attorney hired by the executor. After a few words, he babbled something about conflict of interest and hung up on me. I don’t know what that was about! He didn’t seem to realize that he was actually representing me as well, albeit indirectly. Then I wrote to him, twice, in exacting detail describing the incorrectness of the deed and it’s potential ramifications. No response. Ugh…so much time and energy wasted.  Frustrated and feeling alienated down here in Florida. Thanks for letting me vent.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-05-24T19:28:09Z
Content: You may need to get an attorney or law firm that is not in your immediate area. What you described happens a lot of times, especially in small towns. There are always someone that is like that executor.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-05-25T13:48:07Z
Content: Sorry for your problems. You are not correct that the Estate attorney works for you even indirectly. He does have a conflict. You were correct to advise him of the error. He has a duty to research that error and report to the Executor. Since these parties do not want to address the issue, you should follow the advice of@Bob77and@TennisDazein order to protect your interest and minimize damages. This action will not be free of cost to you.

Author: sclausen
Date: 2025-05-26T20:49:38Z
Content: Your problem is not a look into it problem.  Assuming you have located a firm near or in the county in which the estate is being administered, you want to hire that attorney or firm, which means an engagement letter and paying a retainer. That attorney or firm should be provided with a copy of the deed, your correspondence, and the correspondence you have received.  Your legal counsel likely will send a letter demanding that a correction deed be issued and may demand your attorneys’ fees be reimbursed–keep in mind Executor has breached fiduciary duty for failure to correct and if attorney has drafted an incorrect deed, attorney has made an error aand likely committed malpractice, especially if refusing to correct.  Once dust settles you will receive new division orders and can inquire if producer has made payments based on wrong deed and, if so, demand damages from executor.

Author: user41
Date: 2025-06-10T07:56:53Z
Content: Be careful about ending up with assigned taxable value.  A lot of times you don’t want a negative working interest there can be expenses

Content: Net Mineral Acre. Most interests in minerals are undivided amongst family members. The net mineral acre would constitute a single person’s interest if it were divided.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-09T18:28:12Z
Content: Net Mineral Acre: example.  Grandpa had 40 gross acres.  When he died, he left his acreage to his four children at 25% each undivided. If the deed or probate said “divided”, then is usually for a very specific geographic location such as the homestead cabin and the garden.  Those are pretty rare.

Topic: Inherited Mineral Rights with offer to purchase

Author: mthom
Date: 2025-04-03T23:45:11Z
Content: It was found that I have inherited mineral rights and received an offer to purchase.  I have no idea what minerals there might be, nor if leasing is a viable option given it is less than 2 acres.  Can anyone provide guidance of where I should start?  The offer is for $3,000/acre which I read on the forum from 2024 is low.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-04T00:42:18Z
Content: You would need to give a location with the township name.  Most offers to buy come right before drilling, so don’t be too quick to jump until you know what you have and why they are offering.

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-04-04T12:09:11Z
Content: @mthomto build on what@M_Barnesis saying, location is VERY important.  Also, have you signed a lease?  If not, you want to negotiate a better sales price as unleased minerals are more valuable

Author: WVGAS
Date: 2025-06-08T21:01:31Z
Content: My brother and I have a 15 acre tract in the Battelle District in Monongalia that is of interest to an energy and a couple mineral purchasing outfits…is there a lot of activity there?  Are folks getting 5K or 6K leasing or purchase offers?

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-06-09T01:31:58Z
Content: It all depends. In Monongalia County, you’re going to be hard-pressed to get 5k or 6K as a lease bonus, unless you sign a really crappy lease.  And that’s something that people often forget, you can get a higher bonus with a worse lease, and your bonus will go down if you want a good lease.  It’s about understanding what your goals are.

Author: Nancy_Mosley
Date: 2025-06-09T01:32:39Z
Content: There are frequently permits for new drills (wells) in that district of Monongalia. CNX (Consol) seems to be the main company. I don’t know about lease offers. Hope somebody has more information.

Author: Khaled_Helmi
Date: 2025-06-09T01:50:06Z
Content: Northeast is also very much active in Monongalia county - probably more so than CNX.  Definitely very active in Battelle as we have a number of leases with them in that district

rag_documents.title: Advice on Oil & Gas Lease

Topic: Advice on Oil & Gas Lease

Author: Robert_Eggebrecht
Date: 2025-05-08T13:26:23Z
Content: Not being up to date on current mineral leasing in Williams Co. I do not know current lease amounts.  I believe that what you were offered is a little low.   Hopefully someone with more current knowledge can help you.

Author: Well_Wisher
Date: 2025-05-08T13:50:36Z
Content: I would leave out the “any other product” and require it be oil and gas only!  I would also request 20% and a higher bonus.  As I have read previously, if these acres are in different sections, do a separate lease for each section and try to stick to three years.  I’m not really up on bonus amounts but saw someone had reported getting $1750 in ND recently.   They can only say no.   But I would definitely not let them “lease” any other product. That should be separate and specific,  In North Dakota mineral interests refer to ownership of “oil, gas, coal, clay, gravel, uranium, and all othermineralsof any kind and nature.”

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-05-08T20:16:53Z
Content: Have a ND attorney with oil and gas experience review the proposed lease.  I don’t understand the phrase “18% royalty across 5 people”.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-05-08T21:01:23Z
Content: Make sure you get a depth clause.  Im not sure what you mean by “any other product” for the increased interest of rare earth minerals under the current administration".  If you are referring to Lithium, its been going on for awhile and courts are still trying fo figure out if the surface owner or mineral owner owns the rights.  To make you sleep better at night, simply ask them to strike the any other clause and make it oil and gas only.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-09T13:13:44Z
Content: Each heir should have their own lease unless language in the title documents indicates otherwise.  You would have your share of the net acres.  If in different sections, then each section needs its own lease.

Author: Evan_Thomas
Date: 2025-05-09T14:28:35Z
Content: Williams is very hot right now. I’ve seen better terms out there. At the level you’re working at, it would be very worthwhile to hire a lawyer. Mine redlined several items out of what I considered to be a favorable lease.

Content: 5, 6-159N-103W
Current activity has KODA Resources leasing.  No old wells showing up.  KODA has horizontal permits for three section wells in 160N-103W just to the north of you.

Author: Steve_Hunt
Date: 2025-05-13T15:35:26Z
Content: Hello 4th…
We have mineral interest in Oklahoma so I have no knowledge of the situation in ND. But in our experience, the first offer and even beyond tend to be lowball and you should not be timid about entering into a negotiation. I have doubled and in one case tripled the initial offer. I think your percentage 18% correlates to a 3/16 royalty. I just closed a lease on one parcel by negotiating a lower lease bonus and a better percentage (20% or 1/5). This forum is a great place to become more knowledgeable about how all this works. One more thing. If you and your other family members can negotiate as a bloc, you will have more leverage, even if you each sign an individual lease for your respective interests. I wish you the best.

Author: NodakColorado
Date: 2025-05-14T11:29:02Z
Content: There is not much activity in that area compared to other areas in Williams County.  You may be able to get slightly better bonus amounts and royalty, but it won’t sky rocket until they start drilling.  Because you are apparent heirs, you may have to file probate in ND, which can cost 2k-4k.  Companies will be able to lease you without probate, but you won’t get paid on your royalty until there is probate in the state of ND.  Sometimes independent landmen and land companies will help with the probate process, operators will not.

Content: A prudent operator will have a title opinion conducted to pay out on their new wells. I know Lynx Oil Company is leasing in North Dakota and they are willing to pay for the probate.  Might be worth reaching out to them.

Author: avs201
Date: 2025-04-21T18:56:20Z
Content: Wife died  in 2023 and receives cks from oil company, they tell me it is in the elk city unit1, but they cannot give me legal discerption soi  can get deed swop over to her children ,  have contacted Beckham county clear office and they cant pinpoint  deed with out legal  discerption  beside elk city unit 1- tried contacting a couple lawyers in okla with no response . any help or direction would be appreciated

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-21T19:20:11Z
Content: The reason the courthouse cannot tell you is that there are many wells that start with “Elk City” and they cannot help with legal work on deeds, just can help with filing them at the county courthouse.    Who is the operator on the checks?  Have you contacted them?  They will have the location.  Have you tried looking up her name onwww.okcountyrecords.com?

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-04-21T21:51:54Z
Content: You should also include your wife’s maiden name and/or parents’ names during your search.  Also, the checks should have a county description.  These will often also provide the Section Township Range.

Author: SeanCapo
Date: 2025-05-21T19:10:31Z
Content: You may be able to pull a legal description off the mineral tax rolls using her name on the Beckham County Assessor Office website.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-05-21T23:45:13Z
Content: Oklahoma doesn’t tax minerals and doesn’t have a mineral tax roll.

Author: SeanCapo
Date: 2025-05-22T00:13:51Z
Content: Not quite, while the counties dont assess an ad valorem tax like Texas, the state does collect a severence tax on gross production. The county assessor will maintain ownership records, legal descriptions, and transactions. Apologies if I was less than clear.

rag_documents.title: Mineral ownership
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Mineral ownership

Author: mbf22
Date: 2025-05-27T17:21:14Z
Content: I purchased property in Adams County Colorado with the mineral and water rights. Eventually split it into 2 lots, both sold several years later. I leased minerals for several years on both properties.  I was doing some research and found that the owner of the south lot sold the mineral interest which were not conveyed. One attorney I spoke to replied ’ just because he sold them doesn’t mean he owns them.’  I have no idea where to start and without a lot of recources. I would like to sell if they are indeed mine. Any ideas out there on how to proceed? The original deed showing ownership of the minerals was never recorded. Thank you

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-02T13:33:50Z
Content: Not giving legal advice, but in general, if you did not specifically retain the mineral rights reserved when you sold the lots, you may have sold them in the sale.  You may have leased them after the sale, but that may have been sloppy leasing work without the lessee running title.  You need an attorney to work out the details.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-03T16:30:05Z
Content: You have several issues. By the tone of your post, you will need to get a professional involved to perform a title search in order to confirm your ownership. I would start with a landman for the initial evaluation. Balance your need to know with the expected value of the property.

Author: MistyRose
Date: 2025-06-07T14:09:45Z
Content: Well we got a lawyer. The lawyer, the court house people all say we own the mineral rites but the oil company is still saying they have to do a quiet title search. Is this normal for property that has been owned since 1919?

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-07T15:47:10Z
Content: Courthouse employees are generally forbidden by law to offer opinion as to ownership. Your attorney should be able to address the issues related to a quiet title action rather than offering the opinion that you own the property.

rag_documents.title: New oil well producing with no Divsion Orders
rag_documents.content:
Topic: New oil well producing with no Divsion Orders

Author: Jamesri94
Date: 2025-06-07T14:08:51Z
Content: I have a lease in Dawson County and a new Lateral was drilled with 1/3 acres of the lease
allocated. The well started producing and oil sold in December 2024 per the State Comptrollers report. I have been trying to get a Division order and payment since the law states payment must be made in 120 days and 60 days thereafter and still do not have the correct DO.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-07T14:51:36Z
Content: Send a certified letter return receipt to the Division Order department of the operator demanding payment with statutory interest and that usually gets their attention.  Give your name, address, description of acreage and the well name.  Sometimes that moves you up on their “to do” list.  It also starts a mandatory clock in Texas.  Keep a copy of everything that you send.

Topic: New Offer to Purchase Mineral Rights

Author: Carl_Alexander
Date: 2025-05-05T16:02:23Z
Content: Just received an offer to purchase mineral rights in Eddy in two locations:  Township 18S Range 26e Section 24 and Township 18S Range 27E Section 19.  The offers came from Dorado Petroleum.  I am not sure who they are.Their offer is $2,000 NMA (subject to 1/4 royalty interest).  What does anyone know about these two locations, which are pretty much adjacent to each other, and/or Dorado?  There appears to be some producing wells in the area.  Any activity going on there to encourage offers to purchase?

Author: LeeA
Date: 2025-05-06T20:08:24Z
Content: Based on the information in the NMOCD,
There are 8 Proposed Aggie Wells on Section 24, T18S, R26E and 9 proposed Horned Frog wells on Section 19,T18S, R27E Eddy County .
You can go on the NMOCD Well search and give the sec, township,range and county this will give you all wells . If you click on a well when it opens on the right side of the page is a legend scroll down to Action this tells you all current information. Hope this helps Not sure what your mineral interest is but that’s a low-ball number. Last recent offer I received for minerals in Loving was 4700.00 per ma. I have made 5x that in the last 2 months on new wells.

Author: Nan-9
Date: 2025-05-06T22:22:07Z
Content: Can someone give me some information on sec 24 25 &35 in township 21 range 28. Any wells permitted near.
Curious

Author: LeeA
Date: 2025-05-07T00:49:09Z
Content: Okay looking on the NMOCD Well search site,
This is the descriptions I looked up
Sec 24, T21S, T28E Eddy County ,3 wells currently from 2010 still producing and 1 proposed well, last activity 2019.
Sec 25, T21S, T28E Eddy County , 1 well from 2009 still producing today and 4 proposed wells last activity May 2019.
Sec 35,T21S,T28E Eddy County, there are 3 Saltwater Disposal wells dating back from 1978 until 2019.

Author: Nan-9
Date: 2025-05-07T01:22:21Z
Content: Thank you! Question, does a proposed well mean that it is permitted to drill?

Author: LeeA
Date: 2025-05-07T03:46:59Z
Content: From what I read on the documents these wells had APD’s in 2012 and an approved extension in 2014.
If you search NMOCD Well Search you can use the drop down boxes to input your description and this will show you all wells.
To view the wells information and files open up the well link, there is a legend on the right side of the page, go to files and this is your well documents. You can also go to Action and this is all current approvals and actions.

Author: Carl_Alexander
Date: 2025-05-07T16:29:56Z
Content: Okay, did  as you suggested, and I see the proposed wells, and I also see in the same area some plugged wells by a different operator.  Are the new proposed wells different type wells than the plugged ones (different depth, etc.)?  I need some clarity of what I am seeing.  What would these rights be worth, if under active leasse?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-08T13:58:27Z
Content: The older wells in the section are conventional vertical wells.  The new wells are horizontal wells which should give significantly higher returns. (Hence the interest in buying).

Author: LeeA
Date: 2025-05-08T14:22:56Z
Content: I replied to your post via email but not sure if you received it. I attached several screenshots of the well page and quick links on the NMOCD site.
Please let me know if you did not receive my post..

Author: Judy_Nickson
Date: 2025-05-08T14:46:54Z
Content: Sorry, I did not receive your email..checked my spam also. Thanks for trying to help.

Author: LeeA
Date: 2025-05-08T15:06:05Z
Content: Did you open each well link and go to the Quick Links on the right side of screen? Open files and it gives you All the information on the well.
You can also go to the Action Status  and this will give you the most current activity. Plugged well means no longer active.
Proposed wells will have a Spud date if being drilled. I have found many wells drilled in the active link but not updated on the NMOCD Well Page.  This is why I search the files and Action Status.

rag_documents.title: Bonus offer on a 1/4 Royalty
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Bonus offer on a 1/4 Royalty

Author: tbonne
Date: 2025-06-03T19:23:01Z
Content: Hello - I am getting some offers on Sec 5 -3S -1E in Carter Co.  One of the offers is a bonus at a 1/4 royalty which seems very attractive since typically there is no bonus to get a 1/4 RI.  Anyone else getting similar offers or have any other information?

Author: norm1
Date: 2025-06-04T22:24:43Z
Content: I could sure use some baseline lease rates for Carter County.  Some guys have been calling but I don’t wanna do anything ‘flying blind’.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-06-05T09:56:07Z
Content: You can always wait for a pooling. Since they are offering a 1/4 royalty you should at least receive that. A pooling may provide some bonus money also. At pooling you can shop your minerals for better OGL terms to companies interested in participating in the drilling.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-05T14:15:57Z
Content: The bonus amounts will be tied to the reservoir location, so you need to be more specific about a township, range and section. Bonus amounts are not public.  The closest you can get are pooling orders within the last year in the eight contiguous sections.

Author: tbonne
Date: 2025-06-05T15:01:20Z
Content: Thanks all for the info.  The offer I received was $1000 / acre for 1/4 royalty.  I am waiting to receive their sample lease.  So if I wait and go to pooling, how do I make my election and attempt to receive the best terms under a 1/4 royalty?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-05T16:12:48Z
Content: 0_The Pooling Process in Oklahoma.pdf(340.4 KB)
If you go to pooling, you will get an order that gives several bonus/royalty pairs.  You must select your option within 20 calendar days and send back (preferably by certified mail return receipt) on time or you will be assigned the lowest royalty option.

Author: tbonne
Date: 2025-06-06T01:58:46Z
Content: Thanks for the very helpful info.  So I did receive a copy of the lease and right off the bat I am having a problem with …
“In consideration of the premises the said Lessee covenants and agrees: to deliver to the credit of Lessor, in the pipeline to which it may connect its wells, the 1/4 part of all oil … less a proportionate deduction for any transportation or other fees or taxes charged to the Lessee; to pay Lessor for gas (including casing head gas and coal bed methane gas) of whatsoever nature or kind (with all of its constituents) produced and sold, or used off the leased premises, or used in the manufacture of products therefrom, 1/4 of the gross proceeds received from any party (whether or not an affiliate of Lessee) for the gas sold, used off the premises, or in the manufacture of products therefrom, less a proportionate part, of any production, severance and other excise taxes and costs and/or fees incurred by Lessee in making marketable Lessor’s share of gas, and/or in gathering, transporting, processing, compressing or otherwise marketing Lessor’s share of gas, but in no event more than 1/4 of the net amount received by the Lessee from any such party.”

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-06-06T13:12:31Z
Content: A good oil & gas attorney will be able to help you with the proper wording for no post production costs.  There are some other clauses that you need to watch out for to strike or amend and some that need to be added to further protect you.  You can read examples of leases on www.okcountyrecords.com-some are good and some not so much.

posts.content: Thanks all for the info.  The offer I received was $1000 / acre for 1/4 royalty.  I am waiting to receive their sample lease.  So if I wait and go to pooling, how do I make my election and attempt to receive the best terms under a 1/4 royalty?

posts.author: M_Barnes
posts.content:
0_The Pooling Process in Oklahoma.pdf(340.4 KB)
If you go to pooling, you will get an order that gives several bonus/royalty pairs.  You must select your option within 20 calendar days and send back (preferably by certified mail return receipt) on time or you will be assigned the lowest royalty option.

“In consideration of the premises the said Lessee covenants and agrees: to deliver to the credit of Lessor, in the pipeline to which it may connect its wells, the 1/4 part of all oil … less a proportionate deduction for any transportation or other fees or taxes charged to the Lessee; to pay Lessor for gas (including casing head gas and coal bed methane gas) of whatsoever nature or kind (with all of its constituents) produced and sold, or used off the leased premises, or used in the manufacture of products therefrom, 1/4 of the gross proceeds received from any party (whether or not an affiliate of Lessee) for the gas sold, used off the premises, or in the manufacture of products therefrom, less a proportionate part, of any production, severance and other excise taxes and costs and/or fees incurred by Lessee in making marketable Lessor’s share of gas, and/or in gathering, transporting, processing, compressing or otherwise marketing Lessor’s share of gas, but in no event more than 1/4 of the net amount received by the Lessee from any such party.”
