rag_documents.content:
Topic: Selling Mineral Rights

Author: carlsbad3269
Date: 2025-05-02T15:03:56Z
Content: Hello!  What is the process of transferring ownership once a contract has been signed?  Does the purchasing party have the responsibility of notifying the county and producer?  What if we are still receiving production checks?  Thanks for your time.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-05-02T15:20:22Z
Content: This is a general answer. The purchaser has the obligation of notice. Depending on the effective date of transfer, you may still receive checks for a limited time. If you are receiving checks for production after the effective date, then you should notify the purchaser since the funds are not legally yours and would be subject to recovery.

Author: chandlerwall
Date: 2025-05-05T15:16:46Z
Content: I agree with James on this. It’s the obligation of the buyer to notify the operator. Any checks you receive belong to the buyer if the production date is after the sale date.

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-04-03T11:41:33Z
Content: I have received an offer to lease Section 9-139N-98W in Stark County ND.  The leasing company is Murfin Drilling, Inc.  Need advise on 2 things.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-04-03T19:25:36Z
Content: You may want to reach our to@M_Barnessince ND may have some notice issues relating to OGL offers. Murfin has been around for quite some time.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-03T19:57:21Z
Content: Most savvy mineral owners would want the second option at 1/6th, but ask for 3/16ths and see what they say.

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-04-03T22:36:09Z
Content: Do you think the $100/mineral acre is a good value?  And Thank You

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-04-04T21:42:05Z
Content: They are also requesting a 5 year lease.  I’ve read that its best to only do 3.  Do you have any input?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-04T22:12:33Z
Content: Personally, I always ask for more money and a shorter time frame.  So $150 at 1/6th or $100 at 3/16ths and three years.  They may not agree, but you don’t know until you ask.

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-04-13T11:14:58Z
Content: I’ve managed to completely confuse myself.  Can you explain why the $200/mineral acre with 1/8th bonus is not higher.  It appears to me to have an initial larger payout.  I had it mapped in my head and realized the $150 at 1/6 comes out the same in the royalty bonus as the $200 at 1/8th.  What am I missing

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-13T12:24:37Z
Content: I think longer term.  The 1/8th and $200 bonus is a one time payment for the three year or five years.  If I have a productive well or multiple wells, then I would rather have many years of payout at 1/6th instead of 1/8th since 1/6th (0.16666667) is larger than 1/8th (0.125).  The bonus payment is very small compared to lifetime payout especially with multiple wells.  The risk is that they never drill, then the 1/8th is better for a one time payout.

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-04-13T17:19:41Z
Content: Thank you so much for the clarification.  I’m back on track.  At the end of the day it is, indeed, all a risk but I need to look long term.

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-04-18T14:42:56Z
Content: So the landman has become very snarky.  He has offered another section with what I suggested at 150/mineral acre with 1/6th royalty.  I asked for a 3 year lease with option to do 2 additional with anther bonus.  He has agreed to 150 for all sections at 1/6th but 5 year lease.  I need guidance moving forward.  Im not opposed to 5 yr lease but feel I should have the option for bonus payout…am I wrong?  Murfin is new to ND market and has some new lease in Dunn county

Author: Rick_Tatum
Date: 2025-04-18T19:14:18Z
Content: I think you are right. 3yr with option. They may not be the only ones interested. So don’t be afraid to push a little.

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-04-21T04:23:02Z
Content: Thank You.  So far we have no other offers and I know Murfin is new to ND.  I think I need to hold firm but have fear of missing out…(FOMO).   I guess if I stand my ground it may be only then they counter.

Author: Towlcm
Date: 2025-05-04T15:44:29Z
Content: Is there somewhere I can look to find out how many mineral acres I have in Stark County, Section 4-139N-98W?  Thank You

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-05T12:08:21Z
Content: You would need to either find a deed or probate and hope that the acres would be listed on it.  If you have producing acres, then you can ask the Division Order analyst for the operator.

rag_documents.title: Finding Tyler County Land Description
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Finding Tyler County Land Description

Author: UncleJed
Date: 2025-05-01T01:45:09Z
Content: We recently found out that we have rights in Tyler County, but they’re asking for the description which we don’t have. What is the best way to find the description?

Author: Nancy_Mosley
Date: 2025-05-01T14:33:43Z
Content: How did you find that you have rights? Who told you? If it is a landman, he might have more information. There is a long complicated way to work this out but you would need to know your family history back a few generations.

Author: Ryan_Fairbanks
Date: 2025-05-01T17:27:48Z
Content: The best way would depend on what information you do have. I’d start with a Grantee search for any family members names associated with it. A Grantor search might also provide any leases or other conveyances that those family members have done.

Author: Nancy_Mosley
Date: 2025-05-01T19:22:42Z
Content: Good idea, but the poster needs to know, for example, which side of the family might have been the original owner. And remember Land Grants which might be the original source. If the minerals have been severed, as this sounds like, the deed severing them is very important. The Land Books could be helpful too. (Tyler has them online unlike some counties). And remember the poster might not know how to find the Tyler County documents website. This, as I said, is complicated. But possible!

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-05-05T02:03:11Z
Content: Tyler County WV’s land records are online.
YOu may have to sign up for the service. I don’t remember whether I did initially or not.IDX Search Tyler County

Author: Nancy_Mosley
Date: 2025-05-05T03:33:47Z
Content: I believe the online site which you kindly provided the link to only has a regular index search going back to around 1997 or 1998 except for a few things like births and marriages. For earlier records, you need to go to the Vault indexes. Scroll through the left hand side drop down menu to “Grantor Index to Deeds” or “Grantee Index to Deeds”. Grantor is the one giving something to the other party  (the seller or leasor). Grantee is the one receiving (the buyer or lessee). From the Middle drop-down, select the first letter of the name you are searching. The “S” entries are at the bottom, divided into 2 sections. Then go to the right hand drop down. Some letters have several pages at the beginning, starting with 0 then 0-001 etc. The last one is corporate entries. If you see a separate listing for a particular name, go the the number listed for that name and start searching. The left hand column is the date the deed is recorded. The next column is the last name. The next 3 are for first names, divided by parts of the alphabet.The next is Grantees (for the Grantor index, reversed for the Grantee index). Then are columns for the book number, page number where the document starts, then the type of document, then a description.If the name being searched does not have its separate set of pages, you find a page for a range of names for parts of the alphabet. Once you find something that might work (might be an ancestor for example) then go to the Image Search back on the main page. Select the type of book (Deed includes oil and gas leases), the book and page you found in the index listing. Then look at your document. There is some more to this but this is the basic set of information needed to start searching. There might not be a deed to your ancestor, if he came to Tyler county early enough. posts.author: Nancy_Mosley
posts.content: I believe the online site which you kindly provided the link to only has a regular index search going back to around 1997 or 1998 except for a few things like births and marriages. For earlier records, you need to go to the Vault indexes. Scroll through the left hand side drop down menu to “Grantor Index to Deeds” or “Grantee Index to Deeds”. Grantor is the one giving something to the other party  (the seller or leasor). Grantee is the one receiving (the buyer or lessee). From the Middle drop-down, select the first letter of the name you are searching. The “S” entries are at the bottom, divided into 2 sections. Then go to the right hand drop down. Some letters have several pages at the beginning, starting with 0 then 0-001 etc. The last one is corporate entries. If you see a separate listing for a particular name, go the the number listed for that name and start searching. The left hand column is the date the deed is recorded. The next column is the last name. The next 3 are for first names, divided by parts of the alphabet.The next is Grantees (for the Grantor index, reversed for the Grantee index). Then are columns for the book number, page number where the document starts, then the type of document, then a description.If the name being searched does not have its separate set of pages, you find a page for a range of names for parts of the alphabet. Once you find something that might work (might be an ancestor for example) then go to the Image Search back on the main page. Select the type of book (Deed includes oil and gas leases), the book and page you found in the index listing. Then look at your document. There is some more to this but this is the basic set of information needed to start searching. There might not be a deed to your ancestor, if he came to Tyler county early enough. Author: Meier488
Date: 2025-04-23T10:36:43Z
Content: I had a lease in Lea County a few years ago and it was very similar. (3 years with $200 bonus per acre) so it sounds good to me.
Do you mind if I ask what company? I’m curious to know if the original company our lease was with is still in the area.
We have rights on lots that comprise over 300 acres in Lea county but our previous lease was for a quite small area.

Author: pollytabeling
Date: 2025-04-23T13:19:23Z
Content: The lease was offered by Matador (MRC Permian Company.)  Should I get a 25% royalty rate?  Should I only accept a 3 or 6 year term?

Author: Terrel_Shields
Date: 2025-04-23T14:36:17Z
Content: 3 year with NO OPTION TO EXTEND. 25% is a very good royalty in most cases. I want them to drill or get out. The bonus money is not always very important but should be about one-third the price of buying the actual mineral right. And beware of anyone offering “bank drafts” for payment.

Author: Meier488
Date: 2025-04-23T14:37:44Z
Content: Though our lease started in 2015, it was 25%, 3 years with an option at the end for 2 more years (which it did) and $200 bonus. We were told by a friend in the industry who looked over the terms at the time that this was customary and a good contract. So yours seems to be good.i can’t find anything to say that terms have changed drastically since then.
You may want to check with someone in the industry specifically concerning Lea County right now since it is hugely productive right now.  I’ve also been trying to do some research for more updated information, and am hoping to get another lease on ours.

Author: Ollie
Date: 2025-04-24T01:48:26Z
Content: It is my understanding that Matador (if it’s them) is the only legitimate driller in that area.  There are other companies trying to flip leases, but I rather deal with the actual driller.  In that section 10, there are no wells in that section or any section around it, so I don’t know if it’s any good or not.  It’s my understanding this is a wildcat area.
Be careful with people telling you to only lease for 1/4 or no option or any of that…easy to say when they’re not the one getting the offer or they haven’t signed anything in your area.  Regardless of what people think, not every single permian area is worthy of 1/4 royalty, especially in an area that has not yet been proven.  I don’t want to be force pooled either.  Try to hit them up for more money or royalty, and if they are steadfast, then make your own decision not based on what other people think about an area they have no idea about.  Personally I take the deal especially if nobody else is contacting me.  They can pull out at any time and then you have Zero offer.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-24T18:33:10Z
Content: [quote=“pollytabeling, post:1, topic:81005”]
1-Personally, I will not do an option to extend.  Three years is long enough.  An additional three years puts control all in their hands and I would rather have a choice at that point.

Content: Ollie, do you cross out any pooling wording in leases you receive?

Topic: Mewbourne letter question

Author: oneida_valentine
Date: 2025-04-30T14:56:07Z
Content: Mewbourne sent a letter that offers $600.00 per acre for a lease/assignment covering all of your right, title and interest in said unit, delivering an 81.25% net revenue interest; or no cash for a lease/assignment delivering 75% net revenue interest.  Proposed well-Ambassador Inn “19/31” DM#1H.  "If you wish to participate in the drilling of the proposed well by paying your proportionate share of costs, please sign…"We are not understanding what this letter is about.  Can someone explain?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-01T16:03:34Z
Content: This is a common notification letter.  I do not sign the letter as only a signed lease or a force pooling is the actual agreement. Why waste a stamp.  It usually means that leasing is happening and a pooling case is about to be filed.  They are offering a 3/1ths option (18.75% to you and 81.25% to them) or a no cash and 1/4 lease (25% to you and 75%) to them.  Participating is not for the novice.  Many of us would take the higher royalty and no cash bonus as the higher royalty payout on one or more wells is usually far higher over decades of production versus a one time lease bonus payment.

Author: oneida_valentine
Date: 2025-05-01T16:47:06Z
Content: Thank you for your response.

Custer County, Oklahoma

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-01T16:54:40Z
Content: Mewbourne and others are drilling horizontal wells into the Cherokee and Redfork in that area.

Topic: Unit Title Discrepancy

Author: CameronBussell
Date: 2025-04-07T03:57:02Z
Content: Hello, I have .00892800 Working interest, .00781200 NRI, and a .00260400 ORRI interests of all wells within a lease in Sec 13 1S 4W of Stephens county Oklahoma covering about 130 acres. Most of the active wells were pooled into a unit in the late 70s / early 80s called the WILDHORSE UNIT. During my transfer I have found that one of my operators, who controls  most of this unit, have been paying my predecessor on wells in Secs 11, 12, and 24. These sections all contain wells from this unit. However, during my title search there is no proof of any interests in these sections at all. Furthermore, This operator has producing wells in my lease, but is not paying on them. Has anyone ever experienced this? Is this a normal occurrence with a Unit? Also there are other operators that have producing wells that I am not currently getting any royalties from. How do I approach this and what would be the smartest way to handle this. As always thank y’all for your expertise.

Author: B_Elam
Date: 2025-04-08T02:01:54Z
Content: What is the difference between these three types of interest?

Author: CameronBussell
Date: 2025-04-09T05:02:32Z
Content: This is a great question. I had posted this in a previous thread and I didn’t get a straight answer. I am pretty much finished with the title search. The next step will be handing all of this info to my estate attorney. There is also an oil & gas division of this firm, so I’m sure they will be able to figure it out and explain. As of right now these are the numbers that I have been able to collect from the deeds and operators.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-04-10T01:05:17Z
Content: The Wildhorse Unit appears to be a large waterflood. As to your predecessor  receiving royalties in adjoining sections, I suspect the Division Order or check listed all the sections in question under the unitization order. Therefore, your predecessor was receiving revenue from any well from any land that was included in the very large unit.

Author: CameronBussell
Date: 2025-04-10T21:06:54Z
Content: Tim, thanks for responding. So, if I’m understanding correctly, When wells are unitized you will receive a portion of all producing wells in that unit? I have tried to research this but have come up empty handed. It just seems weird to me that I would be getting paid on production from other sections, while I’m receiving nothing from the wells that are within the lands in the original lease.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-25T13:10:43Z
Content: Working interest-The interest in a property entitling the holder to production royalties and responsibility of costs-

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-04-26T01:32:10Z
Content: Think of the unit as one large golf hole, with fairway, tee and green. Your ownership may be in the section that is the green, but any well drilled on any part of the first hole, including the tee box and fairway would come to you as well.

Author: B_Elam
Date: 2025-04-26T05:39:30Z
Content: Thanks for explaining the differences. I always appreciate your insight.

Content: This may help.  I am attaching the unitization plan for the WILDHORSE unit.   Using Tim’s excellent example of a golf course, here is the “outline” of the course with all of the holes at the time of the unitization.

Author: CameronBussell
Date: 2025-04-29T10:52:54Z
Content: Thank you both for your responses. I agree, great analogy! Are there any books or other study materials that you would recommend so that I can learn more about this subject?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-05-01T15:56:31Z
Content: If you are new to oil and gas, the Mineral Help tab above is a good primer.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-04-02T15:00:38Z
Content: Keep in mind that there are very short time limits to make a pooling order election.  Best practice is to file your election with the OCC and land records.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-02T17:31:23Z
Content: You have 20 calendar days from the date of the order to file your election. If you do not make the cutoff, they will assign the lowest royalty option. I always send by certified mail return receipt for proof of mailing and receipt.

Topic: Change of Operator

Author: TDL
Date: 2025-04-24T10:03:49Z
Content: I inherited a royalty interest in mineral rights in Crockett County, TX a few years ago. Apparently in December 2024 the operator, Epic Permian, was replaced by Scout Energy Partners out of Dallas. When I contacted them, they said they were having a hard time locating my account. After I sent them my documentation, they keep telling me that accounting is working as hard as they can to download all the information and I should be patient. Has anyone else had this experience? I haven’t received a royalty check in several months.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-04-24T17:12:37Z
Content: Even when working with properties where Scout has been the operator for years, they are very slow to respond. Be persistent with follow-up emails on a regular basis. Maintain an email thread for reference.

Author: TDL
Date: 2025-04-25T14:19:37Z
Content: Thanks so much. Yeah, I’ve been emailing them weekly and getting the same response that accounting is working as hard as they can to get all the info downloaded. Will continue to be persistent.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-04-29T18:20:47Z
Content: Send them requests via certified mail, has gotten a faster response in my experience. Make sure and notate that your request falls under the Texas Natural Resources Code for good measure.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-04-30T21:20:50Z
Content: It shouldn’t be this way, but sometimes letters from an attorney gets quicker responses.  If your interest is significant seek out a Texas attorney’s assistance.

Kind of a hateful thing to do as I literally just signed his lease offer with no revisions or demands etc.  Then he ghosted me and wouldn’t return my calls/emails!

posts.author: DPerson
posts.content:
That seems like a HUGE undertaking.
I would find the time to start researching this yourself because it belongs to you. I’m currently doing the same thing from a gas lease back from 2010. It’s not fun but it beats spending time finding someone to invest their time let alone having to pay them out of pocket.

rag_documents.title: Decimal Interest - Mineral and Royalty Deeds?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Decimal Interest - Mineral and Royalty Deeds?

Author: Alejandro_Padua
Date: 2025-04-09T23:34:03Z
Content: Does anyone know if a Texas Mineral or Royalty conveyance Deed can be based upon a Net Decimal Interest in a Well / Unit that is being conveyed?   The transaction involves a portion of a Decimal Interest that Grantor owns.

Author: D_Wells
Date: 2025-04-11T19:50:35Z
Content: I’ve never seen it done that way.  A conveyance of any real estate, including mineral interest, should include a legal description of the land and the whole or the portion of undivided interest being conveyed.  The decimal interest on the revenue statement is the proportion that your net royalty acres in the property represent in the unit.  The legal description could be created so that it would only include the portion of the property included in the unit.  I wouldn’t recommend making a conveyance using the Decimal Interest as the description of what is being conveyed.

Author: SeanCapo
Date: 2025-04-29T16:23:36Z
Content: In my experience, the use of a NRI in the conveyance can be useful to provide notice to the operator of what exactly is being conveyed especially if the Grantor is only conveying their interest in a particular well or unit. It is a good idea to couple the use of a NRI with a legal description and make sure that the granting language reflects what you are conveying, i.e. interest in that particular revenue from that well/unit or the underlying mineral interest or just a royalty interest, etc. Also watch out for catchall language that specifies an NRI but ends with “All interests I own in _____ County”.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-29T16:46:32Z
Content: Documentation of an assignment of a wellbore-only interest vs. a deed for minerals are very different, whether one is assigning all or only a portion of the interest owned.  In either case, assignment of only a portion of the interest conveyed must be carefully worded.  The safest approach is to state the fractional interest being conveyed, such as one-half of seller’s interest, whether in the wellbore or royalty stream or minerals, coupled with a good legal description.  One problem with specifying the exact decimal arises if it is later determined that the seller owned less than he thought.  Such as an NPRI burden which was not accounted for in the original DOI determination or the reinterpretation of earlier deeds.  If the seller warranted title, then he can have real legal or financial mess.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: Mitsui Requests Exploratory Well Permit

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-02-19T18:43:08Z
Content: Mitsui filed a drilling permit request today for an exploratory vertical well to be located 5.5 miles east of Buffalo.  Max depth listed as 30,000 feet.

Author: Zaphod
Date: 2025-02-20T06:00:09Z
Content: That sounds deep to me. Seems to me they’ll get quite a bit of info on the geology. When they drill, do you know if there’s any data they are required to publish & where one could find the data? Or is the only public info the leases they sign? I presume they’ll file for horizontal permits based on what they find, once they have the leases they want?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-02-22T14:12:22Z
Content: The data that they are required to file will most likely be found on the Texas Railroad Commission site. The As-Drilled information will be posted eventually.

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-02-25T03:55:26Z
Content: Rig is on site, spud date today (2/24/2025).  Scandrill 2000 HP rig.  Enverus shows it as a stratigraphic/core test well.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-03-04T20:08:05Z
Content: This a horizontal well to be drilled. The 30,000 ft. is the projected total depth including the horizontal lateral.

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-03-04T20:28:07Z
Content: No, it is a vertical test well permitted to 30,000 feet.  Enverus lists it as a vertical stratigraphic/core test well.

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-04-01T13:57:39Z
Content: Spud date was March 2.  If they actually drill close to the permitted depth of 30,000 feet, it will probably take about four months, so there won’t be any news for a while.

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-04-08T18:49:32Z
Content: Mitsui has amended the permit for this well to horizontal.  Now the 30,000 feet permit makes sense!  Guess their test wells results were good.

Author: nielloeb
Date: 2025-04-08T20:34:10Z
Content: If the bottom hole is in an abstract the company hasn’t leased, what do they do for those owners?

Author: Alan_Herrington
Date: 2025-04-08T21:03:31Z
Content: The E&P company has to have leases for all the tracts crossed by a horizontal wellbore where there are perforations, subject to Texas RRC guidelines.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-08T21:12:38Z
Content: You can see the sections affected by the permit plat.

Date: 2025-04-08T21:58:45Z
Content: The P-16 Form filed with the permit amendment can be found here:

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-04-08T22:04:22Z
Content: The Survey that was done for this unit states that it is not a boundary line survey at the bottom of the plat!

Author: Zaphod
Date: 2025-04-28T01:55:12Z
Content: Got it, at least at my idiot level. Looks like Comstock may have a little competition in this area. BTW, we’ve been getting offers to buy our leased mineral rights from outfits that must be scammers, because I can’t see any way they could make back their money in royalties during the term of the lease. I haven’t talked to any of these folks, but I assume they’re just running a basic “bait & switch”: entice you to talk to them, then try to convince you take a ridiculous low-ball offer. Maybe something even more nefarious? Anyone have any experience with these folks? My guess is they just scan the list of recorded leases & do a mass mailing, hoping they hit someone gullible.

Date: 2025-04-28T21:56:56Z
Content: I have received offers, both lowball and good.  I have spoken with the “good” companies.  They think it will be re-leased because there are a lot of minerals available.

Author: Zaphod
Date: 2025-04-29T10:53:22Z
Content: Do the “good” companies give any idea of how soon they expect to make their money back? They must be expecting a very good rate of return if they’re counting on re-leases to make their profits. Seems to me they’d want at least a 150% return over 6 years. I think they’d want more, because unless they have non-public info, it’s not 100% certain that there will be any returns at all. I guess we shall see.

rag_documents.title: How to find permitted wells in texas
rag_documents.content:
Topic: How to find permitted wells in texas

Author: Archie_Smith
Date: 2025-03-29T21:44:17Z
Content: what are the best sources of information regarding status of permitted wells in texas winkler county

Author: SteveCo
Date: 2025-03-31T14:53:23Z
Content: You could always call the operator’s land department and just ask them for any updates. Sometimes you find someone that is happy to help and keep you informed when you call for updates.

Author: AJ11
Date: 2025-03-31T22:42:37Z
Content: Texas RRC office staff may have access to information which has not been updated online. I called about a well which for months had shown as having gone to spud but nothing else.  It is helpful to have the permit number and other details handy.

Author: Archie_Smith
Date: 2025-04-13T17:25:08Z
Content: Perhaps someone can provide commentary that will allow me to understand what is going on with a Continental Resources well in SEC 13 BLK A-56 PSL with a completed and paying well (jackrabbit 1308A 1-H) which has just had a new drilling permit issued. Does this mean the old well will just be turned off and a new well drilled ? The new permit (as of 4/ 8) describes this as a new drill, indicating total depth 300 ft deeper than earlier.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-25T15:10:12Z
Content: Jackrabbtit was still producing as of February.  Continental has the Bullsnake 1404A 01H just about 1.5 miles west.  Is that the one you are looking at?  Rig onsite now in Abstract A-1728. Blue abstract has Jackrabbit.  The new well is over to the west-long one 35067

Author: Archie_Smith
Date: 2025-04-27T04:47:01Z
Content: Those are the wells I am asking about. I understand the new, 3 mile long in sec 14 is still being drilled. A real question I have is the new permit allowing a redrill of a well that is still in production in sec 13. It is not a barnburner by any measurement, but it is still generating a small monthly royalty payment. How do I interpret the new permit to drill an existing well still producing. when does the current production get turned off and the new drilling begin?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-27T15:45:31Z
Content: When you see amended permit, read the remarks and review all the attachments to see what is being changed.  Compare to earlier permit forms and plats.  The December 2024 remark notes that field is being changed per RRC recommendation - from Ruppel (Woodford) to Flying Dove (Miss) - and the TVD was also being changed.  This is not a re-drill.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-28T12:57:32Z
Content: Also check the API number for the new permit versus the original well.  If the number is different, then it is a new well.  If the number is mostly the same, but the last four digits change, then a change to the original wellbore.

Author: katydid979
Date: 2025-04-25T20:03:36Z
Content: I’ve been offered $16,000 for 5.3 acres of property in Converse County, Wyoming. I currently lease the rights to a company that pays me about $3,000 for every 3 years. El Dorado Mineral Partners has been quick to make this offer. I’ve not ever had an offer to purchase the rights, just a lot of offers to lease it. I have always stayed with McDonald Land/Chesapeake. rag_documents.title: Stephens County Oklahome Recent Lease Offer from Bearcat
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Stephens County Oklahome Recent Lease Offer from Bearcat

Author: MICHAEL_A
Date: 2025-03-04T16:31:27Z
Content: Family has owned rights on two sections in Stephens County OK for years.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-06T15:05:56Z
Content: Given that Continental has permits for horizontal wells just to the east of you to drill horizontal wells in 2,3,10 and 11 from SE to NW, I suspect they may be the future operator.  BearCat frequently leases for them.  Personally, I do not go for an option as that makes the time frame too long and gives too much power to the lessee.  I prefer the highest royalty offered.  Balco Energy has been leasing in section 5-they pooled for the W2 NE4 for the Viola in 2024.  I suspect others will pop in closer to drilling for the rest of the acreage.

Author: John_Moseley
Date: 2025-03-06T15:44:45Z
Content: Why are they drilling SE to NW?  Is the formation contoured or is there a fault. Most of the surrounding wells are N-S.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-06T15:57:06Z
Content: They are trying to hit the structural grain of the reservoir at the optimum angle to the well bore so the fractures drain the best. They probably learned something from the early wells that made them switch direction.  CLR has quite a few permits/wells trending that direction nearby.

Author: John_Moseley
Date: 2025-03-06T16:40:00Z
Content: That makes sense. We are in S2 and the discovery well (Gentry) survey showed wide variation in vertical depth across the section.

Author: MICHAEL_A
Date: 2025-03-09T17:11:43Z
Content: Ms. Barnes I thought I had thanked you for your constant informed help to me and others over the years but I do not see my previous Reply. So let me try again…thank you so much very appreciated. Several very helpful tips as I prepare for negotiations with Bearcat. If you get a chance, can you give a novice like me a dumbed down primer on advantages/disadvantages of letting Deadline pass and waiting for “pooling”. Thanks again, be safe.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-10T13:40:57Z
Content: In OK, all minerals rights must be accounted for before drilling. For the mineral owners who cannot be found, are deceased, refuse to lease, lease close to expiring and fell through the cracks, etc., the Oklahoma Corporation Commission has a forced pooling procedure to handle those acres.

Author: MICHAEL_A
Date: 2025-03-11T15:29:42Z
Content: Update. Initial Negotiations with Bearcat Regarding Sec 5-3S-4W and Sec 32-2S-4W.
Offer Being Considered: Lease Term of 3 Years with a 2 Year Option; at 1/5 Royalty; Lease Bonus of $402 per Mineral Acre.

Author: MICHAEL_A
Date: 2025-03-19T00:08:22Z
Content: I will certainly understand if Ms. Barnes (and others) have already devoted enough time to assisting my family–and the assistance has been invaluable–regarding the pending Offer from Bearcat.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-21T13:55:54Z
Content: “downstream of the tailgate” and “shall be deductible for all purposes” are  huge red flags. That is opening you up to all sorts of charges.

Author: MICHAEL_A
Date: 2025-03-21T15:49:24Z
Content: Ms. Barnes you are beyond awesome and this is not a recent observation of mine (you have helped us at least 2X with previous Leases in Stephens County OK). While awaiting arrival of the Leases to be signed if acceptable–highly unlikely now–I plan to call Recon Resources and Gulfport Energy to at least see what they have to say. Very unlikely we will consider what Bearcat has proposed.

Author: John_Moseley
Date: 2025-04-22T22:39:13Z
Content: Drove thru SE Stephens County over the weekend. New pad is built immediately to NW offset of Gentry well in S11,3S,4W. Another large pad with LOTS of equipment and personnel was in NE corner of section immediately N of Hwy 53.

Author: MICHAEL_A
Date: 2025-04-26T19:22:15Z
Content: Updates: when I kept pushing Bearcat o/b/o Continental to either drop the "Gross Proceeds Clause (more accurately a “Potentially Large Expenses to Lessor” Clause) OR to give me some potential range (Hiundreds? Thousands?) of possible future Deductions other than stating “The Deductions can never exceed the Royalty”; but certainly can potentially put a huge dent in it) they have not been heard from since my e-mail to Bearcat of two weeks ago.

Author: Tom_Ed_Moore
Date: 2025-04-26T20:43:45Z
Content: you need an exhibit A that states no deduction, no warranty etc.

Author: susanslakeplace
Date: 2025-03-31T20:24:00Z
Content: I received an letter of options from a Landman for Prime along with Freedom Operations Company to lease my inherited mineral rights.  Legit?  I have never had options.  I reading on this forum that getting an attorney, counter offering, and to not sign the option letter but wait for the lease agreement.  True for Lincoln County, OK, too?  Offer is quite low as my rights are divided heavily among others.  Advice appreciated.  Mineral Rights, Section 20, Township 14, South half of the SW corner, Lincoln Co, OK

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2025-04-01T10:57:19Z
Content: You have an incomplete legal description. Section, Township & Range.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-01T13:28:17Z
Content: Welcome to the forum.  The option letter is the first approach.  I do not sign the letters-ever. I do not think it is wise to sign something before I have even seen their draft lease.  Once I see the lease and review with attorney’s advice, then can counter offer or chose to wait for force pooling if a good lease is not forthcoming.  Your location needs a complete section, township and range.  Lincoln County will have a N on the Township. Are you in Range 5E or a different range?

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-04-01T15:25:15Z
Content: I reading on this forum that getting an attorney, counter offering, and to not sign the option letter but wait for the lease agreement.

Author: susanslakeplace
Date: 2025-04-07T20:56:06Z
Content: The description is as follows: South Half (S2) of  Section 20, Township 14 North, Range 5 East, Lincoln County, Oklahoma.  Proposed drilling of the Mickelson 1-20HP.
Since the mailing of the first proposal options of which there were three concerning royalties and amounts per acre a certified letter came from the same land man, John Mayo, of Jurray Land Services, INC with an offer added to participate and share the costs of drilling with an “urgency” to reply.  “FOPCO anticipaters filing a forced pooling application with the Oklahoma Corporation Commission in the near future…” so the letter says.  Wait for pooling to respond?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-25T13:33:29Z
Content: If timing is short, then pooling is probably the best option.Freedom pooled the north half in 2024 for the Prue.  $80 1/8th, $75 1/6th, $50 3/16ths.

Author: susanslakeplace
Date: 2025-04-25T14:38:15Z
Content: Thank you for responding!  You, Ms Barnes, are very helpful.

Date: 2025-04-25T14:39:09Z
Content: If you need an example of a pooling order response letter, come back and I can give you a draft.

Date: 2025-04-25T15:08:58Z
Content: That would be great.  My deceased mom used to handle all this and is now my responsibility.  She worked for an oil company and had much more info than me.

Date: 2025-04-26T18:44:00Z
Content: Thank you for the form letter to expect.  You are so helpful.  I do not have the means to participate in the drilling.  I only have a share of the mineral rights passed down to me.  As a senior citizen, the forms are changing and sometimes confusing to us.

Content: Most regular mineral owners choose not to participate.  It is not for the novice.

rag_documents.title: Sample owner-friendly clauses in OGL?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Sample owner-friendly clauses in OGL?

Author: Skimo
Date: 2025-04-18T18:26:48Z
Content: Cheers.  We have negotiated a fair lease in the Bakken and are now down to the clauses in the lease.  Does anyone have examples of owner-friendly language? More specifically,
1, Examples of depth clauses for the Bakken,
2, Realistic shut-in clause vs the producer offered $1/NMA/Year,
3. Wellhead production vs In-the pipe.

Author: Bully5
Date: 2025-04-18T20:47:30Z
Content: Gas well or oil well?
One clause in many leases which could be problematic is oil royalties paid " at the wellhead". That should be " royalties paid at the point of sale" in my opinion. “At the wellhead” production is undeterminable in that wellhead production is not ever just oil.
That might open the mineral owner to " post production costs". I am not a lawyer and this my opinion. Happened to my son.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-18T21:14:02Z
Content: The royalties paid with  “at the wellhead” language varies by state.  Also be careful about “at the point of sale”.    “At the point of sale” could be at the well head by an operator selling to their own company at a discounted price.  Or it could be another transmission company.  Many good leases have language about “at the tailgate of the processing plant” to a third party un-afilliated company with no post production charges.  Language varies by state. That is why it is a good idea to get a good oil and gas attorney to review the lease.

Author: AJ11
Date: 2025-04-19T01:42:36Z
Content: You might consider:
1.) Uploading your lease to an AI platform for a plain English analysis. Also have it address your specific questions and concerns.
2.) Search the county records for a recorded lease whose lessor is a company which invests in minerals–one that will likely not accept something like a “Producers 88” lease. In Texas, notice of leases can be recorded with a Memorandum instead of the full lease. A Memo-ed lease will not be of help. Every now and then–in Texas–an mineral owner (apparently) will insist that the full lease is recorded. Leases may not be memo-ed in Montana and/or North Dakota.  Back to  Texas where leases for State owned lands are not memo-ed and the perfected(?)_lease is available. Are there state owned minerals in the Bakken?
3.) Find a landman who does not work for the company which is trying to lease your minerals and get him/her to look at your lease.

Author: Skimo
Date: 2025-04-20T23:32:08Z
Content: Thank you—some very sharp and insightful answers from all of you.  I’ll give it a go.  We have been frustrated trying to find a Bakken area lawyer that will take on new clients or whose firm is not engaged with the Lessee.

Author: fjonesiv
Date: 2025-04-21T01:32:46Z
Content: We have been frustrated trying to find a Bakken area lawyer that will take on new clients or whose firm is not engaged with the Lessee.

Author: Brian_Burns
Date: 2025-04-22T14:18:55Z
Content: I used an excellent firm in the area to probate our ownership. They were very reasonable and pretty quick. If you’d like the info, I will look it up.

Author: Jbeee
Date: 2025-04-22T18:06:32Z
Content: How do we run a lease through AI? Please pardon my ignorance. I’m still trying to wrap my head around this AI stuff

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-22T18:25:59Z
Content: Personally, I would only use AI for informational purposes and not for legal purposes.  AI only knows what it was trained on and may not know the statutory difference from state to state.

Author: Skimo
Date: 2025-04-22T18:41:37Z
Content: As mentioned by others, AI is a great research tool, and can help you get an idea of what is more fair for a Lessor vs the contract the Lessee will start with.  Many of the clauses are really part of the negotiation, and may or may not have implications down the road.  Some owners only look at the Bonus, %, and Term. In the end, a Lawyer is advised. But finding an available lawyer that specializes in oil leases in Williston is tough.  Possibly look for a firm that specializes in oil/gas but dont limit yourself to ND?

Author: AJ11
Date: 2025-04-25T22:51:56Z
Content: This is a very abbreviated version of my reply which was for some reason not published. Google “Gemini” and Bing “Copilot” AI models allow one to upload files. If you have a pdf of your lease, upload it and ask your questions. You can also cut and paste lease language or even type by hand. If you have Copilot app on your phone, you can probably just take photos of the proposed lease

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-04-21T19:56:34Z
Content: If so, what are you guys expecting the increase in well costs to be due to the significant increase in drilling pipe costs and other steel needed to refurbish rigs? Have you started seeing the increase in prices yet? I dont own many non op sections but have recently received some paperwork on 3 properties, 2 in OK and 1 in Texas, guessing they are 6 months away from AFE’s if they do drill the wells, just curious what more experienced people are seeing/hearing about pricing on 1-2 mile laterals.  Thanks Bob

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-04-22T19:45:51Z
Content: Take a look at your recent AFEs and add 10-20% to your pipe cost. A greater affect on activity will a 10% drop in crude prices and growing instability in the Nat Gas market.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-04-23T21:31:58Z
Content: Not worried about the natural gas and oil prices, instability is always a factor.  Was just curious about pipe/casing etc costs.  You say 10-20% but from my understanding it could be up to125% increase in costs, which is a different ballgame.  Guess my question is probably 2-3 months early as the pipe being used now to drill wells is already here, but will be interesting to see how much completing a well/well costs go up 4 months from now.  If it does go up to125% like some are saying and oil and gas prices fall even more in the worst case scenario but very likely to happen, not sure how companies will be able to drill new wells given the economics.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-04-24T01:45:02Z
Content: There has been a great deal of speculation in this area due to supply source. The present concensus is balancing US production of OCTG with foreign supply and applicable tariffs should create a 15% increase in OCTG. This should increase well cost by 2-5%. Current prices should decrease new wells more that this issue and should decrease DUC completions.

Date: 2025-04-24T22:04:15Z

rag_documents.title: Questions about Offer to Buy Inherited Working Interest
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Questions about Offer to Buy Inherited Working Interest

Author: sasha
Date: 2025-04-23T02:24:21Z
Content: Hi, newbie here. My family was recently contacted by a Landman who has made us an offer on a 2% Working Interest of oil and gas that was owned by my parents, both deceased for many years.  Here is the location: Section 3, Block 35, T-3-N, T&P Ry. Co. Survey, Dawson and Martin Counties, Texas.
We didn’t know about this and thought everything had been sold when my mother died more than 20 years ago. The Landman told us the working interest has not produced anything and is for 200 feet below the Sprayberry Dean wells. Everything to 200 ft was sold after my mother died.
I’m really new to all this and wondering if we should accept the offer or do some more research to see if it’s worth anything. Does anyone know of any companies that are going to drill deeper than 200 ft in this area? Or can direct me to a professional who can advise us as to the value of what we own and if this is a good offer.
Thank you so much.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-04-23T23:20:19Z
Content: You have a few issues here. First, you have to determine the actual rights for the subject WI. 200’ below the Sprayberry is the issue and not below 200’.

Author: sasha
Date: 2025-04-24T10:04:02Z
Content: Thank you for your reply. I understood it to mean the WI is anything below 200 ft. I’m not sure what you mean by " 200’ below the Sprayberry is the issue and not below 200’." Can you explain further?

Author: NMoilboy
Date: 2025-04-24T11:39:45Z
Content: The Dean formation is roughly 8800’ deep there.  So basically sounds like you have a 2% WI (in some amount of acreage) in any wells that would produce from formations below 9000’.

Author: sasha
Date: 2025-04-24T19:03:45Z
Content: It’s a WI in 2% of all of Sec 3, 640 acres, 200’ below the Sprayberry wells. The Landman is valuing it at $500 per acre. Is this low?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-24T19:18:53Z
Content: You should research origin of the WI.  Did your parent(s) take a lease from a mineral owner and what was the royalty rate?  Many of the old leases were at 1/8 to 3/16th.  Or was it an assignment from another WI?  Consider an assignment (sale), but reserve on overriding royalty of the difference between 25% and the existing royalty and overrides.  That adds considerably to the value.

Author: CH1
Date: 2025-04-24T20:51:49Z
Content: One thing to take into consideration is that once horizontals wells are drilled you will owe the operator 2% of the cost of each well drilled. WI is a great asset if you have the capital to participate.

Author: NMoilboy
Date: 2025-04-24T21:00:24Z
Content: There is a non-zero chance that we are not talking about the same thing here.

Author: sasha
Date: 2025-04-24T23:50:29Z
Content: He’s offering $6.4K for 2% WI across all of the 640 acres. So you’re saying that’s too low?

Author: sasha
Date: 2025-04-25T00:31:36Z
Content: Thank you James_Garner1. I have confirmed it’s 200’ below the Sprayberry. I’ve contacted Diamondback. I would be interested in the attorney’s name. Thanks for your help.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-04-25T01:40:31Z
Content: Rick Strange at the Hamm Law Group in Midland. Good luck.

rag_documents.title: Different leases, different counties
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Different leases, different counties

Author: Lila
Date: 2025-03-31T14:27:04Z
Content: I have mineral rights for three wells Tyler county, the lease agreement is for these 3 wells. In January 2025 I accumulated 2 more wells in Wetzel county, plus another well I think it’s a pool. Question is, on the new two wells that have been pumping since 2023. I would have thought I would have gotten a lease agreement for these two new wells. They are in a different county. Maybe someone here can give me some advice. Thanks

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-31T14:30:03Z
Content: Each tract of land would necessitate a different oil and gas lease.
It is possible the lessee is producing under a pooling proceeding.
Inquire of the operator if they have a lease.

Author: Lila
Date: 2025-03-31T20:25:54Z
Content: Another question for instance 1/1/25. Gas value pumped $793,919.33 after deductions $667,301.26. then with more deductions and interest. I got $72.57. Then on all of this, have to pay mineral taxes to Tyler county, then file income taxes to West Virginia for what little you received then you have to pay West Virginia again on the income taxes you had to file. Looks like to me only folks that make any money on this entire situation is West Virginia, then of course the gas and oil folks

Author: Lila
Date: 2025-03-31T20:26:03Z
Content: Another question: why on the statement on the monthly royalties. The company takes out deductions on the gross, then takes more deductions out of what small amount the owner gets. So the gas and oil company is taking the deduction out twice. For instance it’s oil, by the time they take out all of these deductions. That comes to a total 0.13¢.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-25T14:58:45Z
Content: If allowed by the lease and the state statutes, the operator can take out deductions for the post production charges such as marketing, transportation, dehydration, taxes, etc.  Your royalties are calculated using a formula that takes into account your net acreage, the spacing for the well for that reservoir, your royalty, post production charges and taxes.  It is normal.

rag_documents.content:

Author: Barbie59
Date: 2025-04-24T19:04:03Z
Content: I am a complete newbie to all of this. My siblings and cousins were notified about a year and half ago, by Bearcat Land Dev. who was representing Continental Resources, that we were the heirs to mineral rights in several horizontal wells in Stephens County Oklahoma, Specifically the Springer well, and several others. Long story short, Continental went to court and declared all of us the heirs,  along with a slew of other people in January of this year.
Then they went to court again several times to split the wells so they could drill more oil per day.
At Least that is what we could understand in the numerous envelopes of paperwork from continental attorneys and the state of Oklahoma. The President of “Bearcat”  has spoken l with my brother and my cousin many times, and they also saw them in court. rag_documents.title: Well Reached Payout after Penalty for not participating
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Well Reached Payout after Penalty for not participating

Author: Spunky_dez
Date: 2025-03-01T03:03:37Z
Content: How do you know if an oil and gas operator is being honest about a well being in pay status after penalty is paid for not participating in your working interest portion? How can you double check this? Especially when you had no idea about the interest at the time the wells were drilled.

Author: Steve_Durrett
Date: 2025-03-01T22:50:07Z
Content: You can request a payout statement from the Operator and you can hire an accountant to perform an audit.  If you know of other owners who are in risk penalty status, you could possibly share the cost of the audit with them.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-03T14:47:09Z
Content: You should post the State and the Operator for better replies to your situation. Statutory requirements vary by State.

Author: Spunky_dez
Date: 2025-04-21T22:34:36Z
Content: Do you happen to know how much these audits generally cost?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-22T14:32:06Z
Content: Cost would depend on the depth of the audit - cursory look vs reviewing the JIB summaries vs analyzing and reconciling the invoices - times the hourly fee of your expert (maybe $300-$1,000).  It would be expensive and not financially worthwhile unless you have a sizeable revenue interest in the well.  Moreover, you should also review the future JIB statements that you will be paying for your WI.  Oil companies have experienced in-house petroleum engineers and analysts who do this on a regular basis for their non-op working interests.  Small individual WI owners generally just accept the data as the costs would wipe out their revenues.

Author: Spunky_dez
Date: 2025-04-25T03:11:14Z
Content: It seems that small working interest owners are just made to accept whatever they are given with no regard for what is fair, legal or ethical. That are at the mercy of the operator.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-25T04:50:28Z
Content: This is a serious business and each owner is responsible for keeping their own good records.  Larger non-operating WI frequently spend their own time and money auditing the well financial records.  You can ask for access to the detailed records, but if you have no expertise or experience to analyze, then you need to hire your own experts.  This is not unethical or unfair.  Think if it this way.  If you buy a rental house and are not skilled in carpentry and plumbing to make your own repairs, then you have to hire experts to do this for you.  This is why most small mineral owner lease their minerals instead of participating in the well.

rag_documents.title: Elected to take on additional non consenting working interest
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Elected to take on additional non consenting working interest

Author: Spunky_dez
Date: 2025-04-25T03:27:26Z
Content: I received an offer of elections to take on the additional non consenting working interest in addition to my consented working interest share. I returned the election form promptly and it was acknowledged that they received it by the operator. It is now time for the wells to start paying out and the additional interest is not included on my division orders. The landman said sorry that was the best we could do for you. Can the operator just decide they don’t want to give you the option after agreeing to give it to you and you signing the election form. The wells are in Eddy, New Mexico.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-25T04:33:27Z
Content: The question about whether or not you would elect to take on additional workin interest is sent out to all WI at the same time, as part of AFE process.  In the event that one or more WI opt out, then those interests will be divided among those WI who elected to take on additional interests.  If 100% of WI agree to participate in the well, then there is no interest to be divided up.  You would have received a notice that you were being allocated additional interest and you would have paid the extra share of all related well costs.  It is not extra income you get for free.  You have to have paid the extra up-front costs.  Review your AFE and JIB statements to see that you were not paying an increased share (increased decimal) of the total expenses.  Generally none of the participating WI will opt out unless they expect the well or the repairs to be a losing proposition.  You may want to research the working interest process to get a better understanding of how this side of the oil and gas business works and the economics, including ultimate liability for the cost of well plugging.  Read the JOA and other documents that you have signed.  And consult your CPA about the proper way to report the revenues and costs on your federal and state tax returns.  For individuals, this is earned income on Schedule C.

rag_documents.title: Participation in drilling an oil well?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Participation in drilling an oil well?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-07T13:10:53Z
Content: Be aware that participating has it advantages and disadvantages.  Participating is not recommended for the novice unless you have deep pockets, can hire an oil and gas attorney and an accountant, get liabilitiy insurance, put the the assets into an LLC to protect you from personal liability, be willing to pay decades of operating costs and pass that on to your heirs.  Just a few items to consider.  Talk to your CPA and attorney before deciding so that you understand the pros and cons.

Author: BP11
Date: 2025-04-07T19:34:16Z
Content: Hi- usually when we receive a participation/working interest lease request we will pass for all the reasons M. Barnes mentions, but we always request the operator/driller provide us with royalty lease terms and then negotiate a RI agreement. They can’t exclude you because you pass up participating in the well but if your minerals remain unleased it will be a long time before you see royalties due to NM’s rules.

Author: Ryan_Fairbanks
Date: 2025-04-07T21:27:18Z
Content: Is it a lease offer, or an offer/election to participate? It seems to me that if it is an oil & gas lease offer, they may be running that concurrently with seeking permitting, but will need to do the spacing/pooling separately once they know who they can lease and who wants to participate.

Author: fixit
Date: 2025-04-21T15:22:23Z
Content: Ryan – It’s both. I can either sign a lease at 1/5 or I can elect to participate.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-21T15:27:06Z
Content: The new drilling of horizontal wells is generally for different reservoirs than the older shallow wells.

Author: NMoilboy
Date: 2025-04-22T14:58:31Z
Content: I would guess the wells will be fine.   They will be Yeso wells.  Hz but shallow.
You are not in the Delaware Basin, you are on the NW shelf.   So it’s not going to look like a lot of Eddy County, but it should look like the Margaret, Leavitt, Kaiser, etc wells just north of there.

Author: NMoilboy
Date: 2025-04-23T22:42:33Z
Content: In general in that area there are a large number of deep vertical wells that have been or could be converted to injection.   In the Cisco etc.  Deeper than any of this production.   Riley Exp for instance has 4 SWD wells in 18s27e that have been taking like 15kbpwd.   Its not THAT expensive to just run lay flat and pump water over to an SWD.

rag_documents.title: What Are Negotiating Points When Signing A Lease
rag_documents.content:
Topic: What Are Negotiating Points When Signing A Lease

Author: UncleJed
Date: 2025-04-16T19:08:07Z
Content: My siblings and I are expecting a lease proposal soon. We’re new to this having inherited the mineral rights recently. What are the negotiating points that we should focus on?

Author: UncleJed
Date: 2025-04-17T14:11:19Z
Content: They’re in Wetzel, Tyler and 2 other counties in WV.

Author: Steve_Durrett
Date: 2025-04-17T14:54:33Z
Content: As Ryan said, there may be a tradeoff between Upfront Bonus and Royalty Percentage.  If the well(s) are successful, you will probably be better off going for the higher royalty and lower bonus.

Author: UncleJed
Date: 2025-04-18T00:03:44Z
Content: What do you consider a significant acreage position?

Author: Nick-TBM
Date: 2025-04-18T17:30:04Z
Content: @UncleJed, you have some solid advise on here already but I work in this area and may be able to shine some area specific insight on this. You said tyler and wetzel, so I’m going to assume its near the county line perhaps? This likely puts you in Antero territory. Be VERY thorough signing a lease with them! They are a big group and know the ins and outs of a lease to maximize their profits (as any company would I suppose). The negotiating points of a lease is just as much about removing certain things as it is about adding some in. For this area they typically offer a 12.5% lease with 12.5% deductions. If you can, avoid this by any means necessary. Tyler/Wetzel produce decently and any deductions will be very costly in the long term. I’ve seen them also exclude certain minerals from their royalty payments. For example it stated that royalties would be paid on all oil and gas, but not gaseous liquids which are NGL’s and these are very profitable. You need to make sure 100% that you get royalties on every single thing coming from that ground.

Author: UncleJed
Date: 2025-04-23T01:28:37Z
Content: Thank you, that’s some really good information! My Aunt and Uncle have already signed their lease agreements. My Dad was the oldest and I believe 3 wells have already been started. The rights are on 252 acres in Tyler, Wetzel, Pleasants, and Jackson.

Author: UncleJed
Date: 2025-04-23T02:24:49Z
Content: Antero is the main company, but EQT is also dealing with us on some of the land.

rag_documents.title: Calculate royalties based on co. investment
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Calculate royalties based on co. investment

Author: nielloeb
Date: 2025-04-19T01:41:22Z
Content: Is there a way to calculate expected royalties based on what a company invests?Example 1:  A company provides a $100,000 lease bonus.  They obviously expect to pull more than $100,000 out of the ground over a certain period of time.  But can you calculate their expected royalties payments during, say, the most-productive period of time (which I understand is perhaps the first three years?

Topic: Dry Creek Operating Lease

Author: John_B_Mann
Date: 2025-04-21T11:53:09Z
Content: I recently had a leasing request from Dry Creek Operating for my mineral rights in this section. What is going on? Grady county 34 6N 7W

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-21T13:06:27Z
Content: Camino has rigs drilling horizontal wells in 13/24/25 just to the NE of you.
I do not see any filed leases in the last 24 months in 34, but there are many leases across the township.  They range from 1/8th, to 1/4th.  I suspect Camino or Continental will be the operator.  If you have not leased before, it is wise to get a good oil and gas attorney to look at any draft lease as the they are not in the mineral owner’s favor and need improvements.  You can also wait to see if there is force pooling which is a viable alternative to leasing.

Author: John_B_Mann
Date: 2025-04-21T15:56:36Z
Content: Thanks Martha,  I have leased this mineral right before, It seems to be a very good offer, so I am a little leery,

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-21T15:59:48Z
Content: Watch the language on the lease.  They are drilling infill wells on the ones to the NE of you.  You do not want post production charges!

Author: April_K_Gamertsfelder
Date: 2025-04-21T16:06:40Z
Content: Not sure if my question got through…We have minerals in 13,24,18 and 19… We have leases with Camino and Continental.  How close to being done are these wells in 13 and 24?
Any help would be appreciated!
Thanks,
April

Author: Don_Bray
Date: 2025-04-21T16:32:41Z
Content: There are 3 Camino leased rigs. Two are drilling 2 wells each from section 13 into section 24 (North to South)).  The other rig is also drilling 2 wells; 1 from section 24 into section 25 (GRANT 0607 24-25-1UXH); and 1 from section 24 into section 13 (TYLER 0607 24-13-3WXH). All in 6N-7W. 6 total wells. All rigs still drilling.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-21T16:48:39Z
Content: A general rule of thumb in that area (13,24,25 set) is about a year from spud to pay plus or minus a month or so.  They will probably get them all drilled and then come in and do a zipper frac to save time and money. Then it takes about five months to run the title for the division orders.  They have to pay 180 days from first sales.

Author: John_B_Mann
Date: 2025-04-22T10:41:30Z
Content: Martha, the lease does not have a post production clause.  I still have a hard time beliveing it is so rich: 1/4 royalty and $1,250 bonus. !

Author: Don_Bray
Date: 2025-04-22T16:11:11Z
Content: Section 12 6N 7W… I was offered 1/4 royalty and $1,500 bonus from another company. After lengthy negotiations they would not agree to no post production charges in the lease. I didn’t walk away from the lease… I ran!!! lol

rag_documents.title: Newbie questions please
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Newbie questions please

Author: JALSR
Date: 2025-02-05T17:29:06Z
Content: IS the royalty in East Texas (Cass) a standard 1/5 rate? How  negotiable is this ?

Author: D_Wells
Date: 2025-02-05T22:51:27Z
Content: There is not a standard royalty.  The royalty is negotiable, but a 1/4 if usually the highest possible. The “sign on bonus” is offered by the landman.  You will not know if there is competition until someone else appears and makes you an offer.

Author: JALSR
Date: 2025-02-06T17:03:02Z
Content: Stupid Question Here.
What is the incentive to reach out to all mineral owners?
If someone says no they still go after the oil.

Author: E_W_WILLIS
Date: 2025-02-06T17:03:19Z
Content: Virtually all the leases we have negotiated are 1/4 royalty.  Just as important is the lease form. If you don’t have a royalty owner friendly form join TLMA and use their form.

Author: Michael52
Date: 2025-02-07T19:03:59Z
Content: Hello very newbie here, I appreciate  everyones advice and time. I am in Lincoln, Nebraska and my mineral rights are in Monongalia, county WV. I received them through inheritance from my grandmothers passing. She received them through her husbands passing. So that would make me third generation holder of said mineral rights.  I am not sure if I am the rightful owner or really how any of this works.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-02-07T19:04:12Z
Content: Believe you have another post on this matter.  Everything is negotiable as long as theres multiple parties involved. Since you only have 1 acre, it doesnt leave you in a position to have much if any leverage.  One can only determine the bonus offers based off whatever offers they are getting at the time, its not set in stone.  For example, if someone owns 100 acres in a hot area, they are going to get much better offers than the person that owns 1 acre in the same section, as the 100 acres could decide whom operates the well.

Author: D_Wells
Date: 2025-02-07T21:09:23Z
Content: The incentive to the explorer (operator) to reach out to all the mineral owners inside his prospect is two fold.

Author: JALSR
Date: 2025-02-08T04:05:46Z
Content: If they only need to have 50% what happens to the rest?

Author: JALSR
Date: 2025-02-08T04:05:56Z
Content: There are several of us family members who have equal  1 acre interest
Should we be trying negotiate as a family even if we only have small individual acreage?

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-02-08T23:42:28Z
Content: They join in the well, its just not theirs to drill/operate. Ill just be honest with you, even if you get 5 more family members to join you, 6 acres total doesnt leave you with much if any power to negotiate especially when you add 5 more parties into the mix as operators will simply save the time and money to move on to larger interests.  Your acreage does set up perfectly for small non-op companies, so Id sit tight until the smaller companies start calling you and play ball with them as they generally are easier to work with and more flexible on their terms.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-02-08T23:43:15Z
Content: Joint negotiations can be helpful financially, but can also be like herding cats.

Author: Nick-TBM
Date: 2025-02-13T13:37:48Z
Content: @Michael52there are a lot of ways to determine mineral ownership. It sounds like you would own them through heirship which would follow west virginias laws for succession. Were you named in the last will and testament from your grandmother? Was she named in the will from her late husband? If there is a direct paper trail it is much easier to track. If not, it can still be determined by heirship and heirship affidavits. Determining ownership, location, and any activity would be pretty high up on my list of priorities which can be done by a landman in WV pretty quickly. Are companies approaching you about these minerals?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-02-13T14:10:43Z
Content: Standard lease time varies by area and competition.  Most of the leases in many states are a three year lease, but some areas have five years as more common.

Author: Ryan_Fairbanks
Date: 2025-04-17T15:42:22Z
Content: The County where they are located and the proximity to other producing wells, as well as the geology and potential opportunity for high-volume producing wells, will all be factors in how the operator will determine the economics of their offers.

Author: MJSm1th
Date: 2025-04-19T12:49:43Z
Content: Hello,
I inherited mineral rights in Meigs County, Ohio and would like to know how to go about finding out if there is any interest in leasing or drilling there. I sat on this while Biden was in office but now with Trump’s ‘Drill Baby Drill’ initiative I am hopeful that there will be some activity. I would love to hear feedback on where to start.

Date: 2025-04-19T20:58:25Z
Content: What do you mean you sat on it? As in you turned down multiple offers due to whom was the president until youd negotiate? Just curious if you are still getting those same offer amounts with Oil prices where they are now?  Drill baby drill leads to lower oil and natural gas prices, lower prices = less drilling, therefore much fewer new leases taken.

rag_documents.title: Landman Survey: Farmout Agreements
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Landman Survey: Farmout Agreements

Author: adb
Date: 2025-04-09T23:34:47Z
Content: I am taking some courses in petroleum land management and am surveying landmen to get their opinions on farmout agreements. If you work as a landman I’d love to hear your responses to the below questions. Thank you!

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-04-12T21:33:20Z
Content: tim_dowdApril 12, 2025,  9:33pm2In the oil and gas industry, a farmout agreement  is a contract where one party (the farmor) transfers a portion of their interest in an oil and gas lease to another party (the farmee) in return for drilling or other work on the property. The farmee typically agrees to drill or perform work to earn a working interest in the lease.
2.companies farm out acreage for any number of reasons. Their budget doesn’t support drilling in this acreage. This acreage may not be a priority. Think of it like a monopoly board. The farmor is interested in the oranges and reds , but they get an offer on the greens (pacific etc). This is not in their geographical area.
The farmor is willing to let the farmee risk their capital to prove or disprove the viability of the Green acreage tracts.Terms or standards in a farmout: a) drill a well or complete a well in paying quantities to earn the acreage; b) must drill by a certain date. Especially helpful if leases are expiring; c) any formation or a specific depth; d) does farmout receive an overriding royalty interest.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-04-17T23:43:07Z
Content: Rarely see “farmouts” these days, atleast from what Ive seen in the areas that I own in covering Oklahoma, Texas, North Dakota and Wyoming.  Seems like most people use 3 year wellbore term assignments these days. In the 80’s I bought 20, 80-160 acre vertical wells where the companies went bankrupt.  I did farmouts on all but 5 of them as I didnt have the capital to drill new wells, so my experiences arent what you are looking for as they are outdated, but anywhoo my answers below.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-04-18T17:29:33Z
Content: Agree with Bob. Term assignments are most common now. The reason is, that landman with company A negotiates farmout with landman with company B. Then when the well gets drilled, the farmee forgets to secure the assignment or contacts Company B, but the landman has moved on. New landman doesn’t know anything about it, and never gets around to learning about it.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-04-21T16:08:34Z
Content: The farmout can still be a useful tool in land management, but it is not widely used today. Companies are more interested in acreage swaps so they have control of development.

Author: Dkmack25
Date: 2025-01-28T20:19:09Z

Content: Parents received an unsolicited offer for 3/16 mineral rights 32 12N 8W. Is there any new activity? They also have mineral rights in 29 12N 8W, but have not received any offers related to that.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-21T20:28:56Z
Content: Mach Resources has two new permits for infill drilling in 29&32.  The wells have already spud.  If it were me, I would not sell when there is active drilling.

Author: sactown_dude
Date: 2025-03-24T20:24:52Z
Content: Thank you. When will we know the production of the new drilling, and how should we value their interests if they do want to sell?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-24T22:12:13Z
Content: They will receive a Division order that states their decimal percentage for the royalties.  It will be based upon the equation net acres/actual spacing acres x royalty x % perforations in their section(s).  Based upon nearby wells and their decline curves and after about six months of production, as estimated future production by volume of products can be determined.  Various future pricing scenarios can be applied to get an estimated royalty value.   Offers will usually be lower than this value due to the time value of money.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-03-26T23:44:06Z
Content: Mach Resources has two new permits for infill drilling in 29&32.  The wells have already spud.  If it were me, I would not sell when there is active drilling.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-27T00:02:08Z
Content: Everyone needs to make their own decision.  I tend to look at the long term as in decades, not short term.  Takes about a year from permit to pay if they are drilling multi-unit wells and multiple wells take even longer.  Many sections in Canadian are excellent for gas, so I like hanging onto gas acreage.  Most offers I have received in Canadian are based upon a discounted cash value for current production and do not include the pending new royalties.  Our family wants those royalties, so that is our strategy.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-03-27T14:09:29Z

Author: sactown_dude
Date: 2025-04-19T17:32:17Z
Content: Thank you. We’ll probably wait until production begins.

Content: With all due respect now is the time to sell if they want to sell. This is the peak of speculation and their minerals will likely not be worth more to someone else than they are now.

rag_documents.title: Lea County, NM Lease Offer
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Lea County, NM Lease Offer

Author: Michelle2024
Date: 2025-03-03T19:27:54Z
Content: My 2 siblings and myself received a lease offer on 240 gross mineral acres. 3yr primary term with a 2yr option to extend. Bonus is $750 per net mineral acre (paid-up at beginning of lease within 45 days) and 20% royalty.

Author: Luke_Alexander
Date: 2025-03-03T20:21:23Z
Content: The first off is always their lowest offer.   The fact that they showed up at your door says a lot.  I have never had a valid offer go down if I tell them my lawyers are busy and they have to look at the lease, and mine is still waiting in the queue.

Author: NMoilboy
Date: 2025-03-04T02:11:29Z
Content: Things change pretty rapidly in 24s36e.   As you move West to East you start to go from the Delaware Basin where horizontals are good, to the Central Basin Platform, where that’s much less of an option.  So a lot of the feedback would be contingent on knowing the section.

Author: Sean_Preston
Date: 2025-03-04T22:42:41Z
Content: Let me guess. Matador Resources (MRC). I received a similar offer, but 80 gross acres. Same terms. One of my issues is the Landman didn’t tell me how many net acres I own…He told me to sign the lease and send him an image, once they get that they would tell me what I owned and pay me…My interest is in Sec 25, Township 25 South, Range 36 East.

Author: Sean_Preston
Date: 2025-03-04T22:42:53Z
Content: He said 240 gross acres, not net. I’m sure its a undivided fraction within the 240 acres.

Author: AJ11
Date: 2025-03-05T02:33:39Z
Content: By “paid-up at beginning of lease within 45 days” are you saying you are considering handing over a signed lease without simultaneously exchanging it for a check backed by immediately available funds? Search this site for “bank draft” and “order for payment”

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-06T14:36:39Z
Content: I am not a fan of a two year extension and will not agree to it.  I think it is very unwise to hand over a lease without getting paid.  Many land men use the “gross” acreage as a teaser.  Most folks do not own that much and to me, it indicates, that they may not have done the title work yet.  Very expensive to do that.  The gross acreage often goes back to an original land patent grant, so easy to look up.  The title work is much more time consuming.  45 days is actually nine weeks!  Do you want to wait over two months to get paid?  Gives them plenty of time to flip the lease and you may or may not get paid-can be challenging if the lease is filed…

Author: Wnations
Date: 2025-03-07T14:35:56Z
Content: We’ve received an offer to lease our mineral rights in section 10E of T25S-R36E containing 320 acres for $1,000.00 per acre. We own 7 net mineral acres between three of us. I have very little knowledge about how this works or of this is a good offer or not. And advice would be appreciated!

Author: Ollie
Date: 2025-04-06T18:01:13Z
Content: It’s my understanding the formations differ drastically from east to west in that area. The eastern side of the township is much less proven and therefore much more speculative than the western side. 3 or 4 miles can make a difference. There’s a well map somewhere and the eastern side has virtually no horizontal wells. It only has shallow vertical wells, and I doubt that company is drilling shallow verticals.

Author: Bully5
Date: 2025-04-18T14:42:09Z
Content: Stay away from the 2 year option. Not good at all for you. Royalty: most royakties are migrating to 1/4 leases. Warning!! Everyone who shows up at your door with a lease and a check is not necessarily an Oil Company.
NEVER sign a lease without recieving immediately available funds!! They say " I need time to check title". They can check title befire they show up. They want 30-45 business days ( actually 60+ days) to do that. You are hog-tied for the duration. O&G lawyers are a must. Smooth sailing..BTW always throw a bank draft in the trash. It ain’t money.
