rag_documents.title: Wishgard LLC Lease offer in Wood County
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Wishgard LLC Lease offer in Wood County

Author: Buck22
Date: 2025-01-23T18:59:05Z
Content: Wishgard LLC out of PA has held several meetings and group signings in my area. They are offering 600 an acre with a 16% royalty. Several people have signed, but my close neighbors and I are leery of the contract. Has anyone had experience with this company? There has been no activity that I’m aware of in this area as far as drilling.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-01-24T15:32:56Z
Content: I would be wise to get several of you together to get a good oil and gas attorney to review the lease as the drafts are not generally in the mineral owner’s favor.  Operators frequently use a contract land company to do their leasing.

Author: Nick-TBM
Date: 2025-01-27T15:22:04Z
Content: @Buck22Not much activity in Wood, nor does there appear to be any activity in the next few years. I’m curious what they are hoping to gain from this lease. 16% WITHOUT deductions is not bad. $600/acre for a non producing area is not bad either. Never hurts to ask for more though!@M_Barnesis very right, they never offer you the best on the first go. This is a business and they are out to maximize profits. Talk to others in your area and shop this rate around, also talk to the landman/company and see what they think is going on there because WV DEP maps don’t show anything promising.

Author: Buck22
Date: 2025-02-11T19:38:35Z
Content: @M_BarnesThanks for the reply. I agree with getting the lease looked at, it does not appear to be in our favor for sure.

Author: Buck22
Date: 2025-02-11T19:38:40Z
Content: @Nick-TBMI wondered if there was anything coming to Wood and why there is such a push to get these leases. There is another round of meetings scheduled this month pertaining to several districts in Wood County and one in Jackson county. It sure seems like a great deal of money to lease a lot of non-producing properties.

Author: nhunley
Date: 2025-03-23T15:03:20Z
Content: My family lives in Wood County and I’ve been provided with the lease form. If memory serves, Wishgard puts together landowner groups to entice operators to buy the package, so I doubt they’re actually working for a real operator, but I don’t know. I assume this is a speculatively play only. rag_documents.title: Mineral Rights in West Virginia
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Mineral Rights in West Virginia

Author: NDB
Date: 2025-03-23T16:40:47Z
Content: I inherited a trust that holds mineral rights in WV. The trust terminated in 2008. What happens to the mineral rights? The taxes have been paid and are current.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-23T17:10:34Z
Content: The trust still owns the interest until the Trustee or successor Trustee prepares and records a deed to the beneficiaries.  Even though the Trust terminated, it can still act in order to clean up or finish its business.

Author: NDB
Date: 2025-03-23T22:39:22Z
Content: Thank you, Tim,
I am the trustee, and my second cousin is the other beneficiary for distribution. Our grandfathers were brothers, and we share the same great grandfather who is the original trustee per the trust doc. Because his grandfather predeceased my grandfather, our side became the trustee.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-24T21:03:00Z
Content: I would recommend that you distribute the minerals to yourself and your second cousin, individually.

Author: Nick-TBM
Date: 2025-04-04T16:16:24Z
Content: I@NDBI have seen this a few times and I often see the trustee’s work together to just sell the mineral rights directly from the trust as that would mean the new land owner is the one doing the work to deal with the legal documentation and transfer paperwork. As was mentioned already, if you wish to retain them, you will need to work with the county/counties to show the dissolution of the trust and how it was divided so they can assess the property meaning you will begin having the taxes in your name for your portion of the parcels. If you are interested in selling, it may be better to do so as a larger plot of land, but everyone needs to be on board first.

Author: Elizabeth_McBride
Date: 2025-02-03T18:05:26Z
Content: A Final Order for Increased Density was granted to Continental Resources for Section 32, Township 7 North, Range 6 West, Grady County, OK per documentation sent to us because of our lease.   Since then, our lease has expired.  Did any activity ever happen?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-02-03T18:20:13Z
Content: Your lease may not have expired if production is still in progress.  Leases have a primary term (usually about three years in OK) in which an operator may drill. Author: mjacobson
Date: 2025-01-28T01:23:31Z
Content: On the Texas Unclaimed Property site, I discovered that there are a number of royalty payments due to my deceased husband from wells and/or property his family owned.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-01-28T14:54:24Z
Content: Do you have any paperwork that has clues to the descriptions with a county, operator, old check stubs, probate documents, etc.?  The property ID might help with the RCC maps, but if they are internal company IDs then it won’t.

Author: mjacobson
Date: 2025-02-02T19:30:57Z
Content: Thanks for the quick reply. I’ve been trying to find documentation, however I can’t find anything among his papers. The only info I have is the property IDs and Company name. Mostly Chevron, a few TEP Barnett, and two Sunoco. I’ll try reaching out to them.

Author: min4me
Date: 2025-02-12T21:44:12Z
Content: I just saw your post and am somewhat confused - who is asking for property info and division orders?

Author: ragruwell
Date: 2025-03-31T22:20:36Z
Content: I am in the same boat. The Texas Unclaimed Property (TUP) lists only Property ID and the Oil Company for my deceased grandmother’s unclaimed mineral royalties. First TUP only wanted proof of heirship which I provided, but recently TUP sent a letter requiring Legal Description and Division Order for her listed Property IDs.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-01T01:20:49Z
Content: The property id may be the oil company’s internal id, not a state well lease number.  Some counties on Texasfile have limited years available.  Did you also look under your grandmother’s maiden name and for her parents?  Was your grandmother (or parents) from another state and the royalties were remitted to Texas because it was her address?

Author: ragruwell
Date: 2025-04-01T20:42:08Z
Content: Thanks for your reply. Turns out the Property ID is simply the record ID within the TUP database, and therefore has no relation to the original mineral royalty info.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-04-01T21:09:40Z
Content: Do you now the name of the well in OK?  We may be able to help with the current operator.  Did you check unclaimed funds in Iowa as well?  Probably was filed in TX since the operator was in TX.  It sometimes takes multiple tries at the TX office.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-04-02T23:36:33Z
Content: Under the uniform rules of unclaimed property, the funds are supposed to be filed with the state of residence of the last known owner. If they don’t know where your grandmother lived, then, typically, it goes to the state where the property is located.

Author: Tombstone7805
Date: 2025-01-18T19:21:49Z
Content: I Own a majority interest in a small land parcel in Karnes County, TX with an undivided interest. Looking for legal advice and assistance on petitioning the court for a sale while retaining my current separate mineral interest.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-01-18T21:33:38Z
Content: In Texas you can separate the mineral rights from the surface estate by a deed filed of record in the local County Clerks Office in the County where the property is located. You can also sell your undivided interest without going to court. You can sell your undivided interest to anyone. Try selling your interest to the others that own the other part. Or buy them out.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-01-19T21:21:06Z
Content: It would be wise to get an attorney involved in order to sever mineral interest from the surface estate.  One wrong word can nullify your intentions.  The forum cannot give legal advice.  There are several attorneys listed in the Directories tab above.  You do not need to go to court unless something unusual is involved.  The attorney will let you know if that is the case.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-01-24T02:03:53Z
Content: @Tombstone7805you mention petitioning the Court regarding a sale, is there some impediment related to the property that requires a Court approval? Maintaining your mineral interest is a simple process that can be accomplished by executing a “Surface Only” deed. Most attorneys can assist you with this process.

Topic: Change of language on division order

Author: mineralinterested
Date: 2025-04-02T20:28:14Z
Content: We received a division order and amended it as it went against our lease terms. Though we provided documentation, the operator didn’t accept change and sent a new DO to sign. Our lawyer suggested not fighting this term, and we agreed as it probably wouldn’t effect our royalties.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-04-02T20:31:56Z
Content: Which state?  If you are in Oklahoma you are not required to signanydivision order.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-04-02T20:45:33Z
Content: Texas division order language is 91.402 of Natural Resources Code - see link below.  The DO should include statement in all capitals “THIS AGREEMENT DOES NOT AMEND ANY LEASE OR OPERATING AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE INTEREST OWNERS AND THE LESSEE OR OPERATOR OR ANY OTHER CONTRACTS FOR THE PURCHASE OF OIL OR GAS.”  If not, then you should insert.NATURAL RESOURCES CODE CHAPTER 91. PROVISIONS GENERALLY APPLICABLE

PROVISIONS GENERALLY APPLICABLE

rag_documents.title: RI Pooling and Ratification
rag_documents.content:
Topic: RI Pooling and Ratification

Author: bh77
Date: 2025-03-22T23:43:12Z
Content: Question…I am a royalty owner in Texas in a section of land that has some leases on it. I have been sent a ratification that some owners in a different section of land want to pool and do a directional well that goes from their land to where I have the RI. It sounds like a horizontal well but it is not for some reason. Those owners have not authorized pooling for their lease that is wanting to do this. I do not think I have to authorize this but your input is helpful. It seems like I should have a lease that I am already part of pool to that area vs a totally seperate lease that is just trying to access oil.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-23T13:22:38Z
Content: Normally a ratification is sent by an operator with respect to planned well operations.  You need to review the ratification and cover letter and make sure you understand the proposal before signing and agreeing.  More specific information about the existing unit and proposed well(s), operator and sections and county are needed for you to get responses.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-23T13:24:40Z
Content: What type of interest do you own?  Are you a mineral owner under a lease or do you own an NRPI with a need to act to be included?

Author: bh77
Date: 2025-03-23T22:43:38Z
Content: Thank you. In reviewing the leases that want me to pool my Royalty Interest (I am not a mineral owner) I am not part of their section of land and they have not authorized pooling in the lease.  The lease wants to drill and then access where I have Royalty Interest so they want me to allow pooling. I have other leases in my section where I own RI, and there are a couple other operators that could pool as well.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-24T13:20:56Z
Content: You need to see the planned path of the well along with the other documents.  Here is an example of a family that was asked to pool in the South half of the NE4 of a section. The blue well is a horizontal well, but could be shorter and a lesser angle and be directional.  The owners in the rest of the section needed the spacing to be changed to 640 acres because the new well was going to be a gas well.  They asked for a ratification from the owners in the green part to change their lease from 160 acre pooling option (red) to 640 (black).  That was reasonable.

Date: 2025-04-02T16:47:21Z
Content: Thank you for that information.Screenshot 2025-04-02 at 10.17.37 AM1116×818 50.6 KBI have attached an example of what they want to do.

rag_documents.title: Check depositing & Mailbox Services in Oklahoma
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Check depositing & Mailbox Services in Oklahoma

Author: Megan_H_L
Date: 2025-03-31T15:42:21Z
Content: I do not live in the state of Oklahoma but am looking for a service there that would receive my mail including royalty checks, OCC filings & mineral rights correspondence.  The checks would need to be deposited and all mail scanned and uploaded to me.  My accountant does this currently but I would like to find a professional service that can do just this for me while providing me with an OK mailing address.  Any suggestions?

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-03-31T19:39:19Z
Content: Why dont you just have them send all that info to your accountant? Guess Im saying, I dont see the point of settting up all this in Oklahoma if you dont live there?

Author: Megan_H_L
Date: 2025-03-31T20:02:10Z
Content: All of my mineral rights are there and are in an Oklahoma trust. There are other reasons as well but that’s a big part of it. Im also going to be changing my accountant, so I’m trying to plan ahead.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2025-04-01T02:36:33Z
Content: My guess is she is trying to get around the state withholding 5% for out of state owners. That forces them to file Oklahoma state tax returns to get that money back.

Author: Megan_H_L
Date: 2025-04-01T05:35:19Z
Content: Thank you for that helpful reply, Todd! I’m actually trustee for my mother’s trust and she resides in Oklahoma. As her trust already files taxes in OK, I didn’t know there was a 5% withholding for non-residents. I live part of the year outside the US and thus need help with my mail.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-04-01T15:32:57Z
Content: You need a Lockbox type service that can also handle documents. Contact Stephaniefirstapproach.com

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2025-04-01T15:33:33Z
Content: Glad I could be of help. Have you inquired from those parties sending checks if they offer Direct Deposit? Most do, but some don’t so that is a pain. Secondly, you might inquire at the bank that you use in Oklahoma if they can handle these things for you. Most do with a fee and if they are versed in oil & gas, they will know what to do with all of the OCC filings. Of course you can hire an accountant that is willing to do all these things for you and knows the oil & gas business. Asking them to handle affairs of the Trust could open them to liability that they don’t want.
Another option is a Minerals Management Company. I don’t know of any personally, but searching the internet should provide you several options to choose from. There may be some in the Directories tab at the top of this page. Good Luck.

Date: 2025-04-01T19:00:27Z
Content: My guess is she is trying to get around the state withholding 5% for out of state owners. That forces them to file Oklahoma state tax returns to get that money back.

Date: 2025-04-02T13:08:01Z
Content: I am absolutely not interested in doing anything illegal or that would put me in the crosshairs of the IRS or OK tax authorities.  Right now, the trust’s beneficiary is an OK resident and all is on the up-and-up.  However, because of my cross-border residency, I am already planning for the not-too-distant future when I will inherit the mineral rights from my mother and am speaking to a few different OK attorneys.  I do need an accountant that is very well-versed in Oil & Gas and has international experience.  My current CPA is fine but not for the next step. Nearly all of my checks are already on ACH but I still get 4-5 a month from operators that are old school.

Topic: SKIM on Revenue Statement

Author: Mary_Cooper_Gilliam
Date: 2025-03-27T14:32:46Z
Content: This is the first time I have seen this on a Revenue Statement in 30 years. The new company is Diversified Productions, who are unreachable.
Can someone shed some light on what it is
Mary Gilliam

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-27T17:15:10Z
Content: Think of skimming the fat off of the top of your pot of chicken stock!

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-03-27T23:17:51Z
Content: Most probably, the situation with “skim” as to your well is tied to the operator taking any oil / condensate that is in the water tanks on location (which will rise to the top of the water column) and is reporting that as production and selling that volume.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-27T23:46:20Z
Content: Better that they are skimming and selling it and reporting to the mineral owners. When I was a roustabout, I heard stories of skim being stolen.

Author: Mary_Cooper_Gilliam
Date: 2025-03-28T15:37:00Z
Content: Many thanks for the replies. I have never had it with other companies. I have oil that does come out of these gas wells but always noted as oil and in greater amount.

Author: Kitchen
Date: 2025-04-01T14:14:56Z
Content: At least they are paying you for skim oil! I’ve had operators in the past that stole it and then lost a class action suit on it a few years later and had to pay. I still don’t trust them as we haven’t seen a skim oil check in years. Water disposal volumes are still at normal levels, so did the oil magically stop flowing?!

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-04-01T14:46:24Z
Content: Presence of skim oil in the water tanks may be tied to some inefficiencies with the separator unit (i.e. not getting all the oil out of the water leg). Which may be tied to some different on-site operator efficiencies and tweaking of the equipment.

rag_documents.title: Thoughts on Negotiations
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Thoughts on Negotiations

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-01-01T12:07:37Z
Content: I have been participating in this forum for a while now and I wanted to offer some thoughts on negotiations. Some background: I started as a landman in 1981, developed a mineral consulting practice as well as a revenue enhancement consulting practice, started developing my mineral portfolio in 1982, and have been a party to multiple property purchases/sales. I have solely focused on managing my mineral portfolio for the last 28 years.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-01-01T22:09:47Z
Content: And take it easy on the poor guys/girls that work in accounting/division orders that constanly get chastised by “know it all mineral owners that have no idea what they really own” for not knowing how do their job when they call in griping about 1.9 vs 2.0 net mineral acres.  They are only going off what the title opinion/system says and doing their best to keep their job and keep a roof over their head.

Author: AJ11
Date: 2025-01-03T14:45:26Z
Content: How often will an oil company agree to something like an unmodified Producer’s 88 it readily uses to lease minerals when leasing its own minerals to another oil company? I may be in la la land, but, for me, there would be ethical concerns about employing a “caveat lessor” approach which incentivizes treating unsophisticated or otherwise challenged mineral owners far differently–to their detriments–than more sophisticated and empowered ones.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-01-03T18:08:59Z
Content: Dealing with lease brokers is not always a pleasurable experience. A lot of mineral owners do not own enough minerals to justify hiring an oil and gas attorney. A lot of local attorneys don’t know much more than the mineral owner. If you can deal with the “In House” company landman usually it is better. Eliminate the middle man that is trying to make himself look good to the company.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-01-03T18:10:36Z
Content: Caveat Lessor would be lessor beware, which is excellent advice. There are consumer statutes that apply when a professional is dealing with a consumer/non-professional. Unfortunately, some people fail to adhere to these limitations. Additionally, many mineral owners do not know what language to listen for or the questions to ask in order to focus the negotiations.

Author: mmccabe77
Date: 2025-01-03T22:01:13Z
Content: Between NARO and TIPRO, which is the most useful for expanding one’s understanding of mineral ownership in Texas?

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-01-03T22:02:29Z
Content: There are a lot of people and mineral owners without much experience that have jobs and work too. Their minerals and assets, their families are important to them also. They might need the money as fast as they can get it! It’s their right!

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-01-03T22:36:28Z
Content: The are both good organizations. TIPRO will be more focused on the producer, but will provide helpful information. NARO is a mineral owner group, so it will offer more in the area of successful mineral management protocols. If you can only choose one, then I would suggest NARO.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-01-03T23:31:42Z
Content: I believe it is safe to assume that the vast majority of mineral owners have jobs. If the assets and the funds are important, then they deserve the requisite attention prior to a decision. Generally, fast as you can is what leads to poorer results. But we can disagree.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-01-04T22:45:59Z
Content: There are a lot of people and mineral owners without much experience that have jobs and work too. Their minerals and assets, their families are important to them also. They might need the money as fast as they can get it! It’s their right!

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-01-04T22:47:18Z
Content: I will echo what Bob77 said. There are posts on here, where knowledgeable people give solid advice, but then others think it is just better to send a mean threatening letter by certified mail. Worse, then people love that or press the heart button.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-01-05T17:41:02Z
Content: A company can spend 20 million dollars on drilling and completing a well and not have all the mineral owners leased prior to including them in a unit! Or have incorrect title. There are a lot more mineral owners than oil and gas companies. People simply want their money! Would you buy a tract of land and build a house and not have a “clean correct title”?

Author: SteveCo
Date: 2025-01-05T21:52:29Z
Content: Kind of disagree here. Sending a request or communication via certified mail is important, especially if the differences lead to litigation. Nothing about it has to be mean or rude, it is meant to ensure your requests for communication regarding whatever matter you have are not ignored, and that they cannot claim ignorance of the mistakes later. At the end of the day, this is a business, and we all need to protect ourselves.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2025-01-05T21:53:01Z
Content: The oil companies hire the best title attorneys around to figure out who owns what.  Do they make mistakes? Sure, but youre acting like its common practice for title opinions to be wrong, which I simply disagree with.  The majority of the issues Ive seen on this board are people being deeded/probated a 1/16th interest under the NE4, so then they think thats what they own and no matter how its explained by the board, attorneys or the operators accounting/division orders, they wont take no for an answer.  But they dont factor in prior title, so that 1/16th is often the 1/16th of a 1/4 interest owned 60 years ago and of course it ticks people off when they start thinking of the money they are about to make.  As far as buying a house, youre comparing apples to oranges, its 1,000,000 easier to determine the ownership of surface vs minerals.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-01-05T21:53:05Z
Content: The example you give is for new wells. 90% of the people on here who are having issues involve wells that have been producing for years, or they are the third or fourth generation removed from the lessor.
I will also suggest many of these problems are because the prior generations didn’t provide the company with probate orders or deeds. So, it is not the company trying to keep the mineral owner’s money, it is lack of information available to the company because prior generations dropped the ball.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-01-05T21:53:09Z
Content: It is the job of the landmen, lease brokers and title attorneys to complete their jobs in a timely manner and not take months and months stalling to keep from paying. They ought to be called out on it!

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-01-06T00:29:44Z
Content: Companies do not take a certified letter as rude. It is considered just as any other communication. Sure there can be statutory reasons you may want to use a certified vs email, but today it just takes longer to get in the Q. By all means you should protect your interest

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-01-06T00:29:48Z
Content: understand and you have a valid point. I should have phrased my response better.
My main point is if somebody isn’t getting paid, just sending  certified mail, jumping up and down  and demanding payment doesn’t serve any purpose. The first step is to determine if the company has the person in title, are there requirements or is there anything the company doesn’t have to make sure the owner gets put in pay status.

Author: SteveCo
Date: 2025-01-06T00:29:59Z
Content: Exactly.  Without prompting from the mineral owner, the oil companies suffer no inconvenience by keeping funds in suspense. And there are many more issues that arise outide of just title opinions. Chastising a mineral owner for speaking up and wanting a timely resolution is a bit much,  calling such resolution “threatening” or some form of yelling is incongruous with the purpose of this board at the bare minimum. Forums like this, and organizations like NARO exist only because so many people have been taken advantage of

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-01-06T19:04:28Z
Content: Not sure what you mean by clean correct title. It is poor practice that 100% of all owners be leased prior to drilling, but it is not required. The fallout from such a practice can lead to diminished returns for the oil company for many reasons. With that said, there can be business/economic reasons to proceed in this manner. My experience when someone drills on one of our properties without leasing (or force pooling where applicable) us first generally leads to much better economic options for us.

Author: Louisiana52
Date: 2025-03-31T13:58:29Z
Content: Location: Harrison county, WV
Last year we were approached by Eastern Gas Transmission. They informed us that there an old mineral rights contract on the property, that they were working on getting a permit to drill, sign an updated lease agreement or be pooled, blah blah.  We did and got a small benefit.
I just found out that a permits has been issued to Diversified Production LLC and the proposed well seems to go across our property. I’m trying to determine

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-31T14:47:01Z
Content: Very common.  No, they do not have to notify you unless that clause is in your lease contract.  Many operators hire leasing agents to lease for them and then transfer the lease to them.  Also, many operators have additional working interest partners in a well and you may have leased with one of the partners.  The operator has to abide by your lease.  I wouldn’t worry about it.

Author: Kathy_Mounts

Date: 2025-03-06T16:51:27Z

had no idea who they were, which of my leases they bought from whom. I went to Enverus which showed Apache deposits  stopped at end of year and Hilcorp deposit posted in Feb. there was no Jan. Deposit posted. I don’t know if they bought all or some of my Apache wells.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-06T18:30:16Z
Content: It is not uncommon for there to be a one month delay in getting new openers and wells into the accounting system.  It is excellent that you are already in pay.  Look at check detail for Dec Apache check and Feb Hilcorp check and compare wells and production months.  There may not be a gap between last oil or gas month paid by Apache and first month paid by Hilcorp. May be easiest to use spreadsheet with lines for each well and columns to oil, gas and products listing production month.  Keep in mind that some companies pay all production for same month and others pay different months for oil vs gas and products.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-06T21:57:29Z
Content: If the Hilcorp check has production month immediately succeeding the production month on the last Apache check, then you are fully paid.  Sometimes the first check from new operator will cover multiple months.  You can only determine this by reviewing and comparing the check detail.

Author: Chris_Cusack
Date: 2025-03-11T20:25:20Z
Content: Yeah, I got the same letter from Hilcorp and notification from Apache.  Poor communication all around. I sent an email and have not heard back about the missing income.  They will be paying interest.

Author: Mineral_Owner5

Date: 2025-03-11T21:13:17Z

As a mineral owner, I am small potatoes to these oil firms with few rights so its just’ hope for the best’

rag_documents.title: Mineral rights new and don't know where to begin
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Mineral rights new and don't know where to begin

Author: Abbelynn
Date: 2025-03-21T20:06:43Z
Content: Okay, brief background, my father passed away many years ago when I was very young, no siblings, father also had no sibs, my mother, widowed and never remarried, she passed away a couple of years ago.  Right before she died we had received several phone calls from what I thought at the time was a solicitor or bill collector and I didnt return the calls, I finally answered the call after theyd called several times and was told I was speaking with an attorney’s office about mineral rights claims as the heir of my father. My mother was in hospice and died a few days after that call and the name and number got lost in the shuffle afterwards. I have tried to look into this since but I’m at a total loss. This is out of Oklahoma and there are 2 parcels of land that had been granted to my great grandfather and grandfather,  one is in Ottawa County and the other is Texas County.  Ive been on the OCC site and found there is an active natural gas well on the land in Texas County thats been actively producing since 1946. The API is 3513900471, Operator is. 23138 and name is Lois, well 1. From what I’ve read, you can inherit mineral rights but not actually own the property, at least that’s what I think is a possibility but I really have no clue and I’m totally lost at the present point. I wouldn’t think that someone would have been trying so hard to contact me regarding this if I wasn’t eligible, but I don’t know that for certain. Im sorry for the lengthy explanation but I wanted to get the pertinent details in there. If anyone can please tell me if im wasting my time or if I’m on the right track, and if so, where do I go from here? Thanks in advance for any help or advice at all. To be honest, it would be a much needed bit of assistance if there’s anything from this because after Covid things have gone quite badly and it would be a genuine miracle if there is any money due, although things like this never happen to me so i will not be surprised if there isn’t,  but I am ever hopeful and working hard to try and turn the tides of fortune to better days! Thanks to any who may help and hopes that all have a lovely day.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-21T21:36:59Z
Content: Mineral rights and surface rights are both real property in Oklahoma and in most States. You can own minerals and not own surface as well as the opposite. This is termed a severed mineral interest. Scout Energy is the operator of the well this their owner relations emailownerrelations@scoutep.com. Contact them with your information and ask if they have your relatives as owners and explain your situation. They should be able to provide basic information to get you started. Scout is generally slow to respond, so be diligent. Check for your relatives in OK unclaimed property also as well as the State where they resided. Good luck. Check back if you need more help.Screenshot 2025-03-21 at 1.35.11 PM1015×622 66.1 KB

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-22T02:37:39Z
Content: This well is still producing, so you need to check the unclaimed funds at the OK Treasurer’s office and also contact the operator as James has suggested.OTC Lois 1 info.pdf(428.5 KB)

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-03-24T20:27:00Z
Content: Sorry for your losses.  Reaching out to the companies producing would be a good place to start.  Ask what is needed to get your minerals into “pay status”.  In Oklahoma this usually requires a probate.

Author: Abbelynn
Date: 2025-03-25T19:29:43Z
Content: Thank you so much for your response and the helpful tips on what else to check. I have checked the unclaimed funds under my name and my relatives and hadnt found anything.  Does that mean definitively there isn’t anything? Or I may not be searching under the right person?

Author: Abbelynn
Date: 2025-03-25T19:29:48Z
Content: Thank you so much for all the great information and I’m going to be contacting Scout right away.

Author: Abbelynn
Date: 2025-03-26T01:51:46Z
Content: Thank you very much for your reply and the great tips on where to begin.  I live in Illinois and I have some of the land information from genealogy research I’d been doing.  I’m going to get started with contacting the Scout energy and looking over what records I have on the land. Is this something that I can do myself or do I need to hire an attorney or land man or both? It seems like I could easily get lost or taken advantage of by not knowing the legalities of all that’s required, and where should I start with that? Thank you again for your help, and im sorry to bombard you with more questions! Have a great day.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-03-26T19:57:00Z
Content: Probably just no unclaimed property.  This must be paid in if in the hands of the producer for X number of years.  This varies by state.  So there could be money payable currently that doesn’t currently show up in unclaimed property.  Check in your relative’s home state as well as Oklahoma.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-03-26T23:43:57Z
Content: Learn as much as you can from the land records before engaging a professional.    You also may want to search for probate records of ancestors.  There are two tools in Oklahoma:

Author: A_Monty
Date: 2025-03-27T16:47:06Z
Content: No, it doesn’t mean nothing is there. You can call and talk to someone in unclaimed property and they can search. For Oklahoma it’s (405) 521-4273 Office Hours: 8am to 5pm Mon-Fri. Have everyone names and Soc. Sec. numbers if at all possible. (I’ve known them to find things I could not from an online search.)
Meanwhile, keep following all of Martha and Richard’s advice.

Author: Abbelynn
Date: 2025-03-27T19:05:14Z
Content: I was able to find the Petition for Probate of Will for George E. Leonard filed 9/13/1928 in Texas County Oklahoma filed by his widow Sarah P. Leonard. It states he had filed a will on January 26, 1920. There’s an order admitting the will to Probate filed 9/26/1928. There’s a copy of the will, and an order Setting Date for Final Settlement dated 2/1/1929.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-28T01:29:54Z
Content: Congratulations on your research skills. Good luck on your journey.

Author: Abbelynn
Date: 2025-03-29T02:50:47Z
Content: Thank you. I feel like each thing I find brings up 3 new questions. So the Will and Probate records I found are for the original land owner, George E. Leonard, my GG Grandfather and per those records he left everything, including that parcel of land to his wife, my GG Grandmother, Sarah P. Leonard. Do I need to search for subsequent records of Wills and Probate for each consecutive owner then? Search for records of a Will for Sarah, then for whoever inherited after Sarah, etc.? I believe that I have found some of the title records as well, but I am not sure exactly what I am looking for.  There are entries showing where the land was mortgaged and then paid off, then ownership transferred to heirs. I’m sorry if I’m driving you crazy with questions, but I really do appreciate all of your help and guidance.  I’ve found out more in the past week than I have in the last year. Thank you so, so much.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-31T13:58:39Z
Content: In order to properly chain the title from four GG GF, then you must follow the subsequent documents until they come into you. You are following the mineral title, so follow those issues rather than the surface once the minerals are severed from the surface rights. On a practical basis, you do nort need to follow mtg related issues for this type of title chain.

Content: Ive gone through quite a few leases and each one can be different. in my latest lease agreement, i offerred zero signing bonus for a higher percentage and that didnt happen AT ALL. I ended up with their signing bonus but i did happen to get ZERO COST. i dont know how that happened but its the only lease that i got that on. Date: 2025-03-28T13:49:04Z
Content: I would keep pushing for 20%. The group you are talking to is most likely flipping your lease and wanting to keep an override.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-29T00:04:48Z
Content: The lessee is unlikely to give you effective ‘no cost’ lease language as it not to their advantage.  It is up to you to propose any changes to the lease form or to present your own form.  Leases are complex and interpretation of clauses are affected by state law and cases.

Date: 2025-03-31T07:51:58Z
Content: I only accept 25% royalty.  Why is the bonus so low?  I have gone unleased in many cases when the bonus is low.  I end up with 100% royalties less production costs.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-31T13:10:45Z
Content: Brenda, Lease rates and bonus vary widely across US, and even within a county due to geology and potential production.  Presumably the poster owns very little acreage.  Different states have different laws for payout for nonparticipating minerals.  Texas is 100% of costs on a well by well basis.  New Mexico sets a penalty of 200% to 300%, and I think it may include all wells under a pooling order.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-30T18:40:06Z
Content: You have cut off multiple columns of the data lines, including the commodities.  If you post well information, then it is easier to review.

Author: Randy_M

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-30T22:04:28Z
Content: There are 5 new Neff wells.  The gas is being reported to CONG under each RRC lease id.  The gas purchaser is reporting all the gas for the 5 wells under the single RRC lease id.  The purchaser is likely transporting and measuring at a common combined point and does not know how the gas volumes are allocated back to the individual wells.  So it reports as a combined total to a single well.

rag_documents.title: Continental's Jackrabbit 1308A Hanging on
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Continental's Jackrabbit 1308A Hanging on

Author: Charlie9806
Date: 2025-03-26T12:16:21Z
Content: The production has steadily gone down to very little since the Fall of 2024, the same year it was drilled. I looked on the RRC website, and it shows the drilling permit has problems and is currently unapproved and in Engineering status. On the CONG website, drilling permit#895891, shows little production for the past several months. Are these connected or is the well just not a good producer? This is Continental Resources.

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-03-27T19:57:31Z
Content: Despite the multiple permits, only one lateral has been drilled at the Jackrabbit well (API 42-495-34927). Based on the directional survey (public record via Tx RRC site), this was a 10,428’ lateral that had a TVD of 10,360’ at the heel and 10,428[’ TVD at the toe. It is interesting that the TVD of the lateral dropped to about 10,770’ in the middle of the lateral (about 5000’ out). Why was this done? May be following the structure in this area along the 10,000’ lateral path. Or the lateral path may have been adjusted to “get back into target zone”. No way of knowing what the operator’s intent was for this type of information.

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-03-27T23:18:45Z
Content: No way this Jackrabbit can be a multi-lateral well. This could only occur if these were open hole completions with no casing that didn’t require casing (and stimulation). An example of that would the naturally fractured Austin Chalk in South Texas.

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-03-27T23:19:02Z
Content: Last comment on this AJ 11 post - I am 99.9% confident in saying that Continental would not purposefully “slow down” production from this or any other wellbore as they wait on the determination of any ongoing, pending or planned protest. They still need to make money and as much production as is feasibly possible without focusing on things that are beyond their control.

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-03-27T23:19:15Z
Content: After looking at the reported production data, I would have to say that this is just a bad well. The increase from Aug 24 to Sept 24 was probably tied to installing tubing in the wellbore to increase annular velocity (and thereby increase production rate).

Author: Charlie9806
Date: 2025-03-28T12:24:20Z
Content: Thank you!
I hope the Bullsnake in Sec. 14 that they are currently drilling and the following one they plan on drilling in Sec. 15 don’t run into these problems. But it’s interesting to know the challenges of drilling wells.

Author: Rock_Man
Date: 2025-03-29T19:14:39Z
Content: Only know that well was spud on March 10th and rig is still on location

rag_documents.content:
Topic: Los Angeles City Lot Mineral Rights Determination

Author: websurf700
Date: 2025-03-25T14:38:35Z
Content: Hello, Where can you find out what mineral rights you have for a house lot in LA City?

Author: PeteR
Date: 2025-03-25T16:31:03Z
Content: @websurf700, you would have to check the county records,
probably all the way back to statehood, and see if any previous owner sold, retained or otherwise transferred or assigned the mineral rights for your portion of your section-township-range.
If nobody ever did anything with the mineral rights and you are the fee owner of your surface lot, then you would also have the
mineral rights.  Typically in a housing development the builder or developer will retain the mineral rights if they are available
and the residence owner will not obtain the mineral rights, but
you won’t know until you check.  You can use the California
Oil & Gas Gis maphttps://maps.conservation.ca.gov/doggr/wellfinder/to find your section-Township-Range.  (Something like
27-1S-13W).

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-26T01:52:04Z
Content: This will be an extensive search in the old records at the Recorder’s Office in Norwalk. The old records are a combination of Grantor/Grantee indexes maintained in hard copy books and microfiche/film. The more current day transactions are maintained on computer, but they are still grantor/grantee based.

rag_documents.title: TX mineral rights claim, will, descendants
rag_documents.content:
Topic: TX mineral rights claim, will, descendants

Author: mwillse
Date: 2025-03-27T23:17:05Z
Content: I would like to know some Texas legal rights.  I discovered a distant relative that left some mineral rights in Reeves County TX.  I informed my family about it and how we are related.  We agreed we had equal shares split 6 ways from our grand mother.  who passed away about 26 years ago.  When she passed away there was no knowledge of any mineral rights  and my cousins were granted 2/3 of estate since their parents had passed away.  They were in their 30’s at the time.  My mother passed away 9 years ago and left them 20% of her estate.  The probate on these was closed and did not cover any mineral rights.  My cousin summited a letter of administration with out telling us in Maryland adding mineral rights to my grandmothers will so instead of receiving 18% each they received 25% and we received 8%.  I get its immoral, but was it legal?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-28T00:02:55Z
Content: Without a specific will provision, the minerals would pass under the rest and residue clause of your grandmother’s will.  For example, if she left her estate to her 3 children in equal shares and 2 died before her, then the 1/3 for each deceased child would go to his or her children.  Your mother as living child A got her 1/3 and the grandchildren under deceased child B would get 1/3 and grandchildren under deceased child C would get 1/3.  When your mother died, her 1/3 would pass in accordance with the terms of her will, which you say left 20% of 1/3 to your cousins and 80% of 1/3 to you and your siblings.  If there had not been any wills, then the Texas minerals would pass per Texas intestacy law.  The exact percentage to each person depends on the number of siblings.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-16T17:15:55Z
Content: Your point highlights the need to state the full name of a company when asking about its reputation or information.  It can make a difference if it has an LLC, LP or Inc at the end.  Landmen sometimes form a new entity for leasing an area on behalf of an operator because the operator has done a lot of analysis and research and wants to lease without tipping its hand and having third parties take advantage of the operator’s work.

rag_documents.title: Oklahoma mineral acreage
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Oklahoma mineral acreage

Author: season
Date: 2025-03-25T18:53:25Z
Content: I have a mineral deed for Stephens County, OK that lists ownership in Township 1 North, Range 4 West Section 10 SW/4 SE/4, NW/4 NW4, N/2 SW/4 NW/4, SW/4 SW/4. I was approached by a landman wanted to lease my property, but I don’t have any records of the number of acres the ownership includes. How can I find this?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-25T19:39:33Z
Content: Welcome to the forum.The easiest way is to ask the landman which parcel or it he wants to lease all parcels and how many net acres he is carrying for you.  If he/she doesn’t know, then they have not run the title yet.  Is the deed in your name or an ancestor’s?

Author: season
Date: 2025-03-26T01:52:19Z
Content: Actually the deed was conveyed from a trust to the nonprofit organization I work for. The legal document only lists a “schedule” of properties that just lists the property as follows:
Township 1 South, Range 4 West
.
Section 1: N/2 NW/4 SE/4, SE/4 NW/4 SE/4, NE/4 SE/4, E/2 SE/4 SE/4, N/2 NW/4
SE/4, SE/4 NW /4 SE/4
Section 10: NW/4 NW/4
Section 12: E/2, North 17.5 acres of the SE/4 NE/4

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2025-03-26T12:48:25Z
Content: Make sure that the nonprofit address and description of acres are filed in the county courthouse. Section 10 had a pooling case listed in 2024.  Continental planned to drill a well.  No order yet. Case 2024-000995.  You will need to be ready to answer the pooling in 20 days from the date of the order.  Many of us would pick the highest royalty option. Author: GT2
Date: 2025-03-19T00:09:07Z
Content: Is it common to have an appraised value on a well when there are no well logs and no royalties being paid?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-19T18:02:51Z
Content: You need to post a more detailed question, including the state and county.  Are you a mineral owner who is not in pay and why (such as title issue or not received a division order or in process of transferring mineral ownership).  When was the well completed and started producing?  If you identify the well, then you will get the best answer.

Author: Steve_Durrett
Date: 2025-03-20T00:06:08Z
Content: If this is for an estate valuation, the appraisal should be as of the date of death, without taking into account any additional information that may have become available later, including logs and payment/production history.

Author: GT2
Date: 2025-03-21T21:52:33Z
Content: Garza County, Texas.  I have a tax statement with an appraised value and have not received royalties on the well in a couple of years.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-22T01:25:16Z
Content: Look at the statement and see what year or years are included.  If for 2024, you should have received a Notice of Appraised Value last year and had to protest within 30 days.  Is the well still producing?  If so, contact the operator and get in pay.  If not, then in 2025 the value should be zero and you can protest any value.

Author: DPerson

Content: be sure to take advantage of the low production tax cut if you are in Texas

Author: robertsonjennifer
Date: 2025-03-17T01:30:54Z
Content: Can undivided mineral rights be separated on a deed?  If four owners are listed on a deed can we get a new separate deed for each person so we can all do what we want separately?

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-17T21:17:34Z
Content: you can do what you want separately now without preparing new deeds. You are not joined together.

Author: zconlin
Date: 2025-03-17T23:38:49Z
Content: I don’t think thats the way it works.  You all own an undivided interest in for example 40 acres of land.  You already are able to do as you please individually with your own mineral interest, you just don’t each own 4 separate 10 acre tracts within the 40

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2025-03-17T23:40:23Z
Content: The answer is dependent on the wording on the deed. Are the Grantees listed as joint tenants, as tenants in common or some other designation?

Author: chandlerwall
Date: 2025-03-19T15:32:26Z
Content: Typically, undivided mineral interests are already yours to manage as you see fit, especially if the deed transfers the property to each of you four individually. However, if the deed lists you as joint tenants or tenants in common, you share rights to the same undivided interest. In this case, you would need a new deed to further divide the interests.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-03-19T16:15:48Z
Content: That doesn’t have anything to do with that question.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-19T16:26:10Z
Content: Todd and Chandlerwall did bring up a good point with the question. If the owners are joint tenants, they will have to sever the joint tenancy by a deed.

Author: robertsonjennifer
Date: 2025-03-20T00:05:28Z
Content: No, not tenants in common.  “Grantees” the rights came from a trust.
Thanks

Author: ShawnMichelle
Date: 2025-03-23T00:24:20Z
Content: Hi Todd, I own a share in 10 undivided acres through inheritance. Where can I find a copy of the original deed? How does one divide the property?

Author: Mikro1TX
Date: 2025-03-23T03:16:40Z
Content: As I understand it. Multiple people/entities can own a % of the same 10 acre tract. If that is the case, it is divided by percentage of the whole 10 acres. So someone or some group may own an undivided 45% and that may be broken down by more percentages of that 45%. Another person/or group may own say 32% and that may be broken down in whatever percentage based on the number of persons or groups for that 32%. All of this pertaining to the same 10 acre tract until 100% of the total of users/persons/groups own all of the 100%. So in a case of 4 individuals owning an undivided/equal shares of a 10 acre tract. They each have 25% of what ever the percentage is that applies only to them under what ever percentage of who they are part of for lack of better terminology.  Example. In one section, myself and siblings each own 25% of an undivided 228 acres, of which we participate with others of a group that owns 26% of that same 228 acres. Where, we as undivided owners actually own only 6% as our whole percentage then broken into 25% each of that, of the 26% of the 100% of the 228 acres. With that we are Grantees. Now whether there are co-tenants or whatever I have no idea? My deed shows me as a grantee with 25% of 6% of 26% of 100% of the 228 acres tract. It says it in a different way, but the gist of it is just that.  I hope that makes sense? Just the way I have been told about minerals and how it applies to me and my siblings. MK

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2025-03-23T16:52:35Z
Content: The “deed” should be of record in the county clerk’s or recorder’s office for the county/state where the minerals are located.
The term “undivided” can be misleading to the novice. It refers to not being able to specifically identify one interest from the another. First, you must know the size of the whole tract to determine your interest in that tract. An example would be you own a 1/10th undivided interest in a 100 acre, or 10.00 undivided mineral acres. You can go anywhere in that 100 acre tract and you own 1/10th. You can’t divide the 100 acres into 10 equal parts for you to identify “your” 10 acres, unless you have everyone that owns in the 100 acre tract, sign the deeds to subdivide the 100 acre tract. That is often called a partition deed.
If you have access to the document that shows you the legal description of your “inheritance”, and if you want to provide the legal description to the forum, someone on here may be able to give you more information. Hope this helps at least a little bit.

Author: robertsonjennifer
Date: 2025-03-23T22:41:50Z
Content: 765 ILCS 520/1) (from Ch. 96 1/2, par. 4901)
Sec. 1. posts.author: Mikro1TX
posts.content: As I understand it. Multiple people/entities can own a % of the same 10 acre tract. If that is the case, it is divided by percentage of the whole 10 acres. So someone or some group may own an undivided 45% and that may be broken down by more percentages of that 45%. Another person/or group may own say 32% and that may be broken down in whatever percentage based on the number of persons or groups for that 32%. All of this pertaining to the same 10 acre tract until 100% of the total of users/persons/groups own all of the 100%. So in a case of 4 individuals owning an undivided/equal shares of a 10 acre tract. They each have 25% of what ever the percentage is that applies only to them under what ever percentage of who they are part of for lack of better terminology.  Example. In one section, myself and siblings each own 25% of an undivided 228 acres, of which we participate with others of a group that owns 26% of that same 228 acres. Where, we as undivided owners actually own only 6% as our whole percentage then broken into 25% each of that, of the 26% of the 100% of the 228 acres. With that we are Grantees. Now whether there are co-tenants or whatever I have no idea? My deed shows me as a grantee with 25% of 6% of 26% of 100% of the 228 acres tract. It says it in a different way, but the gist of it is just that.  I hope that makes sense? Just the way I have been told about minerals and how it applies to me and my siblings. MK

posts.author: TODD_M_Baker
posts.content:
The “deed” should be of record in the county clerk’s or recorder’s office for the county/state where the minerals are located.
The term “undivided” can be misleading to the novice. It refers to not being able to specifically identify one interest from the another. First, you must know the size of the whole tract to determine your interest in that tract. An example would be you own a 1/10th undivided interest in a 100 acre, or 10.00 undivided mineral acres. You can go anywhere in that 100 acre tract and you own 1/10th. You can’t divide the 100 acres into 10 equal parts for you to identify “your” 10 acres, unless you have everyone that owns in the 100 acre tract, sign the deeds to subdivide the 100 acre tract. That is often called a partition deed.
If you have access to the document that shows you the legal description of your “inheritance”, and if you want to provide the legal description to the forum, someone on here may be able to give you more information. Hope this helps at least a little bit.

Author: Mikro1TX
Date: 2025-03-23T18:16:49Z
Content: To those here that know more. What happens to an ORRI in New Mexico that is with BLM land? My understanding of leases that also have an ORRI for some, the ORRI is only enforce while the lease is Active and Producing or HBP? Once those are “NOT” in place, then the ORRI expires, unlike other Royalty interest which the lease holder owns in perpetuity ( as long as the taxes are paid ) or sells the minerals to someone else. Does this apply to New Mexico and BLM land? MK

Author: CanadianTuxedo
Date: 2025-03-24T17:24:45Z
Content: Not sure of your specific curiosity here but the BLM and SLO (State Land Office) do execute leases and the lessees of those leases can burden their revenue by retaining and/or conveying over-riding royalty under the leases. There are various limitations when working with BLM/SLO leases but generally speaking their leases can have an ORRI. You are correct in that the ORRI can expire as it is a burden on the leasehold revenue which would expire when the lease(s) are no longer in effect/expire. Does this help?

Author: Mikro1TX

Content: Yes ,thank you for your response to this. It answers my question. Again many thanks. MK

Topic: Capital Gains

Author: jtarbutton
Date: 2025-03-21T21:54:11Z
Content: I sold an interest I had inherited. I have no idea how to calculate the cost basis of the interest at the time of inheritance. I’d be grateful for any suggestions or into. Thanks.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-21T23:09:18Z
Content: You will have to establish the value at the time of death in order to claim a step up basis.

Author: TayNeatCPA
Date: 2025-03-22T00:45:08Z
Content: CAD values are usually lower than actual, but could serve as a good starting point. It’s important to note that your basis will be decreased a depletion is claimed.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-22T01:20:49Z
Content: It would have to be CAD value at date of death which may be very hard to find after more than 5 years.  Better to look at probate records or federal estate return form 706 to see estate value.  The value may have been negligible if inherited at a time when oil prices were very low and there was no drilling.

Author: mineralsjb2009
Date: 2025-03-22T19:17:51Z
Content: I’m not an accountant and this is not tax advice. However, we’ve always used the price of oil when you inherited vs when you sell. For example, if you sold for $1,000,000.00 when oil was $80 and you inherited when oil was $40 then you could use the step up basis at $500K. This could give a reasonable estimate and the IRS will generally accept the reported cost basis if it is reasonable and calculated using relevant historical data. However , if they were to push back or you were to get audited, you could be required to conduct a formal valuation of the value at the time of inheritance.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-22T19:49:40Z
Content: That may have worked, but it is not in compliance with federal tax law.

Author: jpatul
Date: 2025-03-23T15:05:30Z
Content: You should have determined FMV at DOD. I assume did not so was there a substanial time between selling and DOD? and how $ are we talking?

Author: jtarbutton
Date: 2025-03-23T16:23:39Z
Content: Thanks for your response. It has been 8 years between the DOD and the sale. The sale price was just under $20K. Any further inout would g=be greatly appreciated.

Author: jpatul
Date: 2025-03-24T12:40:23Z
Content: I thought there might be less time between inheritance and sale  - say only a few months - so you can just use the sales value as cost basis. If I ask my friend Google there is a thing called “retrospective appraisal” which I know little about.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-24T13:26:40Z
Content: If the minerals are producing, then the basis at time of death must be reduced by all depletion over the last 8 years, down to (but not below) zero.  Many long-term owners have a zero basis.

rag_documents.title: Preparing to pass mineral rights to heirs
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Preparing to pass mineral rights to heirs

Author: min4me
Date: 2025-02-26T19:43:31Z
Content: I inherited some non-participating mineral rights in Texas from a distant relative. I have been able to get on pay lists and receive payments from TX Unclaimed Property and producers by providing proof of heirship - wills.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-08T21:36:08Z
Content: We have chosen a Living Trust to hold a majority of our assets as well as mineral interests. I established a separate EIN for the Trust since the death of a spouse can potentially create some issues with Purchasers. Tax reporting is still performed on your personal tax return. A successor trustee can issue a MD to the subsequent beneficiaries. As long as you title, issue MD to the Trust, the properties into the Trust, you will be able to avoid probate for these assets. Make sure to work with an attorney that specializes in estate planning to minimize risk.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-09T11:05:43Z
Content: To answer your question. Texas has “lady Bird” deeds which are transfer on death deeds. They are not complicated. But, if one doesn’t do it correctly, it won’t work upon the grantor’s death, and interest would be subject to an estate proceeding. What I can’t tell from your question is how many interests you have.

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2025-03-09T16:35:14Z
Content: A Living Trust prepared properly by an estate planning attorney avoids probate in  Texas.

Author: min4me
Date: 2025-03-10T20:29:47Z
Content: Since the mineral rights I have are currently being paid on the basis of providing proof of heirship from a distant relative’s mineral deeds, do I have to obtain a mineral deed in my name before setting these up to pass to my heir by “lady bird” or trust? If so, what do I request from an attorney? Does the attorney have to be a Texas attorney (where mineral rights are)? What should one expect the cost to be?

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2025-03-10T20:49:07Z
Content: do I have to obtain a mineral deed in my name before setting these up to pass to my heir by “lady bird” or trust?

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-10T22:24:09Z
Content: Unfortunately, people confuse getting “On Pay” as having satisfied chain of title requirements.
Many mineral owners unknowingly create title issues for future generations due to not being fully aware of the need to establish a proper chain of title. This comes in many fashions from improper legal descriptions to failing to complete transition documentation. If you are not familiar with how to prepare a Mineral Deed, then you should have an attorney that practices within this area to prepare the deeds. Be sure this is within their area of practice since I have seen many attorneys that prepare deeds with improper (I am being polite) legal descriptions that will require future curative work.

Author: sclausen
Date: 2025-03-14T19:40:07Z
Content: A lady bird deed and a transfer on death deeds are two different types of deeds in Texas.

Author: sclausen
Date: 2025-03-14T19:50:27Z
Content: The value of the interest and how many persons you want to inherit will determine which option is best for your situation.  If you have a revocable trust, these interests could be conveyed to the current trustee, and they would be disposed of in the same manner as your other assets at death.  A transfer on death deed could work if done properly, which is difficult if you have a number of beneficiaries and want certain contingencies to apply.  For interests with significant value, an LLC could be formed to own the assets and then your estate plan would dispose of your membership interests, which could be held as part of your revocable trust.

Author: Brenda_Johnson
Date: 2025-03-15T09:43:25Z
Content: My relative has filled out Division Orders for her mineral interests  She put her children’s names on them,  Is that enough to transfer ownership or should it be in a will or trust?

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-15T15:24:19Z
Content: No. Title transfers via a Mineral Deed. She will need professional help to prepare the deed properly so that it transfers by her intent (Joint Tenancy or at Death as an example). She can then file the deed with the County and provide a recorded copy to the operator/purchaser.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2025-03-15T18:53:08Z
Content: Explain to your relative that minerals are real property, just like a house.  It requires a deed or probate or similar legal document be filed in county deed records to transfer title.  Just as you sign a deed at closing to buy or sell a house.  Even to give a house to your children, you need to file a deed.  It is a public record to the world that real property, whether surface or minerals, now belong to someone else.  This is why you cannot just donate without a record, like giving away toys or personal items.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-15T19:17:35Z
Content: I am fully aware of that. The question that min4me asked was whether a Transfer on Death Deed (aka a Lady Bird deed in Texas) would work.

Author: min4me
Date: 2025-03-15T19:37:11Z
Content: From my perspective, I am trying to assess the best and cheapest way of insuring a singular heir will receive the mineral benefits I have been receiving upon my death.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-15T21:27:16Z
Content: tim_dowdMarch 15, 2025,  9:27pm15No difference between transfer on death deed and a Lady Bird deed. Texas just has an unusual name for it.Even though there is no probate in Oklahoma from your ancestor, you still own the interest. It’s just not marketable or you don’t have clear title. Real property, and oil and gas interests are real property interests must be owned 100% at all times by somebody. The moment your ancestor passed away, the interest went to you (and anybody who inherited it). It just doesn’t have clear title. So, yes, you can do a transfer on death deed now. But it doesn’t solve the problem of the gap in clear title transfer.As to Texas attorney doing a transfer on death deed, he/she could (maybe). Oklahoma has some peculiarites to their TODDs that the Texas lawyer may not be aware of. If he/she did it correctly, and then your heir filed an affidavit of acceptance within 9 months, it would probably work. But you still have the gap of title into you.You can have a TODD done. It is best to do one per county.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-15T22:56:56Z
Content: You may take two positions, fix the title issues now so you can transfer the interest without question or leave it for your heir to perform that work after your death. You can create deeds today of any nature, but that does not resolve the break in the tittle. Resolving this break is going to most likely require a legal proceeding. I can understand the desire to not want to pay for legal services, but you have an issue that will be resolved eventually. The choice is do you resolve it now or when you are forced to resolve it. Revenue suspension will part of your risk management.

Author: min4me
Date: 2025-03-17T17:31:31Z
Content: Why are you assuming I am not willing to pay legal fees? I paid legal fees to have wills prepared and probated.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2025-03-17T21:14:06Z
Content: tim_dowdMarch 17, 2025,  9:14pm18If there is no probate in Oklahoma for the ancestor to your wife, that is the break in title.A company could suspend revenue or they might let you get paid with an affidavit of heirship and the Texas probate (just have to ask).A landman could prepare the affidavit of heirship, but you would need an attorney to do an Oklahoma probate." I need help getting clear title from my ancestor to my late wife."

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2025-03-17T23:40:35Z
Content: Please look at your thread on this topic and you will see why I would draw that conclusion on legal fees. A break in title occurs when there is not clear documentation in the title progression. An example, a stranger to the title leases a mineral interest; although, the stranger is an heir there is no title document of record in the County to support the execution of the OGL. This provides a break in the record title. The stranger may have a probate from another State that the Lessee relies upon for the OGL and may elect to wait to clear title until production is established.

rag_documents.title: Camino royalty owner problem
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Camino royalty owner problem

Author: Sylvester_W_Brock_Jr
Date: 2025-03-03T02:03:23Z
Content: In my leases with Continental I always included a clause that required my consent to any assignment. My concern was twofold, whether earned royalties would be paid and how thw assignee would treat the owner. Well, I have freely consented to a few assignments but only one do I regret: Camino.
I have been trying to have royalty payments directly deposited. Over six months. For some reason they will not do it. And the last two letters I have sent them have been returned to me unopened.
So. Watch out for these people, the royalty owner is not important to them.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2025-03-03T17:10:17Z
Content: Send you request to:camino@ownerrelationssupport.comorrev.inquiry@caminoresources.com.

Author: Sylvester_W_Brock_Jr
Date: 2025-03-11T22:48:00Z
Content: Todd: My wife called and was told that I am one of a bunch of owners who refused to provide information about actual depositors to or bank accounts. Information that of all my royalty payors only Camino demands blefore arranging wire transfers. Peculiar.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2025-03-13T18:17:10Z
Content: I guess you have a choice between supplying the requested information or risk having the mailbox bandit abscond with your check. If it were me, and this is not legal advice, I would request a Direct Deposit form, complete it as per their request and send back. Wallah, the funds are deposited into the directed account. Be sure and request that funds be distributed once they accrue to $25.00 or more.

Author: Sylvester_W_Brock_Jr
Date: 2025-03-20T02:04:41Z
Content: Todd: You are probably right, and I probably will do that. It just raises my hackles that Camino … nobody else … wants access to information beyond that required to set up wire transfer. And I can see no reason for it. Consider: If I only had Camino paying royalty my trust account would be blank. So first-time lessors cannot have Camino pay by wire? Stupid.
Another problem: I am an old f@rt who doesn’t like to be jerked around. I’ll guarantee one thing. Camino will get no more leases from me, directly or by assignment. But at age 94 I probably won’t be around for the next one and my kids (God, still calling these old folks “kids”) will be pushovers.

Author: Lee_Cooper
Date: 2025-03-20T02:17:13Z
Content: I hear ya!
Also, I’m also shocked at my “Kid’s” ages!

Date: 2025-03-21T20:06:58Z
Content: Camino uses a different vendor to do their direct deposits. And I will admit that FIS is complicated and could be much easier. But it is what it is.

Author: pbjminerals
Date: 2025-03-19T00:11:29Z
Content: I was contacted by a land man who has made an offer to purchase mineral rights we inherited through my grandmother’s estate.  We don’t have the records of these rights or any leases.  He has seen her estate named on these leases and says he can try to cure the title and collect back royalties due to us.  He has also made an offer to purchase any minerals he finds.  In order to do this work he is asking us to sign and Mineral Deed & Conveyance for a variety of sections. Author: Wade_Caldwell
Date: 2021-01-27T22:48:54Z
Content: Pres. Biden signed three executive orders today, which apparently include a ban on new leasing on federal lands, and a suspension of new drilling permits. The C-Span link to the remarks is below. I have not seen the text of the executive orders yet. Onshore production of oil and gas  is 8% of U.S. production. Include offshore, and it rises to 20%. There are some real whoppers in the speech.

Date: 2021-01-27T22:53:03Z
Content: Here are the Executive Orders from 1/20 on Keystone and suspending new permits.

Date: 2021-01-27T23:55:40Z

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2021-01-28T02:28:53Z
Content: Wayne- I am all against the Biden agenda. But to combat the leftist agenda begins in local elections. NM used to be a conservative state. Conservatives became complacent. This is the result. No need to complain about the top of the ticket. Start at the bottom. Run for office at the local level otherwise we are barking up a dead tree. The socialist agenda began in the Johnson administration & won’t be stopped until local governments stop it. My 2cents.

Date: 2021-01-28T02:46:10Z
Content: What Mr. Baker said is correct:No need to waste time, start local.  Find your local GOP group and start there, get involved in local delegates for state conventions.  Start at the bottom and work your way to the top to straighten out this mess!!

Date: 2021-01-28T16:05:28Z
Content: Other outlets reporting the new executive order does not ban new permits, but no confirmation from one I trust yet.

Content: Here is an article summarizing the potential tax changes Biden may push for. Depletion allowance is listed about 1/2 way down.

Content: Forbes summary of impact to New Mexico of the Permian Basin. Lea and Eddy Counties were poised to become the#1and#2oil producing counties in the U.S. before this latest salvo by the administration.

Date: 2021-01-28T18:13:26Z
Content: Wade,
Thanks for all of the information and resources - this is very helpful.  In addition to the potential rollback of fossil fuel “subsidies” like the depletion allowance which will impact all royalty owners, many may be wondering how a federal leasing ban would affect their private mineral rights.

Author: Wade_Caldwell
Date: 2021-01-28T18:35:36Z
Content: A separate Forbes summary of impact of a leasing ban.

Author: Wade_Caldwell
Date: 2021-01-28T19:50:57Z
Content: Gov. Abbott’s response to Biden’s flurry of executive orders.

Author: Carolyn_McGuire
Date: 2021-01-28T20:47:36Z
Content: It only pertains to govt land, not private lands.  I wonder if this will actually be like 2012 with the policy of oil independence. Made so many little guys so much money. Richest I ever was off oil was 2011-2014. So the fat cats in Alaska can’t make money off the govt land anymore, that only makes the Permin basin and New Mexico’s independent guys all that more valuable. This could be great for independent royalty owners. Why on earth would anyone think offshore oil is a good thing for the Permian? Less new places to produce the more you produce in places already permittable.

Author: Steve_Hunt
Date: 2021-01-29T13:55:53Z
Content: I like your logic, Carolyn. It does seem that the ban on exploration on federal lands would create a flight by producers to private lands and that would create scarcity. That could lead to rising lease bonuses and some negotiating power for us little guys, especially for gas wells, that may be more appealing as a “cleaner” fuel. The question is, “will the Biden administration find ways to come after us, too?” The possible attack on the deletion allowance is one example. I would love to hear more thoughts about the impact on small private royalty owners, of the Biden policies.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2021-01-29T15:09:17Z
Content: The problem is that in states such as New Mexico it is very difficult to drill horizontal wells that do not partially include federal lands due to the checkerboard patterns.  If easements are restricted on federal lands, then the oil company cannot install a pipeline to move the oil and gas or a temporary water line to a well, even for private land wells.  Once the anti-oil forces stop production on federal lands, then they will move against private lands.

Author: Marly_Jung
Date: 2021-01-29T19:35:44Z
Content: Local GOP is being more divided of late with the requirement for Representatives to sign agreements to vote 80+% on the far right policies and to ostracize those who do not (or not receive GOP funding).  This was made clear after Cheney stood firm on how she voted.
