Content: Did you inherit these interests individually, or did you inherit the ownership in your father’s company?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-10-23T14:08:49Z
Content: This may be governed by the terms of JOA (Joint Operating Agreement) which is usually signed by working interests to participate.  A party who later acquires the WI will still be subject to the JOA.  An oil and gas attorney familiar with operations side can best advise you, as your decisions may be affected by what other assets are owned by LP.

Author: mmcnail
Date: 2024-10-14T15:35:43Z
Content: I am trying to settle title requirements for mineral rights inherited in Lea Co, NM.  Does anyone know about the average costs and time frame we are looking at?  I am not from the area either.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2024-10-14T15:48:26Z
Content: unfortunately, this question can’t be answered without a lot of additional facts.
Its a little like my car won’t run. How much will it cost to fix? depends on what is wrong with it.
A quiet title suit may be as a result of somebody who died and had a confusing estate. It could also be necessary because of 70 years of deeds and ambiguous granting clauses or descriptions.
We would need to know a lot more.

Author: Jerry_Ithaca
Date: 2024-10-24T13:57:40Z
Content: I inherited mineral rights in Lea County from my Grandmother. She inherited these from my grandfather, he inherited these in1940. Grandmother did not do probate when grandfather passed. Probate was done in TX when grandmother passed. I live out of state. We had to do ancillary probate for both him and my grandmother in NM. There were 6 heirs involved, that drove up the legal costs. This took about 6 months and cost ~7500$.

rag_documents.title: Rights of naked owners to mineral royalties in Louisiana
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Rights of naked owners to mineral royalties in Louisiana

Author: Kevin1
Date: 2024-10-23T20:19:28Z
Content: My father passed away about 12 years ago intestate leaving me and my siblings as naked owners to his half of the estate including mineral rights.  My step mother has usufruct.  My question relates to the extent of her usufruct over the mineral royalties received on gas wells that were drilled after her usufruct took effect.  I believe that she has usufruct over the money, land and mineral rights that existed at the time of my father’s death.  However, after reading the Louisiana statues, it is unclear to me whether or not she has usufruct over the royalties from wells that did not exist at the time the usufruct was established.  Do we, as naked owners, have a right to the royalties that were received from wells that were dug after my fathers passing?

Author: Jimmy
Date: 2024-10-24T15:00:11Z
Content: Yes you should get 1/2 of everything! I believe your best bet is to hire a lawyer and you have to go to court to get this taken care of! Good luck and welcome to the forum!

rag_documents.title: Selling MR before or after November Election
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Selling MR before or after November Election

Author: GregAllen
Date: 2024-10-18T10:55:41Z
Content: I have received a few offers to purchase my Mineral Rights in the Nacogdoches, Texas area.  Should I sell the ASAP before the November election or After?

Author: NMoilboy
Date: 2024-10-18T12:55:20Z
Content: I don’t think the election is much of a factor for that relative to whatever other variables/priorities you may have.  At least not in any way that anyone here can predict today.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-21T20:38:24Z
Content: In my opinion, rushing to sell tied to perceived politics is not a good idea.  It is more important to know what pending activity you might have.  Many offers to buy come before drilling and tend to be low ball based upon my offers received.  If you give your block, abstract and section, you may get folks that are nearby to comment on the activity.  Would hate to have you sell and then find out that you had multiple horizontal wells coming.

Author: Wade_Caldwell
Date: 2024-10-21T21:46:37Z
Content: Agree that potential election results not a good idea to base a sale decision on.

Author: Lee_Clark_Archer
Date: 2024-10-22T22:30:20Z
Content: I have a file for each of property deeds. I file the offers in them. I write the offer amount on the front of the file. It’s fun to my kid’s and now Grand kid’s the fact that I received a ton more money by now selling. I also show them how I could have paid taxes on the sale. Then invested the money and earned dividends on that investment.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-10-23T12:36:12Z
Content: Why did you avoid mentioning the income taxes you paid on the revenue you received?

Author: Mineral_Man
Date: 2024-10-23T19:54:57Z
Content: From what I have heard, the election results will not highly impact your mineral rights values directly. Even if a more pro-drilling president were to take office (say Trump), then most of the additional drilling and permitting would likely be targeted at federal lands and not impact the Permian basin.

Date: 2024-10-23T22:36:15Z

Author: Lee_Clark_Archer
Date: 2024-10-24T13:45:28Z
Content: I didn’t get into all the tax details depletion etc. I don’t live off the royalties. That cash flow is invested. So the royalties are highest during the first few years. Than income bought more stocks than the offer price. Now I have gains from both sides. I’ve even leased part of a section and used the lease money to take a working interest in the property. I wished I had taken a larger working interest in that one. But cash flow needed on another non oil & gas project.

Author: oneida_valentine
Date: 2024-10-24T00:52:51Z
Content: I have 87.5 acres of mineral rights in the NW/4 of Section 29, Township 15 North, Range 17 W.I.M., Custer County, OK.  Different companies have held the lease since 1966 at 1/8 interest.  There has been little income from it.  I have been told by one person that even if they drill a new well, I will not get any income unless it is for surface rights.  Another person has told me that I will get income if there is a new well but at only 1/8 interest.  Which is correct?  Thank you, Oneida

Author: PeteR
Date: 2024-10-24T04:17:31Z
Content: @oneida_valentine,  if the old lease has been held by production, the
1/8th royalty would still apply to any new wells.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-24T11:45:32Z
Content: There are two gas vertical wells and one horizontal well in that section.  Encino has the Centennial horizontal well.  Mustang and Arnold have the two gas wells.  They are older wells.  Any new wells will be held by the original lease as long as it is valid.  Mewbourne has permits for new longer horizontal wells nearby, so if those are successful, there might be more interest in your section for new drilling.  Time will tell.

Topic: Finding the Landman for your NMRs

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-07-26T19:14:48Z
Content: Who is the Continental Landman, particularly for Stephens County, Section 21S, T1S, R4W.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-07-27T14:43:56Z
Content: The leases filed in that section recently have been with Camino, Continental, Dry Creek Energy, Duke Minerals.  One does not have to lease with the operator.

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-07-27T16:12:24Z
Content: Way back in 2018 I signed a lease for the NMR to Echo Energy who soon thereafter passed it on the Camino. Then in April 2023 Continental purchased the lease (or some other arrangement) from Camino. All the drilling in that section is being done with the Gus McCrae. It seems it is easier to get information from the Landman associated with that rig than Continental’s office. I’m looking who that would be.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-07-27T19:43:40Z
Content: What kind of information are you looking for?
A lot of information is proprietary while some is public.

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-07-27T21:15:04Z
Content: Going the fracking process with Section 20 a few years ago, I got nothing from Cheyenne Petroleum for 6 months and then got 1 check covering the production of  5 franked wells over 5 months.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-07-27T22:36:45Z
Content: You are way past the landman stage.  They move onto other projects. The well is called Gus McCrae 01S04W.  It was drilled by Continental back in 2019/20.  The first check that you get is for several months of production and is supposed to arrive by 180 days past first sales (6 mo).  That check is based upon the volume of products and the prices paid at that time.  The next check will be only for a month of product.  At the time, only one well was drilled and fracked by Continental.  Section 20 to the west with Cheyenne had two wells drilled in  2018/19.  Two more infill wells drilled in 21/22.  They would have had their own contracts with carriers for product pricing.

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-07-28T18:55:19Z
Content: So when I get a single receipt from Cheyenne showing 5 separate amounts from 5 separate sources adding up to the check it self, it is from 1 well? What do you call those separate sources coming from that single well?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-07-28T20:26:29Z
Content: Look at the property ID on the statement to see if numbers/names change.  Not seeing the statement, can’t say for sure.

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-07-28T22:41:16Z
Content: 180 days after Cheyenne’s fracking in Section 20 I got the first receipt showing oil, gas and process values. The values came from 1) “Well:OK098201 SKEET 17-20 LW 1H”, 2) “Well:OK098211 SKEET 17-20 S 3H”, 3) “Well:OK098211 SKEET 17-20 S 4H”, 4) “Well:OK098212 Cassie Armour 17-20 S 1H”, 5) “Well:OK098213 Alice Tucker 17-20 S 2H”.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-07-29T13:14:35Z
Content: The Cheyenne statement is showing multiple wells.The Continental statement has the first Gus McCrae well.  The other two should show up shortly.

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-07-29T23:42:36Z
Content: Were the 3 Gus McCrae’s shown in fracfocus were actually drilled down at those 3 location? Or did they all start drilling down at the first location and then went horizontal to the location shown on fracfocus map?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-07-30T18:48:22Z
Content: the two new Gus McCrae wells had a surface location in section 28 and drilled north into 21 and 16. Production is available on the OTC website now. Feb-Mayhttps://oktap.tax.ok.gov/oktap/web/_/#2

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-07-30T22:44:29Z
Content: Thanks for the history of the new wells. That puts my concerns to bet.

Date: 2024-10-23T21:59:10Z
Content: I forgot how to find production. When I follow the website you copied to all I see is dashboard with nothing about wells or production. Does the site state when they began producing?

Author: Brock_Presgrove
Date: 2024-10-23T22:14:04Z
Content: Interesting. I just got an email explaining that well#2is on the west side of the section and well # 3 is on the east side. Seems that some way at least the upper elevation of the section is split in half.

Topic: Ofer to sell mineral rights Carter co ok

Author: Dthaxton
Date: 2024-10-04T15:59:42Z
Content: Received offers to sell mineral rights in Carter County Oklahoma section 4 3s3w of 3600 per acre is this a good price

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2024-10-04T17:10:17Z
Content: I can’t really tell whether this is a good price or not.
I would be more concerned about who the buyer is. There are some companies out there who will enter into an agreement and then try to flip your acreage to another company. If they can’t find somebody, they will walk away. In the meantime, you have something filed in the county clerk’s records that prevents you from leasing, selling or collecting revenue.
There are very reputable buyers and then there are some that are not.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-22T14:50:24Z
Content: I agree with Tim.  Continental has a very active drilling program in Carter County.  Offers to buy often come right before drilling as the buyers think they know something.  Some buyers keep, some flip and some are working for Continental or other operators. Can’t comment on the price.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2024-10-23T12:43:14Z
Content: Looks like you already have had numerous horizontals drilled on you covering the Miss, Hunton, Woodford, Springer.  Takes a lot of time to look at the filings to see if your interest was covered in all of them, lets assume that they were.  This seems like a PDP play since the section is mostly developed, youd have to look at your current monthly income on the wells and do the math on if you get another 1-2 wells, using your past income statements on newly drilled wells as a guide to lead you.  Obviously theres a lot of guessing there as you dont know if they will drill 1 or more wells on a heavily developed section nor what the prices of oil and gas will be at the time.  So basically, you need to sit down for a day or 2 with a pencil and calculator to figure out if its worth selling. Its a crap shoot for you and the buyer

Author: John_Murray
Date: 2024-10-16T19:15:20Z
Content: I have been getting calls and letters all summer about buying my mineral rights in McKenzie and Williams counties.  This is after years of hearing almost nothing.  Many of these offers are from companies I have never heard of, but others are from companies that have made ridiculous offers in the past and I won’t deal with (or who don’t offer direct deposit and like to mail my checks 60-90 days after the date of the checks).  Similarly, my sister gets calls and offers even though she has hung up on these people after repeatedly telling them she has no interest in selling.  I half suspect they call her because they know they won’t get my signature.  Same with my aunt.  What part of “no” don’t they understand?
Does anyone have a sense of what is driving this push?  I see some activity on the ND Oil site, but nothing which justifies this?

Author: Rick_Tatum
Date: 2024-10-18T09:08:42Z
Content: I don’t know and I’m getting the sqme offers. They are better than they used to be but not much. My interests getting offers are in 146,98. And there is no history of production there worth speaking off. I’ve been trying to find info but no luck so far. We should all be looking for what is going on. thanks

Author: John_Murray
Date: 2024-10-18T19:51:01Z
Content: Yeah, it is a mystery.  Of course, I only hear from these companies when there is new drilling or about to be new drilling.
One company has this ridiculous cover letter stating that the oil industry is fading away, that prices are not what they once were, that they aren’t going to make any money if they buy my interest, that they are experts on making tax laws to make the investments profitable, etc., but that they are magnanimously going to make me an offer anyway because they are such generous guys.  At the same time, they post advertisements on Facebook for investment returns as high as 19%.  The incongruity is stunning.

rag_documents.title: Heirs with no will?
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Heirs with no will?

Author: debra_charlie
Date: 2024-10-11T01:12:27Z
Content: Hello, my sister passed away and there is no will with her mineral rights. What steps does her daughter need to take? Does she need a lawyer?

Author: Corywillfilm
Date: 2024-10-11T08:24:02Z
Content: Going through something similar but probate lawyer  who’s dealt with mineral rights would be able to help you out. But you’d probably need one that’s in the state that the rights are in if you are in another state outside of where the mineral rights are. No will would mean it goes to the daughter if there were no other siblings. Also depends on if she still had a husband at the time of her death. Then I think part of it would go to him as well I think. But probate lawyer is your first step.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2024-10-11T15:11:57Z
Content: Corywilfilm was right on target.  Oklahoma law and jurisdiction apply since the minerals are located here.  Don’t let the lack of a last will and testament worry you because the State of Oklahoma’s intestacy statutes would apply.  It would look at your sister’s marital status and her descendants to determine who gets what share.  Often probate cases can be resolved in a fairly short time span and without the need for court appearance by anyone but the attorney.

Author: S549bs
Date: 2024-10-18T13:16:38Z
Content: We used an “affidavit of Heirship” to get everything put in our name. (My sister and I) when our dad passed. Pretty simple. Download from the internet or maybe get one at Office Supply. Has to be noterized and specific to whatever you are claiming as yours as heirs. The form is explanatory

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2024-10-22T22:43:40Z
Content: While some entities accept affidavits of heirship, if the interests are significant a probate may be required.

Author: Bob77

Content: S= Section, enter 4

Leave the others blank

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-21T20:34:26Z
Content: image968×779 116 KBCheck your description carefully for all of the wording.  If you are in the NE quarter, then you may be in Lot 1 or Lot 2 depending upon the wording.  Indian Meridian.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2024-10-22T22:35:19Z
Content: If you were the beneficiary of a trust and it is time to distribute, the trustee would prepare a trustee’s deed.  Assuming you are a close family member there is no documentary stamp tax.  The exempt language can be placed on the deed thereby eliminating the tax stamp affidavit.

Author: Marc_B
Date: 2024-08-20T04:06:25Z
Content: I have been getting a small check every other month. They won’t send if it’s not over $100, which is fine with me.  But this month I just got one for less than $20.  I received the usual check last month.  I looked at the production for this $20 payment and the production was way down from normal months.  Anyone know what could be going on ? Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-08-20T12:25:55Z
Content: You have permits for horizontal wells on either side of you.  You may have possibly been briefly shut in while one of the wells nearby was being fracked.  Or there may have been mechanical work on your well.  Wait and see what next month brings.

rag_documents.title: Need advice re: Colorado minerals
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Need advice re: Colorado minerals

Author: jimsong
Date: 2024-10-19T21:52:43Z
Content: We own a share of minerals in Weld Co., Colorado (location below). We share the rights with extended family all of whom have already sold, or who are about to sell. We have received an offer that would be a good amount of money for our family, but we aren’t sure if it is wise to sell. Our concerns are that we might get passed over if we don’t sell now. Current offer is for 7000 per acre (with some variation on different portions of acreage). We are 60yo and will need this money for retirement, but don’t need it quite yet. Would there be good reasons to lease and not sell?

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2024-10-20T00:27:32Z
Content: The person who contacted you may only be interested in buying, not leasing.
To sell or not to sell is a hotly debated topic on this site. In my personal opinion, its a personal unique to you life decision. Others may suggest you keep it. But you don’t know that you will recover enough in royalties in the future.
Others will suggest you sell at the highest price you can secure if it is needed to pay off a house, put toward retirement, etc. Everybody’s position in life is different.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-21T13:08:19Z
Content: I would investigate the activity nearby and see if exploration is moving your way.  If I really wanted to sell, then I would get several offers and take the best one.  Or I would investigate what an auction site would list it for (they do charge a fee).

Author: Bob77
Date: 2024-10-22T14:47:31Z
Content: If I understand you correctly, the property is not leased, but you have an offer for 7K an acre for the minerals, do you know if the offer is based off a 3/16ths OGL royalty and contingent on you not leasing to another company? Do you know how many net acres you own and if there is any activity on your acreage? You are in a unique situation if in fact your minerals are open to lease.  Depending on your answers from the questions above, If it were me, Id lease to my LLC at 1/4 and then assign them the OGL at 3/16ths on top of selling the minerals, so at the end of the day you get the mineral sale and get to keep a 6.25% ORRI

Author: nop_llc
Date: 2024-10-22T21:40:00Z
Content: There may be another tract or two, but the map shows where you are. Section 5 appears to have been pooled in July. The other sections are being leased up. Offer sounds fair enough, but for unleased minerals it’s sort of mehh; going rates for leases are prob at least 1/3rd of that for 20+% royalty.

Author: HKlatt
Date: 2024-10-18T16:18:14Z
Content: Can anyone show me a map of the well value of JH Gibson Survey Block D Section 750 AB. 1883? Or how I go about getting info. Thank you!

Author: AJ11
Date: 2024-10-18T16:45:27Z
Content: At the top right corner of the page, click on the magnifying glass icon and search “ShaleXP”. Click on one of the archived posts. Find the ShaleXP url and open it.  See if you can find your well. I do not know how accurate the information on the site is.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-22T15:14:56Z
Content: No map will have the exact value of wells.  The value is dependent upon market conditions from minute to minute.  Shale XP and Pecan Tree and others have methodologies which can give you a ball park, but mineral market value is determined by “a willing and informed buyer under no compulsion to buy and a willing and informed seller under no compulsion to sell agreeing on a price.”  Mineral owners are rarely as informed as a buyer who knows the geology, the players in the area, the upcoming drilling plans, etc.

Author: Marc_B
Date: 2024-10-17T14:12:02Z
Content: So I inadvertently found out a company called Warwick-Minerva is applying to drill a new well or two.  16-16n-11w  (CD. 2024-002907).  I currently receive royalty from Devon on one well.  I had not received anything in the mail from this new company.  I guess they didn’t contact Devon to get my address as I looked at their paperwork on line and it has my old address.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-17T14:52:38Z
Content: You need to inform both Devon and Warwick of your new address.  It would also be wise to change your address with the correct form and notary stamp with the Blaine Count courthouse.

Author: Marc_B
Date: 2024-10-17T18:53:51Z
Content: I see now that Devon has filed a protest so I guess we will see where this ends up.

Date: 2024-10-18T13:16:22Z
Content: Ok, it’s weird because Devon has my new address (been here for 4 years). They were sending the checks here until direct deposit took over in 2022, same with Triumph and Contential.

Date: 2024-10-22T14:42:18Z
Content: There can be quite a few working interest owners in a well.  Devon can choose to be a partner with the new well(s) or they might end up being the operator and W-M being a partner.  Lots of wheeling and dealing at the courthouse during the time frame before drilling.

Topic: Increased density application for a new well

Author: nobshere1
Date: 2024-10-12T15:42:56Z
Content: There is a lot of activity in this section all of a sudden.  21-6-4 McClain County That is good!
I received an increased density application for a new well only in this section (21) for the Deese Common Source. In the application it states, “Applicant does not believe the existing well can adequately and efficiently develop the entire unit…”.
Question: What “existing” well are they speaking of? As far as I know, there are no wells in this section that are operating in the Deese CSOS.
Also, all wells in this section include both 21 and 28. Why only a single well in 21 and not both 21& 28? Just seems odd.

Author: KyndallLeone
Date: 2024-10-22T13:09:55Z
Content: We would need a little more information to look up the area.  T6_? and R4_? Operator name helps as well.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-10-22T14:26:53Z
Content: 21/28-6N-4W.  There is an additional case for section 28.  Sometimes they do them together for a multiunit well and sometimes they do not.  Case 2024-002867 is the location exception for a mutliunit well.  Case 2024-002866 is the multiunit horizontal case.image349×489 39.4 KBIt will be called the Indultado 0604 28-21-5OXH.  The current wells go through the Deese so are perhaps capable of producing some day.  If the next well is successful, they may go back and infill between the other wells which are producing in other reservoirs.

Author: Elaine370
Date: 2024-10-14T20:06:34Z
Content: This has a two part question/inquiry
(1) I have paid the taxes on these lots in Richland County
Twn/Rng/Sect 26N/57E/10 S2S2,NESE
Twn/Rng/Sect 26N/57E /15 N2NE, SENE
for about 14 years. Is there a law that states after a certain amount of years that the entire property is mine?
(2) I have PRP Holdings wanting to negotiate a lease, they are offering $7,800.00 for unstated years, no mention of royalties. So what is a reasonable offer?

Author: M_Barnes

Content: If you are paying taxes, then the county is already assuming that you own a percentage of those tracts.  There may be other owners also paying their percentage.  So no, you cannot get more property without paying the other owners for it.  Your ownership is tied to your deeds or probate documents.

rag_documents.title: Division Order %
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Division Order %

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-09-29T17:26:31Z
Content: The Section 36- 48% refers to Section 36 having 48% of the perforations in the wellbore (most likely not exactly 48%) and Section 1 having 51% of the perforations of the wellbore (most likely not exactly 51%) The total must be 100%. This is a multi-unit well so each section gets its percentage of the wellbore based on the percentage of wellbore perforations. The 0.00001 represents your share of the overall production from this particular wellbore.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-09-29T23:19:38Z
Content: If you care to share the Section, Township & Range, I can look at the wells in the area around these to get some approximate production information that may help.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-09-30T01:00:10Z
Content: You should be getting paid on the Liberty Valence 36-1MXH well, now operated by Continental Resources. It is a Sycamore formation well. Author: Sarah_Laster
Date: 2024-08-28T15:36:45Z
Content: I own some very small percentages of some wells in McClain County. The monthly check is my main source of income. Over the last 6 months, each check is less and less until Ialmostwouldn’t miss it. I was wondering if others are experiencing the same thing and if so, what the reason might be? I’m new to getting these checks so I don’t know if this is normal or not. Appreciate any comments.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-08-28T15:47:19Z
Content: Yes Sarah, it is normal for wells to decline rapidly. On average, most new horizontal wells in Oklahoma deplete 30-50% of their reserves in the first 3 years. Add to that depletion, the extremely low price of natural gas and you get this drastic decline in revenue.
Hope for the best but plan for the worst.
Good Luck.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-08-31T22:49:32Z
Content: Sarah, you received some solid advice from Todd. There is some modest horizontal activity in the SW portion of McClain. Ovintiv has posted their predicted spending for OK next year which will be about 5% of its total. The permian is going to be over 50%. This gives you an insight as to where companies are allocating drilling funds currently.

Author: Gary_Gilmer
Date: 2024-10-14T00:10:31Z
Content: I am having issues with the current Unit Operator in receiving timely Royalty Payments.
When they took over in June 2023, it was October before we started receiving any checks.  I know it takes time to get things rolling.  We then started receiving them monthly for production, 4 months prior.
As of now, the last check we received for production in April was in June 2024. They choose not to respond to phone calls, emails, or texts about what is going on.  They have posted data for May 2024 with OCD but are always way behind on that too.
I am surely not the only Royalty Interest Owner or Working Interest Owner of this Unit that is not concerned and waiting for payments.
What recourse do I have, outside of legal ones, to get this Operator doing his job.

Author: kpayne
Date: 2024-10-14T12:57:30Z
Content: I’m not familiar with NM statutes but you can look them up. In Texas and Oklahoma April’s sales would be paid to royalty owners in June. Operators receive the revenue for sales the month following the sales. April sales are received in May and then distributed to royalty owners in June. There could be minimum suspense amounts. If your interest is small and your revenue is under $100 you wouldn’t receive a check until it reached $100. If you can’t reach the operator I would start by researching the statutes there.

Author: ledp
Date: 2024-10-18T12:47:40Z
Content: I know that in Texas and Oklahoma if Royalty payments are not paid afte initial sales within 90 days.  The operator and or oil or gas revenue that sends out funds is obligated to pay interest or your proceeds.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-08-03T15:24:38Z
Content: Giving a section, township and range is more helpful in getting an answer.  The County is large and offers will vary due to geology.  Personally, I never go for more than three years.  The five year and relatively low price is a hint that nothing is happening at the moment.  Best to get an attorney to look at any draft lease as most are not in the mineral owner’s favor and need significant edits.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-08-05T20:29:33Z
Content: David, I have some NPR interests in the area. I am curious where you are specifically located and who has approached you with an offer. White Rock Oil and Gas has acquired properties from XTO in this area. The initial horizontals drilled in this area have not been that impressive; however, newer technology and techniques may improve results for newer wells. You want to be cautious on responding to offers since MT has some curious applications of their forced pooling statute.

posts.content: David, I have some NPR interests in the area. I am curious where you are specifically located and who has approached you with an offer. White Rock Oil and Gas has acquired properties from XTO in this area. The initial horizontals drilled in this area have not been that impressive; however, newer technology and techniques may improve results for newer wells. You want to be cautious on responding to offers since MT has some curious applications of their forced pooling statute.

posts.author: Casey
posts.content:
I just received an offer today T25N R56E sections 14 and 11
5 yr lease 19% $700 per acre bonus.  Anyone have any info?
Thanks guys

posts.author: TexasL
posts.content: And as far as terms, I don’t have current 2024 data but when activity was increasing at the end of 2023 the bonus per NMA had a very wide range.  As@M_Barnessaid, it varies greatly depending on numerous factors.  $200/NMA isn’t terrible but it’s not the highest I’ve seen.  It will be tough to get over 18.75% royalty, but I’ve gotten 20% in Richland a few years ago.  Never grant more than a 3 year primary term and always strike the option to extend.  It’s wise to include a drilling commitment and continuous development language to ensure your tracts get developed.  If you actually own 25% of the minerals in two sections then you have substantial leverage to work with; use it to your advantage.

Author: RunAmuck69
Date: 2024-10-04T21:01:56Z
Content: Hi, I’m trying to help parents/cousins get a better deal as they had in past with Clayton and Weber. Land is off 152 and Wormley lane. Most of their land is Bastrop.I own in both counties.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-09T15:50:26Z
Content: Chris, the company seems to be offering you a series of contracts based upon their option. First part is a seismic bonus of $25/ac. If the seismic is positive, you are locked into an OGL for $125/ac with a 3/2 term. If there is production, then you are locked into surface usage and possibly damages at $50/ac. All this is in the Company’s favor. I would offer a non-exclusive seismic agreement that provided for damages and a fixed amount for the property. I would not allow an option for a future OGL or surface usage since that limits your economic benefits. Good luck to you.

Author: RunAmuck69
Date: 2024-10-14T19:25:19Z
Content: Hey thanks! What is an OGL ? So your saying don’t get into a surface usage unless they are to fix and make it back to what it was?

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-14T22:28:32Z
Content: OGL is the acronym for Oil and Gas Lease. At this point I would only offer a surface damage agreement related to the seismic. If they come back in the future, you will know the seismic looks good. This puts you in a better position to negotiate.

Author: Tilldeath

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-10-08T14:29:06Z
Content: New Mexico has forced pooling.  So you can consent to pooling as approved by NMOCD.  I have not been hearing others complain about the political climate recently, so that may be more of a negotiating tactic.  You need to add the Twn and Range for the location of your minerals.  Then someone familiar with the specific area can comment.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-08T22:53:49Z
Content: Political climate does not delay a permit. Permits have statutory and administrative requirements. They operator may elect to delay permitting until there is a clearer picture on oil and gas product prices.

Content: I have a well in Midland County Texas that had a dramatic drop in revenue last month. When I asked the operator about this, they sent this reply -
Well affected by Offset frac end of July which caused oil/gas vols to drop and water increased. Shut in for Offset Frac 8/6/24-9/17/24

Author: Sunshine_02
Date: 2024-10-12T15:48:33Z
Content: I’ve had same issue with wells in Oklahoma.

Topic: Help understanding a lease offer

Author: James_B
Date: 2024-10-07T20:08:11Z
Content: Hello!
I was recently offered a lease for my small inheritance in Reeves County, Abstract 341
Survey H&GN RR CO
Block 13 Section 305
This land has been in my family for nearly 120 years and I first heard about it just two weeks ago. My late grandpa had a 1/30 interest in 80 acres and it has been passed to me and my brothers. However he died in 1991 and like I said nobody even knew about it, but there is production happening.

Author: David_Bawden
Date: 2024-10-08T13:39:15Z
Content: Hi@James_B. Maybe our ancestors were neighbors! My family has an interest in the W/2 of Section 305.  I’m guessing your family had an interest in the E/2. We never got anything on L49H because it’s in the E/2.  FYI, Vital only recently came into this area - they took over operations recently from another oil company, who themselves had taken over operations in this area a few years earlier. I would tend to agree that if your relative died in 1991 then there should be royalties from the L49H well somewhere. If they weren’t informed of the death in 1991, they may have deposited the funds with the TX unclaimed property division under your relative’s name? Otherwise, you can just call or email the person who reached out to you at Vital to ask what’s going on and see what they say. Another option is to hire an independent landman or an oil and gas attorney to look into things for you. If you were comfortable giving me your relative’s name, I have an old title report from 2013 and I can see if it still lists your relative as an owner.

Author: James_B
Date: 2024-10-08T20:43:35Z
Content: Hi David! I have just talked to an attorney in Huston. McAfee Land management is who contacted us in behalf of Vital Energy. My grand father name was Raymond. H. Crenshaw and J. W. Crenshaw was his father’s name. From what I understand J. W. had a 1/3 stake in 80 acres and it was divided among 10 children. I have searched Texas public records and found a few leases but they date back to 1968 and 1976. I really appreciate you responding to my call for help.

Author: James_B
Date: 2024-10-08T20:45:11Z
Content: Thank you Helen!
I just saw you reply. I have contacted Padau Law in Houston hopefully they can help.

Author: David_Bawden
Date: 2024-10-08T21:52:58Z
Content: I’ll send you the document I have privately. It lists the “heirs of J.W. Crenshaw and any spouse he had” as having an interest in the South 80 acres of the East 1/2 of the section. I’m no expert, but I’m pretty sure that if the operator can lease most of the interests, they can do new development without leasing absolutely every relevant interest. It looks like the report has some deed history so you can at least find a copy of when J.W. acquired the interest originally.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-08T22:48:44Z
Content: James the attorney you contacted should be able to get this under control. The well could have been excluded for many reasons: the well may have been part of an old OGL and still under production, the well may have been orphaned and never plugged, or there could have been title issues related to that well. The landman and your attorney can get it resolved.

Author: David_Bawden
Date: 2024-10-11T03:03:53Z
Content: Sorry but they won’t let me attach things or private message you or post a download link.

Author: James_B
Date: 2024-10-12T00:59:47Z
Content: That’s ok. I have given all the info I had to an attorney. I’m still waiting for a reply from them, but I’m sure they will lead me in the best direction.
Thank again.

rag_documents.title: Mineral rights and taxes
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Mineral rights and taxes

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-10-08T14:03:02Z
Content: In Texas, the mineral owner pays taxes on producing minerals.  Go to the Cotulla County CAD office website and search under both your name and your predecessor’s name for wells and also check your mailing address.  You want to make sure that back taxes are paid for your interest to make sure that the minerals are not sold for back taxes.  Generally tax valuations are done on the RRC lease number.  So if there are multiple wells under one RRC lease number (such as a unit), then you will usually only get one tax bill for all those wells.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-10-08T22:36:01Z
Content: You need to look at the unit acreage, as it may span two counties, in which case the value will be taxed proportionately to the acreage in each county (eg 30% vs 70%).  Also, look at the taxing authorities.  Wells are taxed by county, ISD (independent school district), hospital district, at different rates.  Is it possible that one is for county tax and the other is for ISD as school districts can overlap county lines.  If you post the unit/well name and RRC Lease ID#, then someone can help you look this up.

Author: thegoldentrust
Date: 2024-10-09T18:48:42Z
Content: Yes, one is county and one is ISD. This is a first for me and I really appreciate all the help.

Author: Corywillfilm
Date: 2024-09-24T20:25:47Z
Content: To try and make it short and sweet, Grandma passed 10 years ago. Just finding out about mineral rights that were in her name still, she had a will where the mineral rights went to my dad and uncle.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2024-09-24T21:05:45Z
Content: In many states, transactions involving land requires specific language in a Will, if none or in the case of intestacy, then a special order is required from the state having jurisdiction over the minerals.  Sounds like you need the assistance of a Montana estate attorney.

Author: Corywillfilm
Date: 2024-09-24T23:40:42Z
Content: Yup got one out of billings Montana who also deals with mineral rights in regards to estates as well, so hoping for a quick outcome but just trying to get a gauge of possibilities more than anything.

Author: Bob77
Date: 2024-09-25T00:58:30Z
Content: Yea, as long as you let whomever leasing you know of the situation

Author: KyndallLeone
Date: 2024-09-25T20:19:35Z
Content: Short story is, it depends on the risk tolerance/aggressiveness of the company the landman is working for.  If they have a short timeline and are ok with imperfect title, they may not care.  If this is a long shot play for them, it may give them pause to take the lease. If there are definite drilling plans, you are ok either way.  Just be honest with the landman and try to find out as much about the drilling plans as you can.  Good luck!

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-09T15:49:49Z
Content: Many people come to this forum to find advice to support their desired position/outcome. If you have an attorney in this matter, listen to their advice since they understand the issues. Any attorney would be hesitant to advise you to go forward with an agreement prior to the estate being settled. If you have to go forward for some compelling reason, then please make sure your attorney reviews all documentation prior to execution.

rag_documents.title: Competing oil lease offers
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Competing oil lease offers

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-28T12:41:20Z
Content: Many mineral owners would prefer the higher royalty because over time, the extra percentage adds up from years and years of production.  Perhaps more wells will be drilled in the same reservoir under the same lease and that will add up.  Bonus amounts are usually minimal compared to a successful well.

Author: Corywillfilm
Date: 2024-09-28T16:26:42Z
Content: I have a lawyer who will review the actual lease agreements and make any changes that will make it a fair or better lease for myself.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-28T16:45:47Z
Content: That is the difficult questions and why the members of the forum can sometimes help if they have offers nearby.  You can compare a common royalty such as 20% and ask what is the best offer that you will be giving in this township.  If the other company is higher, then mention that.  The clauses are the real money maker/saver.  If you can get a no post production charges lease and various other important concessions, then the lease with the best clauses wins. Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-21T19:56:18Z
Content: Not sure what your situation is so will answer generically.

Author: John1
Date: 2024-09-21T20:08:20Z
Content: I worked 41 yrs as a D/O Analyst never heard of an addr chg doc being recorded but why wudnt they place notary block on the doc a recorded doc must be notarized?  Addr chgs are never notarized.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-21T20:20:42Z
Content: Not sure which county you are talking about.  Don’t think the address change has to be notarized, but the rules might have changed by county.  We have always done it with a notary signature just to make sure.  The recorder of deeds can answer that question.

Author: John1
Date: 2024-09-21T20:35:06Z
Content: Another interesting requirement is payor will ONLY chg the addr to an addr matching a secondary identification doc which must b provided with the chg of addr doc fully recorded.  So a rich payee wanting checks to go c/o his accountant offices addr isn’t possible or an elderly payee who wants a daughter handling her checks/ affairs isnt possible!  I’m fighting that requirement also. Payee can insert any new addr they want.  A secondary ID card I don’t a have a problem providing but the matching addr requirement is insane too!  I am fighting myself I need no atty I’ve already beaten AT&T & UPS this year a small fry oper shud b a slam dunk.

Author: John1
Date: 2024-09-21T21:42:52Z
Content: While I don’t agree with recording addr chgs docs under any circumstances at least in Tex Okla NM La, a co who DOES want recorded makes their case way better with payee by placing the notary blk info at the btm of their addr chg forms.  I believe not having the notary showing the recording requirement is not enforceable - payee can’t be expected to add the notary info.  So chances of forcing recording is tougher with no notary block on the form. Randomly discussing the recordings for addr chgs with all my D/O friends today in Tex & Okla nobody has ever heard of requiring that. Getting conveyances & estate docs recorded in ea affected county  is tough enough I can’t even imagine wanting recordings of all addr chgs in ever county wells are owned.  I’ve processed thousands of addr chgs in my career.  I was processing 20 name/addr chgs daily the last 6 months of my career cleaning up suspense & contacting payees at new addresses I found! I released 1/2 of all suspense $ in 2 yrs.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2024-09-24T15:46:57Z
Content: The county clerk will not accept a notice of change of address for filing unless it is notarized and the appropriate fee is provided.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-09-24T15:55:28Z
Content: The purpose of the notary is to verify that the person whose signature is on the document is actually that person. If there is no verification, I could claim to be you and send in a change of
address and start receiving your checks. I’m sure you don’t want that to happen to you.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-09T00:35:12Z
Content: John, you may be dealing part of our new era of Owner Relations Contractors. You have a unique situation that I have not seen in 40+ years as a mineral owner and landman. First Winblad nails it, any document filed by you has to be notarized to be accepted by the County Clerk’s Office. I have advised clients in the past to file an Affidavit of Address in cases that it is beneficial to client. With all this said, was there anything that differentiated this address change request on your part other than just the address?

rag_documents.title: Surface Rights Texas
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Surface Rights Texas

Author: Biker_Guy
Date: 2024-10-07T23:32:59Z
Content: I bought 10 acres in Pecos Texas that has some type of storage tanks/tanks on the property I saw on Google earth. I wasn’t told anything about the tanks. How can I find out who owns them? I want them removed. Thank You

Author: Dusty1
Date: 2024-10-08T00:04:23Z
Content: Do you own the mineral interest or just the surface of the tract?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-10-08T03:14:27Z
Content: It seems that you bought the 10 acres without inspecting the land, which may be unfortunate.  Keep in mind that it can be difficult to match Google earth view with the exact location of a particular 10 acres.  Same with RRC GIS Viewer.  The section overlays are not always exact.  So the tanks or equipment may not be on your tract.  If they are on your tract, you will need to not only determine who owns them, but also how the owner has or had the right to locate them on the 10 acres.  For example, it is related to a oil and gas production (dominant mineral rights) or is there an outstanding rental lease or easement which entitles a company to place them there?

Author: Mineral_Owner5
Date: 2024-10-08T18:54:25Z
Content: Google Earth Images have a date the photo or image was taken usually near the bottom right. Some images may be several year’s old. If you got a title insurance policy when you bought the tract it should provide information about the tract title, right of ways and things such as that. You may have “bought” problems!

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-08T23:11:11Z
Content: If you are not local, then you will have to put on a sleuth hat. Have you tried taking to the previous owner or the real estate agent about the property? You can try calling the Tax Assessors Office and ask if they have any information on the tanks since they should be subject to advalorem/personal property. Have the tax parcel number available. If there is a near by neighbor, contact them to take a picture of the tanks and email to you. There should be information posted at the tanks (sign) to tell you who is the owner.

Topic: Questions about lease offer

Author: deanerandco
Date: 2024-10-07T22:22:26Z
Content: Hello,
We received a letter regarding a lease offer in Upton County Tx. stating it is available to lease due to lack of production.  The offer is for Section 8 block 2.  It further stated the intent is to drill below Atoka formation starting at 10,000’ and below.

Author: AJ11
Date: 2024-10-08T05:34:23Z
Content: It sounds as if your minerals were leased at an earlier date. If this is correct, I would think it would
be very important for you to establish that the letter you received is correct regarding lack of production and availability. What happens if you lease minerals which are still held by an old lease in the opinion of the earlier lessee? Perhaps an earlier lease had a depth clause and you can lease below 10,000’ without any issues. I will defer to others here, but I would want an oil and gas attorney to advise me in a situation like this. You should be shooting for a 25% royalty which in actual application–not just in lip service–has zero post production deductions. Do not warrant title, especially given the questions raised in your first sentence. An oil and gas attorney can help you with the lease language and may be able to give guidance on what bonus $/acre is reasonable to expect.

Author: deanerandco
Date: 2024-10-08T20:01:37Z
Content: Thanks for the reply.  I agree with your points and will pass them on to the partners.  I think more research needs to be done and if deemed leasable, addendums you stated would be added along with proposed changes to bonus and royalty %.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-08T23:00:48Z
Content: You have a couple of issues at this point. You can take the title research obligation and make a decision on an OGL. It sounds like what you received is an OGL offer and a letter stating the intended target formation for the initial well. Just call the landman rather than speculating. The answer is probably fairly simple.

Author: Jerry_Magill
Date: 2024-10-02T15:38:17Z
Content: I reached out to XTO, who operates the Fullerton Clearfork Unit TR 014, in Andrews County, TX.  I receive royalties from this lease and have no way of checking production accuracy without the API numbers.  The TX RRC has no record of TR 014, and XTO refuses to provide the API numbers as they “do not provide personal information research.”  Can anyone here advise me where to find the API numbers, or perhaps refer me to a qualified landman in the Andrews County area?

Author: Dusty1
Date: 2024-10-02T16:52:12Z
Content: If you can locate the wells on RRC’s map it will give the API number. But having API numbers won’t help you check production from specific wells since the production from all the wells in that big unit appear to be reported to RRC on a total unit basis rather by well. Not unusal for large units.

Author: NMoilboy
Date: 2024-10-02T20:59:42Z
Content: Its a big waterflood which sounds like its paying on a tract basis (TR 14).   And probably reporting production on a unit-wide (i.e. lease) basis.  Which is going to make everything really rough.   I would guess the tract volumes are a constant % of the unit volumes based on how big the tract is versus the total unit size.   So the tract volumes in your check should follow the overall unit production.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-02T21:20:54Z
Content: You will have to find the original unit agreement and any amendments in order to discover your tract participation percentage. You will then be able to apply your tract participation to your mineral ownership to determine the production allocation. XTO already does this for you, but it never hurts to check for accuracy.

Content: I am a complete newbie to this, my family just learned our Grandparents owns mineral rights for several properties in Stillwater, OK. Is there a easy way to decipher this location to an actual property? I would love to understand the language.

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2024-08-30T19:17:28Z
Content: The description is for a subdivision within Payne County.  at about 2302 S. Husband St.
This site shows the properties within that subdivision:

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-03T20:00:25Z
Content: Good advice from Winblad. The easiest way to read legal descriptions and find them on a map is by reading from right to left. This allows you to find the State, then County, then Township and the corresponding Range, next you find the Section. Once you are in the Section you continue the same process. Think of the Section as a square and you are being directed to an area one step at a time. The NW/4 (Northwest quarter) is the W/2 (West half) of the N/2 (North half) of the Section. A Section is generally considered to be 640 acres. Each following part of the description takes you to a sub-part of the previous description. I hope this helps.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: Texas Record Keeping

Author: Jmcconnell
Date: 2024-08-19T13:14:05Z
Content: I am curious how everyone else is keeping tack of mineral ownership.  I have several mineral deeds across Texas & Oklahoma.  My goal is to create a master list of all “properties” if you will.  Oklahoma is easy because they use the Public Land Survey System (PLSS) whish gives you Section, Township, & Range.  Texas on the other hand, is based on Spanish land grants.  It almost seems impossible to keep tack of without have a map outlining what is yours. What have you found to be the best system to organize land in Texas?

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-08-19T13:19:23Z
Content: I use Excel and do OK by State, County, township, range, section.
TX by State, County, Block, Abstract, section

Author: garyr1944
Date: 2024-08-27T15:59:59Z
Content: If you use excel, you can insert into the spreadsheed a map, photo, or a shot from google earth into the line of the property.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-02T22:21:05Z
Content: You put forth some great questions. Barnes and Gary provided you with a good start. If you want to this digitally, then you have several options dependent upon your budget and producing status. For producing properties, you can use MiQ Essential for no cost in order to track wells, production/revenue and activity levels. I would add to Gary’s suggestion using Google Drive, or similar, to store a pdf of each deed or related document in a folder. You can then link the folder to a spreadsheet.  This is a simple system as long as you do not have a great deal of activity and you have a basic understanding of digital products.

Author: Jmcconnell
Date: 2024-10-02T22:47:51Z
Content: I appreciate the feedback.  I have done just that.  Created a Google Drive and linked it with Spreadsheets.  I am unfamiliar with MiQ Essential though.  Perhaps you could elaborate more on that.  Are you referring tomiq.org?

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-02T23:30:47Z
Content: www.mineraliq .com/ is the web link. This is a service that is a part of Enverus/EnergyLink. Many operators/purchasers use EnergyLink to deliver digital royalty check details to owners as well as other information. I use MiQ Essential casually (currently free) because I use MineralWare to process the digital data from EnergyLink as well as the pdf check details that we receive. I also use MineralWare to track property activity and quicker access to State data. MineralWare is a paid service as well as the higher MiQ products. I believe MiQ processes the State data better than MineralWare, but there is a significant cost difference and I do not believe MiQ will process pdf check details.

rag_documents.title: Question on Forming LLC
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Question on Forming LLC

Author: SSS
Date: 2024-10-01T13:26:52Z
Content: I’m in Iowa and working on forming an LLC for working interests I have in Oklahoma and Texas.
Are their special requirements I need to take into consideration when I have an LLC registered in one state with the property in another state? I am not sure if I need to register in both Oklahoma and Texas somehow, too, or what needs done or how to begin that step. Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you

Author: Richard_Winblad
Date: 2024-10-01T22:27:59Z
Content: What benefits do you believe an LLC would provide?  Royalty owners rarely need to worry about liability.  An LLC may add an unneeded layer of complexity over a Trust.  You would also need to comply with Corporate Transiency Act which is administered by the Financial Crimes unit of the Treasury.  Yikes.

Author: PeteR
Date: 2024-10-01T22:28:21Z
Content: @SSS, generally speaking LLCs are required to register in the states they are doing business in and are required to maintain an agent in each state along with complying with other annual certificate and reporting requirements particular to each state.
The Secretary of State websites for each state often have the
references needed to find the rules in each state.

Author: SSS
Date: 2024-10-01T23:11:19Z
Content: I have non operator working interest in my and my husband’s name. I thought that an LLC would protect our other assets from any liability claim. I see folks saying the non operator working interest needs liability insurance and I am checking with the operator to see if we have that through them. If we don’t, I don’t even know if I can get that for my working interest. So that’s why I was thinking the LLC. Am I misinterpreting the need for an LLC and liability insurance for what I have?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-10-02T00:40:12Z
Content: The LLC will provide a layer of protection.  Generally, non-op WI are governed by JOA and pay their share of expenses, including insurance.  Are you receiving detailed JIB (joint interest billing) statements which list the expenses?  I have not heard of non-op  WI getting separate well insurance.  Of course it is always a good idea to have a personal umbrella policy.   Your business attorney and a CPA experienced in oil and taxation can provide best advice.

Author: SSS
Date: 2024-10-02T21:53:10Z
Content: Neither side has the JOA so I’m not sure what happens next for determining that. I do receive the JIB statements and those have a section for Admin, which is a chunk, but it is not broken down. It may be under there. I am trying to get confirmation. Seems like I’m the first person to ask for this information, which seems really odd. I don’t want to make an assumption.

Author: James_Garner1
Date: 2024-10-02T22:39:14Z
Content: This comes to a question of economics. If the LLC is properly formed and operated, then it will provide a layer of personal liability protection. There is insurance to manage various risk exposures, but the cost can be high and limited; therefore, you have to assess the value of the properties to the insurance cost. The insurance of the operator can potentially protect your interest as it relates to their operations, but you would need to review the policy. If you have concerns, you should get an experienced professional in these matters to provide you with options. A personal umbrella should not offer protection to the W.I. since it is in an LLC. The LLC is considered a separate entity as long as properly formed and maintained. I want to stress, this is not the venue for specific advice on this issue since there are multiple variables and complexities.

rag_documents.title: Oil and Gas Lease
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Oil and Gas Lease

Author: MinerialOwner
Date: 2024-09-26T22:03:41Z
Content: Greeting, we have property in Grapeland TX, Houston County
and was approached by Drake Exploration in leasing our mineral interest.
No.31, John Edens
No.1191 Abraham Zubar
No.1366 TH Barrow
No.1366 TH Barrow
Approx 85 acres. Does anyone know what the signed Bonus payment rate and Royalty is going for in our area.
We were offered 350.00 per Mineral Acre  and 18.75% Royalty. Any help would be much appreciated.

Author: RevGaul
Date: 2024-09-27T00:38:08Z
Content: A 3/16ths royalty is pretty fair. You might insist on a little more money regarding the lease bonus and a cost free clause. Maybe just take the $350 and put in depth clause provisions. Depends on what zones they are targeting, did they happen to say?

Author: Garry_Smith
Date: 2024-09-27T09:32:07Z
Content: I think it can vary quite a bit.  Some places in Houston County are very good, other spots not good at all.  It can also depend on how much (how high ownership %) you own.  I’m down in Lovelady, we have requested and received $500 per NMA and 20%.  But I am a very tiny owner, I believe larger owners have gotten more.  I also own near Shady Grove property where nothing has happened or is happening!!  I was offered $350 per NMA I ask for $500 and never heard from them again!
I recommend you check the Texas Railroad Commission map for drilling activity around your property.  You may get a sense for how good the area is as well as dates when permits and drilling were done.  Good luck!

Author: MinerialOwner
Date: 2024-09-29T00:28:04Z
Content: Thank You for your help. Can you please educate me on what a depth clause provsion is?

Author: RevGaul
Date: 2024-09-29T16:28:06Z
Content: Only lease them the depths they are targeting. That way if another company identifies a different depth zone at some point in the future you can then lease that zone and get paid again. It’s possible to have multiple depths(zones) being operated by different Operators. In my opinion it’s more valuable to have a cost free royalty clause in the lease instead of a couple hundred bucks more per acre for the lease bonus. Cost free means you get your portion at the well. You do not get deducted for. Treating, transporting or storage and other associated fees

Author: MinerialOwner
Date: 2024-09-29T21:34:49Z
Content: Thank You for your help again. I appreciate you and your knowledge on all of this.

Author: M43P
Date: 2024-09-30T15:54:47Z
Content: Where are you located? We have also been contacted by Drake and would like to talk to someone in the area.

Author: RevGaul
Date: 2024-09-30T16:15:49Z
Content: No problem, I grew up in Athens and I’ll try to help my neighbors out when I can.

Author: M43P
Date: 2024-10-01T23:55:37Z
Content: Mineral Owner
Did they have a no cost royalty clause?

Author: MinerialOwner
Date: 2024-10-02T00:34:26Z
Content: Not that I could find. That is something you would have to negotiate.

Author: Bigfoot
Date: 2024-10-02T20:02:43Z
Content: Just my opinion; but, every location is different and most landmen are as well.  IMO, what’s in the lease is considerably more important, no matter what the royalty or bonus money value winds up being.  No lease should ever be signed without the help of a seasoned attorney that has at least some oil lease history.  With all that said, anything less than 20% and anything less than $500/acre for the first three years went out prior to the last big leading frenzy around 2012-2014.

Content: My wife’s grandfather passed down mineral rights , in Kingfisher OK,  to his children, then those are now passed down the grandchildren. This makes 3 family branches.

Date: 2024-09-29T16:27:48Z
Content: I did find out a claim can be filed with Oklahoma Corporation Commission. This claim is what lawyers help a mineral rights owner file with royalty disputes.
But it can be filled out directly by owners on their website.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-09-29T17:22:10Z
Content: The OCC can do nothing about title or ownership problems.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-29T20:29:45Z
Content: You need an attorney or a good landman to sort out the title issues.  Just because you have a deed does not necessarily mean the chain of title is correct before that deed was filed.

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2024-10-01T09:53:31Z
Content: This advice relates to all parties who contact oil companies.
Division Order analysts are often overworked and make mistakes.
With that said, when contacting oil company, it is better to keep reminding them of the underlying problem. Don’t assume they will remember.
Another way to put it is if one contacts an oil company and lays out all the facts with all the documents Now, contrast that with somebody else  who contacts them and that person says there is a problem with this (unidentified)  well in Oklahoma and it is not right, and there are no docs  and no underlying facts, the Division Order analyst is going to fix the first problem first because they can figure it out.  They don’t have to go digging to find the underlying problem.

rag_documents.title: Ancillary Probate in West Virginia
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Ancillary Probate in West Virginia

Author: s_colosimo
Date: 2024-09-29T11:58:30Z
Content: I receive royalties from 2 gas wells in West Virginia.

Author: TODD_M_Baker
Date: 2024-09-29T12:03:18Z
Content: I believe you answered your own question. But to confirm, contact the County treasure or Assessor. You will need the legal description.

Author: s_colosimo
Date: 2024-09-29T12:21:46Z
Content: If they own the land do I have to go through ancillary probate to receive my mother’s share?  She died 2 years ago.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-29T20:24:50Z
Content: The land may be severed from the minerals.  If you have royalties, those go with the minerals.  The surface land may not matter.  Contact the operator to make sure that they have you as the owner.  If you are receiving royalties that are in another person’s name, that needs to be fixed immediately.  Are you paying taxes on the production?  Contact the assessor.  It is wise to get the title moved to your name properly if you are the heir.  By probate if a will or by the state intestate law if your mom passed without a will.  Condolences on her passing.

Author: s_colosimo
Date: 2024-09-29T22:42:36Z
Content: I have been around and around with Diversified, who was paying my mother royalties.
She received a form to file her taxes.  So I assume she paid tax on the money she received from Diversified.
But never on the land.  So why do I have to do ancillary probate in WV?
I probated her estate in N.C., where she died.

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-09-30T02:54:19Z
Content: Minerals are real estate and title must be transferred in accordance with state law where the minerals are located.  It always involves filing a deed or probate order or other document in the county deed records.  It is the same process as when you buy or sell a house or any other real estate.  Some states, such as Texas, will accept out-of-state probate.  Other states require ancillary probate.  The operator will not pay the royalties to you until the title has been moved from your mother to you.  You should consult an estate attorney in West Virginia to get title transferred to you.  Most likely the form your mother received was the annual 1099 which set out the annual royalties and your mother then paid federal and state income taxes on that income.

Author: s_colosimo
Date: 2024-09-30T22:14:32Z
Content: I don’t understand this: Ancillary probate wants the assessed and fair market value of the real estate.
If all that is owned is the rights what goes there?

Author: tim_dowd
Date: 2024-10-01T01:06:11Z
Content: One has to do an ancillary probate on any property that is considered real property.  As Daze pointed out above, the minerals are considered real property. Even though it is not surface property. The ancillary probate is to determine the heirship and the present ownership  of the oil & gas minerals, not the surface.
Minerals get taxed in WV. That is why (probably) your mother paid taxes.
The value that the form of the ancillary probate is seeking is the value of the minerals. They are seeking the value of the minerals in question, not the surface.
Make a good faith guestimate of the value.

It always involves filing a deed or probate order or other document in the county deed records.  It is the same process as when you buy or sell a house or any other real estate.  Some states, such as Texas, will accept out-of-state probate.  Other states require ancillary probate.  The operator will not pay the royalties to you until the title has been moved from your mother to you.  You should consult an estate attorney in West Virginia to get title transferred to you.  Most likely the form your mother received was the annual 1099 which set out the annual royalties and your mother then paid federal and state income taxes on that income.

posts.author: s_colosimo
posts.content:
I don’t understand this: Ancillary probate wants the assessed and fair market value of the real estate.
If all that is owned is the rights what goes there?

posts.author: tim_dowd
posts.content:
One has to do an ancillary probate on any property that is considered real property.  As Daze pointed out above, the minerals are considered real property. Even though it is not surface property. The ancillary probate is to determine the heirship and the present ownership  of the oil & gas minerals, not the surface.
Minerals get taxed in WV. That is why (probably) your mother paid taxes.
The value that the form of the ancillary probate is seeking is the value of the minerals. They are seeking the value of the minerals in question, not the surface.
Make a good faith guestimate of the value.

rag_documents.title: Mineral Appraisal Weld County Colorado
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Mineral Appraisal Weld County Colorado

Author: bsmranch
Date: 2024-09-28T17:17:56Z
Content: We have inherited mineral rights on 25 acres in Weld County. There is a current lifetime lease with 15% royalty. Currently a shut in well so getting the minimum to hold the lease. Getting offers to buy. We are now faced with paying for an appraisal to get a starting value for Capital Gains purposes (quotes have come in from $9k to $25K for an appraisal). Current offer is as high as $7K per acre. There are 4 of us that never agree on anything!

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-28T17:26:40Z
Content: Several thoughts.-If you share the section, township and range, then forum members can comment on the activity.  Probably why you are getting the offers. You may be getting horizontal wells in the future.  Always good to get the most information you can before making a decision.
-Pending the upcoming activity, you may not want to sell
-Depending upon how you inherited, you each may be able to make your own decision.  Those who want to keep can keep, those that want to sell can sell their own portion
-The estate could pay for the appraisal.  Or you might not need to do an appraisal since the sales price minus step up value is what the capital gains is based upon.  Your step up value at the time of inheriting will usually be higher than what the ancestor’s original value would have been.  If you just inherited and sold quickly, then there may not be much in capital gains.  Those estimates sound a bit high to do an appraisal, but depends upon the location.

Author: bsmranch
Date: 2024-09-29T00:23:33Z
Content: The information on the property in Weld County Colorado: Section 31, Township 2 North, Range 68 West The property has been mined for gravel and has had a pump on the property at one time. The well is a shut in well, no royalties at this time. The company is paying yearly to keep the lease, it is a lifetime lease with no ability to negotiate as long as they keep making the minimum payment per year to keep the lease. The appraisal would be for a step up value as my parents have recently passed. If we do not sell soon we do need to get a value for the step up basis. As for appraisals yes, very high. I have contacted 2 and one was referred to by someone that did another appraisal. It seems Colorado appraisals are high. Thank you for the input

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-29T20:20:59Z
Content: Are you on the East side or the West side of that section? The East side has about 10-11 horizontal wells.  The West side has older wells, but room for quite a few horizontal wells.  That might be why you are getting offers.

Date: 2024-09-29T20:49:28Z

Date: 2024-09-14T15:00:42Z
Content: The lake is natural with no outflow. The lake bed is about 110 acres, 6 lots in four different sections surround it. Our family quarter section (approx.) is “clipped” by the lake bed in its NE corner - the intersection of four sections - by 0.6 acres (ugh!). The survey is the initial 1899 survey after North Dakota statehood (surprisingly easy to find online). Surrounding lakes were all surveyed as “land” (too shallow, probably) owned by the lot or owner  - these were the homesteading days in ND. Many of the surrounding lakes also span multiple sections, but without any mineral rights ambiguity.

Our acres are in McKenzie County not Williams County BTW. Good luck.

rag_documents.title: Operators backdating initial reports on gas production
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Operators backdating initial reports on gas production

Author: Tracy_Garvey
Date: 2024-09-27T16:20:16Z
Content: I’m a royalty owner in Reeves County who has a well that is apparently getting ready to stop producing and I need to understand the processes involved with how operators get gas production reported to the RRC and how the operator changes the initial reports. My concern is that I have a lease that terminates with a 90 day period of no production and the well had reported a period of no production for 4 months. After notifying the operator with a letter that the well had gaps in production and low production they backdated the reports with the RRC showing a very small about of gas was produced and flared in the last two months of the 4 month period so that on there was only 60 days of no production. In this case the operator claimed that there is consistent production and the lease was still valid. So my question is how do operators prove what the are reporting on production to be true and accurate?

Author: TennisDaze
Date: 2024-09-27T17:09:48Z
Content: There are some operators who play these games to hold onto a lease or not have to pay plugging costs.  If you post the operator and well, some one may have more information.  In a future lease, have your attorney add that the well needs to produce in paying quantities with a definition of paying quantities.

rag_documents.content:
Topic: Lithium Language for Leasing in Montana

Author: Geoffrey_Don
Date: 2024-08-02T15:42:08Z
Content: Hello all, I have an offer for horizontal wells in Richland County, Montana.  My question is about adding language to the lease for a royalty on lithium, if lithium is to be extracted from brine during this operation.

Author: Jimmy
Date: 2024-08-03T15:14:11Z
Content: Sir you can add a cause on your lease to include brine ! Good luck

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-08-03T15:27:05Z
Content: Best to get legal advice on leasing language.  In general, brine in an aquifer belongs to the surface owner in many states.  Saltwater that comes out of the hydrocarbon stream often belongs to the operator.  In some states, it can be claimed if put into the lease language.  Must abide by the statues of the state your tract is in.

Author: Geoffrey_Don
Date: 2024-08-05T18:32:15Z
Content: Thanks Mrs. Barnes and Jimmy.  Looking forward to the national meeting.

Author: RevGaul
Date: 2024-09-26T23:54:57Z
Content: Lithium royalty rates are typically much less than O&G. Lots of unknowns in the lithium space, it’s so new and interesting but as someone who worked on a lithium project I can honestly say no one really knows what any this is worth. Lots of hypotheticals! I’d wait them out for a couple months, try to get a better bonus and royalty then demand a favored nations clause.

rag_documents.title: Inherited Mineral Rights Value
rag_documents.content:
Topic: Inherited Mineral Rights Value

Author: TXT
Date: 2024-09-25T14:49:50Z
Content: I recently inherited some non producing mineral rights in Lavaca County, TX that are in the Edwin Richeson Survey, A 40. 68.4 acres.

Author: MR_ML
Date: 2024-09-25T16:15:34Z
Content: I don’t know your offer, but i would NOT sell.  EOG has plans to drill that area.  If there is an option period…which I think they had on all their leases in that area you would be getting another $1200/acre in 2 years which is $82,000.  An example of royalty on your 68 acres…say in a 1200 acre unit/pool that 1 well averages 300 barrels per day  first year at $70 / barrel and 22% royalty you would get $95,000 the first year alone…this size of unit could have up to 6 wells…so $565,000 just the first year on these wells alone…this is assuming you have 100% of the mineral rights for the 68 acres.  If you need the money desperately…then I always figure $5000/acre minimum which would be $340,000…but I would hold these.  Matrix is drilling 4 new units bordering you place on the west as we speak…and EOG has committed 5 billion to this area alone…they are starting on the south play by US90A hallettsville-Shiner road, and another 1288 acre unit on the north end of their play close to moravia/Breslau that will go up in October. This well is a test for the upper Eagleford, lower eagleford and Austin  Chalk…they are doing 3 wells on this unit back to back…  Looks like they have about 25-30 units 35,000 acres to drill out,.,and will be using 2-5 rigs coming in shortly…Also looks like just lower Eagleford wells on the southern end of the play…

Author: Washington_Irving
Date: 2024-09-26T17:17:50Z
Content: I totally agree with MR_ML.  Unless you desperately need the money for shoes for the baby with winter coming on, just look at his math.  There’s no reason at all to sell mineral rights outright.  In addition, personally speaking a new lease comes along every 10-15 years with money/manna from heaven.  So if nothing ever happens you or your heirs will get some walking around money if nothing else.

Date: 2024-08-29T22:46:10Z
Content: @Jsfronk,That can depend on many things. First what is your percentage? Then you need to know how many NRA’s ( net royalty acres, not surface acres ), The price each month of oil or gas that is being produced. An allocation well or pooled? Date: 2024-08-30T12:23:21Z

Date: 2024-09-24T15:52:35Z
Content: I don’t find any well with a location in the NE/4 NE/4 of Section 1 going into Section 36-14N-17W.

Author: davem1
Date: 2024-09-24T20:18:55Z
Content: Hi Yankee- I saw your question about Mewbourne in Custer county, and wanted to ask a question of you.   We are newbys with properties in Roger Mllls county, and in the process of signing with Mewbourne.Are you following the drilling costs for purposes of estimating your future payouts, or another reason?After signing the contract with Mewbourne, and the very generic wording related to payout calculations, I’m concerned that the well costs (and driller deductions) will have a bigger affect than we realized.   However, since we’re new and haven’t had active drilling in some time, we’re not totally sure what to expect.Can you share some pearls of wisdom with regards to tracking well development costs??

Author: Yankee
Date: 2024-09-24T23:46:23Z
Content: Hi Todd-
I uploaded the compl rpt for the nene 1 well…hope you can access it here.

Author: M_Barnes
Date: 2024-09-26T12:16:53Z
Content: The drilling costs have nothing to do with the royalty payments.  They are sunk costs and are incurred by the working interest partners.  The post production costs are the costs that are incurred past the wellhead and include items such as compression, dehydration, transportation, marketing, etc.  They can end up being very expensive and you do not want a lease that has those included.  Most draft leases will try just to see if they can get away with it.  It is very wise to get a good oil and gas attorney to review any lease as there are quite a few clauses that need edits and other clauses that need to be added to protect the lessor (you).
